info.title: RecurPost API
info.description:
Public REST API of the RecurPost social media scheduling platform.

Every endpoint is a POST with a JSON body. Call /api/user_login with your account email and API key (from Account Settings, not your password) to receive an access token valid for one hour, then send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other call. The 10 legacy (Zapier-era) endpoints also accept `Authorization: Basic base64(emailid:api_key)` or body credentials (emailid + api_key; pass_key and zapier_key are aliases).

Responses carry X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers; a 429 with Retry-After means the per-minute allowance is used up.

Errors are {status, error, code} with the HTTP status equal to status. Endpoints marked legacy answer errors as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body when called with body credentials; with a Bearer token or a Basic header every endpoint returns real HTTP status codes. Every id is an encrypted string; an id of another user or workspace answers 404. A request to an endpoint path that does not exist is answered with HTTP 404 and the same error body.

Full reference with code samples and a playground: https://developers.recurpost.com/

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description:
Exchange your email and API key for an access token at `/api/user_login`, then send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other call. A token is valid for 1 hour (`expires_in` 3600). There is no refresh token: when it runs out, log in again. Regenerating the API key in RecurPost revokes every token issued before; those tokens then answer `token_expired`.
Key name. The key is sent as `api_key`. `pass_key` and `zapier_key` are still accepted as aliases so existing integrations keep working.
Legacy endpoints. The 10 Zapier-era endpoints (`user_login`, `workspace_list`, `social_account_list`, `library_list`, `connect_social_account_urls`, `history_data`, `post_content`, `add_content_in_library`, `generate_content_with_ai`, `generate_image_with_ai`) also accept the key instead of a token, in one of two ways:
- `emailid` + `api_key` in the request body. Every error then comes back as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body's `status`, as it always did.
- `Authorization: Basic base64(emailid:api_key)`. Errors come back with their real HTTP status.

When a Bearer header is sent it is always the one used. Every other endpoint takes a Bearer token only and answers 401 `token_required` without one.
Errors. Every error has the body `{"status": 404, "error": "...", "code": "not_found"}` and the HTTP status equals `status` (except legacy key-in-body calls, see above). Branch on `code`; `error` is a readable message that may change. A `permission_denied` caused by your role in a workspace also carries `permission`, the catalog key your role is missing.
Paused workspaces. When the owner of a workspace you are a member of (not the owner) has paused the subscription, every call in that workspace answers 403 `owner_paused` with `This workspace is unavailable because the workspace owner's subscription is paused. Ask the owner to resume it.`, as the app locks the workspace for its team. `/api/workspace_list` still lists the workspace, flagged `owner_paused` `1`. The owner's own calls are not affected.
Authentication codes (HTTP 401 unless noted):
- `credentials_required`: `emailid` or `api_key` is missing, on `user_login` or a key-authenticated legacy call.
- `invalid_credentials`: the email and key do not match.
- `token_required`: no Bearer token on an endpoint that takes only tokens.
- `token_invalid`: the token is blank or unknown.
- `token_expired`: the hour is over, or the API key was regenerated since. Log in again.
- `login_locked` (429): too many failed key checks for this email. 5 failures within 5 minutes lock it for 10 minutes, more than 10 within 15 minutes for 30 minutes. The message gives the minutes left, the `Retry-After` header the seconds.
- `too_many_attempts` (429): more than 30 failed key checks in one minute from your IP address, whatever the email. `Retry-After` gives the seconds until the minute ends.

Rate limits. A call in a workspace counts against the workspace owner's allowance, shared by the owner and every team member across all their tokens and keys; a call without a workspace counts against your own. The allowance is sized by the social accounts on the plan (add-ons included):
- Per minute: 60 calls per social account, at most 3,000. Over it a call answers 429 `rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds until the minute ends).
- Per day (UTC): 2,500 calls per social account, at least 5,000. The daily count is recorded and the plan owner gets a warning email at 80%; calls over it are not refused yet.
- Trial plans: 30 calls a minute and 2,000 a day.

Every call that counts against an allowance (errors included) carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` (calls allowed per minute), `X-RateLimit-Remaining` (left in the current minute) and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix time when the minute ends). The minute is a clock minute, not a sliding window. The headers are missing on calls refused before the limit is checked (401 token errors, 404 `workspace_not_found`, 403 `owner_paused`) and for internal RecurPost accounts that have no limit. `user_login` is not counted; it is guarded by `login_locked` and `too_many_attempts`.
Requests. Every endpoint takes `POST` with a JSON or form body. A body sent as JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`) that does not parse answers 400 `invalid_json` (`The request body is not valid JSON.`). An unknown path under `/api/` answers 404 `endpoint_not_found` (`Unknown endpoint.`); any other method answers 405 `method_not_allowed` (`Use POST for every API call.`).
Ids. Every id the API hands out or takes (workspaces, social accounts, libraries, posts, members, roles and so on) is an opaque encrypted string; pass it back unchanged. Only ids that come from a social network, such as a YouTube playlist or a Facebook page id, are plain. A malformed id answers 400 `invalid_id`. An id that is well formed but not yours, or not in the workspace you act in, answers 404 `not_found`, never 403. `workspace_id` is optional on workspace calls and defaults to your own signup workspace; a workspace you are not an active member of answers 404 `workspace_not_found`.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description:
Workspaces group social accounts, libraries and team members. Every call that works inside a workspace takes an optional `workspace_id` (your own signup workspace when omitted); this module lists the workspaces you can use, describes one, creates new ones and manages their members, settings and client report recipients.
Reads are open to every active member. Changes follow the role rules of the Workspaces screen: settings, report recipients and removing accounts or libraries need `workspace-settings`, invites need `invite`, removing members needs `remove-members` (the owner and the workspace's Workspace Manager always may); role changes are for the owner or Workspace Manager; attaching accounts or libraries, cloning, deleting and choosing the Workspace Manager are the owner's. The signup workspace takes no members and cannot be deleted or emptied (403 `signup_workspace`).

tags.name: Team Roles
tags.description: The roles of your account and what each one may do: the Roles page. A role is a named set of permission keys plus the notifications its members receive; members are given a role per workspace with `/api/workspace_invite` and `/api/workspace_member_update`. Roles belong to the account that owns the workspace and only that owner manages them, as on the web page. Without `workspace_id` your own default workspace is used, so you reach your own roles; a team member naming a workspace they were invited to gets 403. Role ids are encrypted strings.

tags.name: Social Accounts
tags.description: The social accounts connected to a workspace, the links to connect or reconnect them, click tracking on their short links, and the option lists some networks need when you post (TikTok and YouTube settings, Facebook backgrounds, mention search, Instagram products and audio).

tags.name: Account & Settings
tags.description: Your own RecurPost account rather than a connected social profile: profile details and timezone, the plan with its limits, invoices and storage, the posting queue switch, the X link-credit wallet, custom fields, and the preference pages (email and push notifications, working hours, white labeling). Profile, timezone, notification preferences, announcements and the report logo are always the caller's own. Plan, invoices, the queue and working hours are the paying account's: the workspace owner only. Any member of a workspace reads its owner's limits, the X wallet balance and the custom fields.

tags.name: Account Groups
tags.description: Account groups are named sets of social accounts a post can target in one go. Groups belong to the workspace owner, but a workspace sees only the groups that hold at least one of its accounts, as in the app; each group lists only the accounts that sit in the workspace the call acts in. Any member reads the groups; creating, changing and deleting them needs the Edit social account settings permission.

tags.name: Posts
tags.description: Publish or schedule one-off posts on your social accounts, follow a post's state per account, preview or shorten links, and look up Instagram places to tag. All post calls share one set of content fields with per-network prefixed overrides; the same fields add and update recurring posts under Libraries.

tags.name: Media
tags.description: Browse the images, GIFs and videos already used in the owner's posts, and reuse their URLs in the post, draft and library calls without a second download.

tags.name: Drafts
tags.description: Posts saved without a publish time. A draft carries the same content and per-network options as a one-off post made with `/api/post_content`; `/api/draft_schedule` turns it into a scheduled post in place, keeping its id.

tags.name: Queue
tags.description: Posts waiting to go out. A queue item is one account at one time, identified by an encrypted `id`; the `post_id` groups the items of one post across its accounts. List and read items, move or rewrite one, remove some, move a whole day, publish right now, or retry a failed post.

tags.name: History
tags.description: What has already gone out: published and failed posts, with the text and media the network received, the permalink on the network and the failure reason. `/api/history_list` covers the whole workspace with filters and paging; `/api/history_data` is the older per-account feed built for polling.

tags.name: Libraries
tags.description:
Libraries hold evergreen posts that RecurPost publishes in rotation on the schedules attached to the library. These endpoints list, create, update and pause libraries, add, read, search and update their posts, move or copy posts between libraries, delete posts, and manage the message variations of a post. /api/add_content_in_library and /api/library_content_update take the content fields of /api/post_content.
Every id in this module (`library_id`, post `id`, variation `id`) is an encrypted string handed out by these endpoints; plain numbers are rejected.

tags.name: Library Tools
tags.description:
The tools the app keeps beside a library: posts that expired out of their library, the drafts of a library, find-and-replace across posts, the next-post pointer of every account, and the public share link with the comments clients leave through it.
Every id is an encrypted string handed out by other endpoints: `library_id`, `library_ids`, `content_id`, `account_id`, `account_ids` and `comment_id`. `position` and the page numbers are plain integers.
Reading needs the Content library permission, adding, editing and expiring posts Manage content (`lib-upload`), deleting Delete content (`lib-delete`), pointers Manage timeslots (`lib-manage`) and share links Workspace settings. Library posts stay visible to every member, also in a workspace that shows members only their own posts. Datetimes are server time (UTC) unless an endpoint says otherwise.

tags.name: Schedules
tags.description: Time slots that publish a library's posts to a social account: which library, which account, how often and at what time. A slot is `weekly` (a weekday) or `monthly` (a day of the month), at a fixed time or at the account's best time.

tags.name: RSS Feeds
tags.description:
RSS feeds that fill a library with new articles. A feed is always handled together with the library it feeds (`id` plus `library_id`); adding the same URL to another library creates a separate feed with its own approval setting.
Every id is an encrypted string: the feed `id`, `library_id`, `new_library_id` and the item ids in `item_ids`. Reading feeds and their items needs the Content library permission; every change needs Manage timeslots (`lib-manage`), as on the Library page's feed panel. Feed URLs must be public http or https addresses. Datetimes are server time (UTC).

tags.name: Import
tags.description: The import plugin: posts an account has already published on its network, pulled into RecurPost so you can add them to a library as evergreen content. List the accounts the plugin can read, page through what each one has published, fetch older or newer posts from the network, then move a batch into a library with optional caption and per-network customisation. Times are in the workspace owner's timezone.

tags.name: Post Labels
tags.description: Labels are account-wide tags you put on scheduled posts and library posts; the label report groups performance by them. Labels belong to the workspace owner's account, so the same label set is visible in every workspace of that owner. Manage the labels here and attach them to posts with `/api/label_assign_set`, `/api/label_assign_add` and `/api/label_assign_remove`. Label ids are encrypted strings like every other id.

tags.name: Content Tools
tags.description:
The tools around composing: hashtag groups per library, bags of tags, watermarks per account or per workspace, testimonial template images, URL shortener accounts and the Instagram product catalog. Everything belongs to the workspace owner. Hashtag groups need the Content library section (`library`), an account's watermark needs Edit social account settings (`manage-accounts`) for reading as for changing, and the workspace watermark and shortener changes need a role permission; the deletes of hashtag groups and bags and every catalog call are for the owner only, and the rest is open to every member (see each endpoint).
Every id is an encrypted string: `library_id`, `account_id` and `account_ids` come from other endpoints, `tag_id`, `bag_id`, `template_id`, `shortener_id` and `domain_id` from the lists in this module. Catalog, business and product ids are Meta's own numeric ids, sent and returned as strings.

tags.name: Approvals
tags.description: Library content approval. When a team member adds a post to a library that requires approval, the post waits for its reviewers before it joins the library's rotation. List what is waiting on you or on others, and approve or reject as a reviewer.

tags.name: Workflow Board
tags.description:
The agency workflow board: ideas and posts (cards) moving through the workspace owner's stages to the schedule. The board belongs to the workspace owner; you act as yourself on it, so the role permissions, stage gates and client hand-over rules of the dashboard apply to every call exactly as they do in RecurPost.
Members see only their own posts. When a card's workspace has this setting on, a member who does not own that workspace sees and reaches only the cards they created or are assigned to. Other cards are left off `/api/workflow_board`, and their ids answer 404 `not_found` on every card call, as if they did not exist.

tags.name: Workflow Settings
tags.description: The account's workflow as built in the Workflow Builder: its switches, the Ideas stage and the stages a post passes through on the board before it is scheduled. The workflow belongs to the account owner and applies to every workspace of the account, so every call here is for the workspace owner only (a member's call answers 403). Workflow, stage and role ids are encrypted strings.

tags.name: Shared Calendars
tags.description:
The client calendar of a workspace: the shareable link a client opens to review the posts queued for them, the people invited to it, and the comments clients and team members leave on a queued post there. One calendar per workspace; the workflow's client review stage and the urgent approval email both send the client to it.
A workspace without a calendar of its own uses the account-wide calendar of the owner's signup workspace (My Workspace) while that one is live (link on, end date not passed), exactly as the app falls back to it. Such a calendar is answered by `/api/shared_calendar_get` with `calendar.inherited` `true` and is read-only here: the manage calls (update, link, delete, clients, invite, remove) act only on the workspace's own calendar, as the app's workspace settings do, and answer 404 `not_found` while the workspace has none.

tags.name: Inbox
tags.description:
The social inbox: comments and mentions on Facebook pages, LinkedIn company pages and Instagram business accounts, direct message conversations on Facebook pages and Instagram business accounts, and reviews of Google Business locations. Reads come from RecurPost's inbox tables (filled by webhooks and syncs); replies, deletes and likes go to the network through the account's own connection, while bookmarks, review marks, assignments and labels live in RecurPost only.
Four kinds of id appear in this module, all encrypted strings: an account id (from `/api/inbox_accounts`), an item id (one inbox entry: a comment thread, a conversation or a review), a comment id (one comment or message inside an item) and a label id. Ids of the network itself (post ids, comment ids on the network, the author's network user id) are returned as the network gives them.
Reading needs the Inbox permission; replying, liking, deleting comments and the AI helpers need Reply to DMs & comments; assigning, marking reviewed and changing the labels of items need Assign messages.

tags.name: DM Automations
tags.description:
Comment-to-DM automations for Instagram business accounts. When someone comments on a post (any comment, or one containing a keyword), RecurPost replies publicly and sends them a direct message with an optional button. Mode `anyone` sends the DM to every commenter; `follow_to_unlock` first asks non-followers to follow and sends the link once they do. Daily counters show how each automation performs.
Automation ids and account ids are encrypted strings; Instagram media ids are returned as Instagram gives them. Reading needs the DM automations permission, creating needs Create an automation, and editing, pausing, resuming or deleting needs Edit / delete automation.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: The analytics RecurPost shows on its Reports page, as data or as a PDF: one account's report, the whole workspace's overview, per-post metrics for one account, the PDF produced now or emailed, plus the Pinterest board, Paid Ads and post label reports, the X Wallet purchase of X analytics, and an AI chat over any report. Every report is read live from the network, so calls can take several seconds.

tags.name: Custom Reports
tags.description: The custom report canvases of a workspace: saved sets of metric and note tiles over chosen accounts, as built on the Custom Reports page, and their PDF. Report ids are encrypted strings scoped to the workspace. `/api/custom_report_metrics` lists every metric a tile can carry, with the networks it has data on, the graph types it draws and the comparisons it takes; `/api/custom_report_templates` lists the gallery templates with their tiles in the save shape. Tiles sent to `/api/custom_reports_save` are checked against that catalog the way the in-app canvas checks them. Reading a report never spends X Wallet money: X tiles use only X analytics already bought with `/api/report_x_fetch`.

tags.name: AI
tags.description: RecurPost's AI assistant through the API: write post text in a multi-turn chat, generate an image from a prompt, read the AI credit counters, pull hashtags for a text, suggest variations of a library post, write from the app's templates and special-day calendar, draft a week of posts, copy an AI result into libraries and manage the brand voice the AI writes with. Credits, chats, generated images and the brand voice belong to the workspace owner: generation spends the AI credits of the owner's plan or add-on, whoever calls. Most calls are open to every member; see each endpoint's permission.

post.summary: Verify your API key and receive an access token valid for one hour.
post.description:
Permission: your own account (no workspace).
Checks your account email and API key and returns an access token. Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other call. Tokens live for one hour; there is no refresh token, call this endpoint again to get a new one.
The API key is not your account password. Generate it under Account Settings in RecurPost. Regenerating the key revokes every token issued with the old one.
Send the email and key in the body, or both at once as `Authorization: Basic base64(emailid:api_key)`. When the Basic header is sent, the body fields are ignored.

Key in the body: errors as HTTP 200: This is a Zapier-era endpoint. When `emailid` and the key are sent in the body, every error comes back as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body's `status` and `code`; check `status`, not the HTTP code. With the Basic header the real HTTP status is used.

Not counted against the call allowance: Logging in does not count towards the per-minute and daily call allowance. Log in once and reuse the token for the hour rather than logging in before every call.

Legacy endpoint: with body credentials errors arrive as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body field `status`. With a Bearer token or a Basic header it returns real HTTP status codes.

emailid.description: Email address of your RecurPost account. Not needed in the body when you send the Basic header.

api_key.description: Your API key from Account Settings. `pass_key` and `zapier_key` are accepted as aliases for existing callers (the first non-empty of `api_key`, `pass_key`, `zapier_key` is used). Not needed in the body when you send `Authorization: Basic base64(emailid:api_key)`.

token.description: 64-character access token. Shown once (RecurPost stores only a hash); store it on your side.

401.description:
credentials_required: emailid and api_key are required. (The email or the key is missing or blank (in the body, or in the Basic header when one is sent).)

invalid_credentials: We could not authenticate the user's RecurPost credentials. (The email and key do not match, or the account has no API key yet. Each failure counts towards login_locked and too_many_attempts.)

429.description:
login_locked: Too many failed attempts. Try again in <minutes> minutes. (The email is locked after failed key checks: 5 within 5 minutes lock it for 10 minutes, more than 10 within 15 minutes for 30 minutes. Retry-After gives the seconds left.)

too_many_attempts: Too many failed logins from this address. Try again in <seconds> seconds. (More than 30 failed key checks in one minute from your IP address, across all emails. Retry-After gives the seconds until the minute ends.)

post.summary: List the workspaces you own or that are shared with you.
post.description:
Permission: your own account (no workspace).
Returns every workspace you are a member of: the ones you own and the ones other accounts shared with you. The `ws_id` values are what you pass as `workspace_id` to the other endpoints; when a call omits `workspace_id` your own signup workspace, the one flagged `is_default`, is used.

Key in the body: errors as HTTP 200: This is a Zapier-era endpoint. Called with `emailid` and `api_key` in the body, an error comes back as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body's `status`. With a Bearer token or the Basic header the real HTTP status is used.

Using workspace_id: Pass `ws_id` as `workspace_id` to any endpoint that lists it. A shared workspace runs under its owner's plan, timezone and limits, and what you may do in it depends on your role there.

Legacy endpoint: with body credentials errors arrive as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body field `status`. With a Bearer token or a Basic header it returns real HTTP status codes.

ws_id.description: Encrypted workspace id. Pass it as `workspace_id` to the other endpoints.

is_default.description: `1` only for your own signup workspace, which is used when a call omits `workspace_id`; `0` otherwise, also for the signup workspace of an account that shared it with you.

ownership.description: `own` when the workspace is yours, `shared` when another account invited you into it.

owner_paused.description: `1` when the workspace belongs to another account whose owner has paused the subscription: it is listed, but every call in it answers 403 `owner_paused` until the owner resumes, as the app greys it out in its workspace switcher. `0` otherwise, always for your own workspaces.

401.description: Authentication failed: token_required, token_invalid, token_expired, credentials_required or invalid_credentials.

429.description: Per-minute rate limit reached; see Retry-After.

post.summary: Read one workspace: libraries, accounts, members, pending invites and workspace manager.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Returns the workspace record with everything attached to it. Every member reads the members by name; their emails and roles go only to callers who may manage the workspace (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`, `invite` or `remove-members`), as in the app, where other members see names and photos only. Your own row always carries your email and role. `libraries` is filled only for callers whose role has the Content library section (`library`) and `accounts` only for those with the Social profiles section (`social`), as in the app's sidebar, or with workspace settings (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`), as on the Social profiles and Libraries panes of the app's workspace settings. Without the section the list is empty. Callers who may manage the workspace also get the owner's `email`, the pending invites and each member's `is_workspace_manager` flag. Callers who may invite (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `invite`) also get the roles of the account (the values `role` accepts in `/api/workspace_invite`); only the owner gets each role's `members` count. Callers with workspace settings (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`) also get `client_email`, `show_own_posts` and the client report recipients. Otherwise `client_email` and `show_own_posts` are `null` and those lists are empty. `workspace_manager` is `null` unless you may manage the workspace or are its Workspace Manager.

Every id is encrypted: User, role and report recipient ids in this module are encrypted strings, like workspace, library and account ids. Pass them back unchanged.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

is_default.description: `true` for the signup workspace of its owner.

id.description: Encrypted user id of the owner.

email.description: Owner's email. Only for callers who may manage the workspace (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`, `invite` or `remove-members`); otherwise `null`.

timezone.description: Owner's timezone; dates in this workspace are shown in it.

workspace_manager.description: The member set as Workspace Manager, as `{id, name, email, role}` (ids encrypted). `null` when none is set, and also when you may not manage the workspace (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`, `invite` or `remove-members`) and are not the Workspace Manager yourself.

client_email.description: Default client email for approvals and reports. Only with workspace settings; `null` otherwise.

show_own_posts.description: `true` when members see only their own one-off posts in this workspace (library posts stay visible). Only with workspace settings (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`); `null` otherwise.

created_at.description: When the workspace was created.

id.description: Encrypted library id (see `/api/library_list`). Filled with the Content library section (`library`) or workspace settings; empty otherwise.

color.description: Hex color of the library.

id.description: Encrypted social account id. Filled with the Social profiles section (`social`) or workspace settings; empty otherwise.
Encrypted user id of an active member. The owner is not listed.

email.description: Member's email. Only for callers who may manage the workspace (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`, `invite` or `remove-members`) and on your own row; otherwise `null`.

role.description: `{id, name}` of the role, the id encrypted, or `null` when there is none. Same visibility as `email`.

is_workspace_manager.description: `true` for the workspace's Workspace Manager. Only for callers who may manage the workspace (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`, `invite` or `remove-members`) and on your own row; otherwise `null`.

id.description: Encrypted user id of an invited person who has not accepted yet. Pass it as `user_id` to `/api/workspace_invite_resend`. Only for callers who may manage the workspace (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`, `invite` or `remove-members`); empty otherwise.

role.description: `{id, name}` of the role they were invited with, the id encrypted, or `null`.

id.description: Encrypted role id. Only for callers who may invite. Either the id or the name is accepted as `role` by `/api/workspace_invite`, `/api/workspace_member_update` and `/api/workspace_create`. Owner roles are not listed; they cannot be given to a member.

members.description: How many workspace memberships across the account use this role. Sent to the workspace owner only.

id.description: Encrypted id of the recipient, the `report_id` of `/api/workspace_report_emails_update` and `/api/workspace_report_emails_delete`. Only with workspace settings.

email.description: Address that receives the scheduled client report.

day.description: Day the report goes out: weekday 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday) for weekly, day of month 1 to 28 for monthly.

active.description: `false` when the report is switched off.

400.description: invalid_id: workspace_id is not a valid id. Get ids from /api/workspace_list. (workspace_id was sent but does not decrypt to an id.)

401.description: Authentication failed: token_required, token_invalid, token_expired, credentials_required or invalid_credentials.

404.description: workspace_not_found: Workspace not found or you do not have access to it. (The workspace does not exist or you are not an active member of it (without workspace_id: you have no default workspace).)

429.description: Per-minute rate limit reached; see Retry-After.

post.summary: Create a workspace, optionally with libraries, accounts and invites.
post.description:
Permission: your own account (no workspace).
Creates a workspace owned by you, in your own account (a `workspace_id` sent here is ignored). You can attach existing libraries and social accounts of your account in the same call and invite people by email, each with an optional role. The libraries, accounts, invite addresses and roles are all checked before anything is written. Invites are sent after the workspace exists and a failed invite does not undo it: the result lists them in `invites_failed`.
Creating workspaces needs a paid plan.

Invites create accounts and send mail: An invited address that has no RecurPost account gets one, with a welcome email carrying a temporary password, exactly as an invite from the app does. Addresses already in RecurPost get an invitation email. Check `invites_failed` rather than assuming every invite went out.

name.description: Workspace name, trimmed, 1 to 100 characters. Must not match one of your other workspaces.

library_ids.description: Encrypted library ids from `/api/library_list` to attach: an array, a JSON array string, or one string with ids separated by commas, at most 50. Every library must be yours (any of your workspaces).

post.summary: Members of a workspace with role and status, and the approvers you can send content to.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Returns the active members of the workspace, by name; emails and roles only for callers who may manage the workspace (owner, Workspace Manager, or a role with `workspace-settings`, `invite` or `remove-members`) and on your own row. Callers who may manage the workspace also get the pending invites and each member's `is_workspace_manager` flag. A caller who is not the owner also gets `approvers`: the owner and the active members of the workspace (people with a pending invite are left out), owner flagged, which are the users library content can be sent to for approval; their emails only for callers who may manage the workspace. For the owner `approvers` is empty.

post.summary: Invite a member to a workspace by email, with an optional role.
post.description:
Permission: Invite members (`invite`) in the workspace; the owner and its Workspace Manager always may.
Adds a person to the workspace by email with an optional role. An address without a RecurPost account gets one plus a welcome email, as in the app; an existing user gets an invitation email and shows up in `pending_invites` until they accept. Someone who already is an accepted member of the owner's team joins at once. A pending invite is mailed again with `/api/workspace_invite_resend`.
Only on workspaces created after signup: the signup workspace cannot take members. The team member limit of the workspace owner's plan applies.

Sends email, may create an account: Every successful call sends mail. An unknown address becomes a RecurPost user with a temporary password before the invite is recorded (also when the invite is then refused, for example by the plan limit), so do not use this endpoint to test addresses.

Changing and removing members: Roles and the Workspace Manager are changed with `/api/workspace_member_update`; a member is removed with `/api/workspace_member_remove`.

id.description: Encrypted user id of the invited person.

name.description: Their name, which may be just the first name for a freshly created account.

role.description: `{id, name}` of the role, the id encrypted, or `null` when there is none.

status.description: `pending` until they accept; `active` straight away when they already are an accepted member of the owner's team.

post.summary: Rename a workspace, set or clear its client email, or switch members to seeing only their own posts.

Permission: Workspace settings (`workspace-settings`) in the workspace; the owner and its Workspace Manager always may.
Changes the settings of one workspace. Send any of `name`, `client_email` and `show_own_posts`; fields left out keep their value. `client_email` is the default address approvals and client reports go to, and a blank string clears it. `show_own_posts` on means team members see only the one-off posts they created in this workspace; library posts stay visible to everyone.

Role first, then Workspace Manager: When both fields are sent the role is changed first. If the Workspace Manager change then fails, the new role stays.

post.summary: List the account's roles with the permission and notification keys, or read one role in full.
post.description:
Permission: workspace owner only. Roles belong to the account of the workspace owner.
Without `role_id` lists every role of the account together with `permission_keys` (every key `/api/role_set_permissions` accepts; `/api/role_permissions` has the same keys with their labels and groups) and `notification_keys` (every key it accepts as `notification_key`). With `role_id` returns that one role with the permissions it holds, its notification settings and the workflow stages it reviews.

Feature masters: `social`, `library`, `inbox`, `reports`, `dm`, `ads` and `client` are master keys that switch a whole feature on for the role; the keys that follow each one in the list are its finer permissions and only count while the master is held.

Reading as a member: A team member's own role in a workspace is on `members[].role` of `/api/workspace_members`; this endpoint is for the workspace owner.

Stock roles are seeded: An account that has no role yet gets the four stock roles (Contributor, Writer, Editor, Publisher) on its first list call, as the Roles page does.

post.summary: List the social accounts of a workspace with their connection state.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Returns every social account in the workspace, paused ones included. The `smpa_id` values are the encrypted account ids you pass as `id` / `account_id` to `/api/post_content`, `/api/history_data` and the other endpoints that target an account.
Every account carries a `reconnect_url` you can hand to the account holder, filled only when your role has the Social profiles section (`social`, as on the app's Social profiles page) and empty otherwise; an account whose token expired reads `Needs Reconnection`. A workspace without accounts answers 200 with an empty `social_accounts` list. Use `/api/social_account_details` for the full state of one account.

Only two states: This list tells connected and expired apart, nothing more. For `active` / `paused` / `needs_reconnection`, the network key, groups and workspaces of one account call `/api/social_account_details`.

Empty workspace: A workspace without social accounts answers 200 with `social_accounts: []` (older versions answered 400 `We can't find any social account`).

Zapier-era endpoint: Besides a Bearer token this endpoint accepts `emailid` + `api_key` in the body (`pass_key` and `zapier_key` are older names of the key), where every error comes back as HTTP 200 with the status in the body, or an `Authorization: Basic` header of `emailid:api_key`, where the HTTP status is real.

Legacy endpoint: with body credentials errors arrive as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body field `status`. With a Bearer token or a Basic header it returns real HTTP status codes.

smpa_id.description: Encrypted account id. Pass it as `account_id` (or `id`) to the other endpoints.

smpa_name.description: Account name followed by the network type in brackets, e.g. `My Page (Facebook Page)`.

status.description: `Connected`, or `Needs Reconnection` when the token expired. A paused account still reads `Connected`.

reconnect_url.description: Link that lets the account holder reconnect the account without logging in to RecurPost. Empty unless your role has the Social profiles section (`social`).

Open a link in a browser (or send it to the account holder) to run the network's login and add the account to the workspace in `workspace_id` (your default workspace when it is not sent); no RecurPost login is needed. Instagram Business comes twice: once through Facebook Login and once through Instagram's own Direct Login.
The list holds 15 links: Facebook Profile, Facebook Page, Facebook Group, X (Twitter) Profile, LinkedIn Profile, LinkedIn Company, Instagram Personal Profile, Pinterest Board, Google Business Profile, Instagram Business Profile (Facebook Login), Instagram Business Profile (Direct Login), TikTok Profile, YouTube Channel, Threads Profile and Bluesky Profile.

Links are personal: Each link is bound to your user, the workspace and the workspace owner. Whoever opens it adds the account to that workspace under the owner's plan, so share links only with people who should connect accounts there.

post.summary: Pause or reactivate one social account.
post.description:
Permission: Edit social account settings (`manage-accounts`) in the workspace.
Pausing stops every scheduled and library post for the account without disconnecting it; reactivating resumes them. Reactivation runs the same plan checks as the app: it is refused when the owner is already at the account limit of the plan, when a free plan holds two accounts of the same kind, or when the same profile is active under another RecurPost account. Asking for the state the account already has answers 200 without a change.
An account that needs reconnecting is refused with 409: reconnecting it in RecurPost is what makes it active again.

Posts are not rescheduled: Pausing does not move queued posts; they stay in the queue and go out once the account is active again, provided their time has not passed. Check `/api/queue_list` after reactivating.

`bluesky_password` is checked with Bluesky before it is stored and is ignored on every other network. `pinterest_link`, `x_premium` and `youtube_category` are refused on accounts of other networks. The answer is the account as stored after the call.

post.summary: Plan limits of the workspace owner and how much of each is used, media storage included.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace. Members see the owner's plan, allowances and storage; the usage counts are for the owner only. No prices or billing.
Returns the plan of the workspace owner with each limit paired with its current usage, add-ons included, so an integration can check before it creates something. Limits follow the owner of the workspace, not the caller: a team member calling with a shared `workspace_id` sees the owner's allowances. The `used` counts of `social_accounts`, `library_content`, `feeds`, `schedules` and `team_members` span the owner's whole account and are sent to the owner only, as in the app; for everyone else they are `null`. `storage` and `posts_per_day` are sent to every member. Allowances are the owner's own plan values plus purchased add-ons (each social account add-on +1, library content add-on +100, feed add-on +1, schedule add-on +10, team member add-on +1).
Media storage is one of them: `limits.storage` gives the bytes used against the allowance as last stored by the app (the account settings page refreshes the figure from storage; this call does not), so `last_checked_at` says how fresh it is.
`posts_per_day` is counted per social account per day. The response lists every account of the workspace (or only `account_ids`) with the posts it already has on `date`, today in the owner's timezone by default, and how many more it may take. Each account's day runs in that account's own timezone (the owner's when the account has none), exactly as the limit check on `/api/post_content` counts it. Each row names the account (`name`, `network`, `status`) only for callers with the Social profiles section (`social`); otherwise a row carries just `account_id`, `used` and `remaining`.

account_ids.description: Encrypted social account ids from `/api/social_account_list`: an array, or one string with ids separated by commas. At most 50. Each must sit in the workspace. Only these accounts are listed under `posts_per_day`. Defaults to every account of the workspace.

post.summary: Balance of the workspace owner's X (Twitter) URL wallet and the Permit Repeated Tweets rule; for the owner also the cost per post, top-up packs and transactions.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace. Only the workspace owner gets `cost_per_post_usd`, `topup_packs` and `transactions`, and only the owner may send `permit_repeated_tweets`.
Posts to X carry a per-post cost that is paid from the workspace owner's wallet. Every member reads the balance, how many posts it still covers, the threshold below which RecurPost warns and the Permit Repeated Tweets rule, as the composer shows them. The owner also gets the cost per post, the top-up packs on offer and the latest transactions, 20 a page. `is_owner` says which view came back.
`permit_repeated_tweets` is the owner's X posting rule from the X settings page of the app: whether evergreen library posts and their variations may go out on X again after they have posted once. It is read here, and the workspace owner sets it here by sending `permit_repeated_tweets` with the call; the wallet comes back with the new state. It is not a notification and /api/email_preferences does not list or accept it.

Top-ups happen in the app: There is no endpoint to buy a pack; the `sku` values match the packs on the X wallet page in RecurPost.

Member view: A team member gets `wallet.balance_usd`, `wallet.posts_remaining`, `wallet.low_balance_threshold_usd`, `permit_repeated_tweets` and `is_owner` (`false`) only: no prices, packs or transactions.

page.description: Transactions page, 20 per page, from 1. Only used for the owner, but checked for every caller.

permit_repeated_tweets.description: Library posts and their variations may go out on X again after they have posted once. Send it to set the rule before the wallet is read: `true`/`false` (also `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`); any other value is refused. Workspace owner only. Omit to read.

posts_remaining.description: Posts to X the balance still covers.

low_balance_threshold_usd.description: Balance under which RecurPost sends a low-balance warning.

price_usd.description: What the pack costs. Owner only.

credit_usd.description: Credit the pack adds to the wallet. Owner only.

type.description: `credit` (a top-up) or `debit` (a post to X). Transactions are returned to the workspace owner only.

date.description: When it happened, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in your timezone.

enabled.description: Required with `email_type`: `true`/`false` (also `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`). Any other value is refused.

post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Returns the whole post behind `post_id`: the shared text and media, every per-network customisation and option the composer saved, and the accounts of the workspace it went to with their state. The fields of `post` carry the names `/api/post_content` takes, so a published or failed post is published again in two calls: read it here, then send `post` to `/api/post_content` with the account ids and a new `schedule_date_time`. This is what the Reschedule button on the History page of the app prefills.
`post_id` is the encrypted id that `/api/post_content` returns as `post_data.id`, `/api/history_list` as `id` and `/api/queue_list` as `post_id`. Queued posts and drafts are read the same way; `/api/queue_post_update` lays a partial change over exactly these fields.

Reschedule in two calls: Take `post` as it is, add `id` (the account ids from `accounts`, or any others) and `schedule_date_time`, and send it to `/api/post_content`. Nothing needs renaming.

Media URLs are the stored copies: `image_url`, `video_url`, covers and the LinkedIn document are the URLs on RecurPost storage. `/api/post_content` takes them as they are and does not download them again, as long as you post in a workspace of the same owner.

post_content re-checks what it is sent: The fields are returned as they were saved; a new post is validated afresh. A reel still needs a video, a Facebook background only applies to a post without media, reel tags need a video, an account that was removed is refused. Drop a field that no longer fits before sending.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When the workspace has show own posts on, a member who is not the owner sees only the one-off posts they created; posts that came from a library stay visible to everyone. Other members' one-off posts answer as if they did not exist (404).

url.description: The link of a link post, or the destination link of an image or video pin (a post with a Pinterest account). Absent otherwise.

video_url.description: The shared video on RecurPost storage.

alt_text.description: Alternative text per shared image, in `image_url` order, taken from the first network tab that carries alt text for the shared images.

&lt;prefix&gt;_message.description: The own text of a network, present only when its tab is customised and the text differs from `message`. Prefixes: `fb`, `tw`, `ln`, `in`, `gmb`, `pi`, `yt`, `tk`, `th`, `bs`. With Facebook mentions, `fb_message` carries `@<page id>` where the stored text reads `@<name>`, the form post_content reads.

&lt;prefix&gt;_image_url / _video_url /.description: The own media of a network, present only when it posts a different set from the shared one, with its alt text in that order (alt text on Facebook, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and Bluesky).

&lt;option&gt;.description: Every option of `/api/post_content` that was set, under its own name and in the form post_content takes it: `fb_post_type` (a list such as `["feed", "story"]` when several types were chosen, as for `in_post_type`), `fb_thumb`, `fb_background_id`, `fb_is_ai_generated`, `fb_ai_images` (objects with `image_url` and `provenance_type`), `fb_mentions` (objects with `page_id` and `name`), `tw_made_with_ai`, `twitter_thread`, `ln_document`, `ln_document_title`, `ln_thumb`, `in_post_type`, `in_reel_share_in_feed`, `in_thumb`, `in_is_ai_generated`, `in_trial_reel`, `in_location_id` with `in_location_name`, `in_location_city` and `in_location_country`, `in_reel_tags`, `in_collaborators`, the `in_audio_*` fields with `in_audio_account_id` encrypted, `in_image_tags`, `in_product_tags` and `in_reel_product_tags` (their `account_id` encrypted), `pi_title`, `pi_ai_modified`, `pi_synthetic_performer`, `gbp_cta` with `gbp_cta_url` (left out when it is only the automatic `Learn more` button on the post's own `url`, which post_content adds again by itself), the `gbp_offer_*` fields and `gbp_redeem_offer_link` on an Offer, the YouTube options (`yt_title`, `yt_category` by name, `yt_privacy_status`, `yt_user_tags`, `yt_thumb`, `yt_video_made_for_kids`, `yt_license`, `yt_embeddable`, `yt_default_language`, `yt_default_audio_language`, `yt_recording_date`, `yt_contains_synthetic_media`) when a privacy status was saved, the TikTok options (`tk_privacy_status` by name, `tk_allow_comments`, `tk_allow_duet`, `tk_allow_stitches`, `tk_promote_own_brand`, `tk_promote_other_brand`, `tk_auto_add_music`, `tk_is_aigc`, `tk_thumb`, `tk_thumb_timestamp`) when a privacy status was saved, and `bs_thumb`. YouTube playlists are not returned.

items.description: One entry per social account of the workspace the post went to, oldest post time first, in the shape of `/api/post_status`.

id.description: Encrypted social account id, as in `/api/social_account_list`. Pass these to `/api/post_content` as `id`.

queue_item_id.description: Encrypted queue item id of this account's row. Pass it to `/api/post_retry` when the row is `failed`, to `/api/post_unpublish` once published, or to the queue endpoints while it is scheduled.

status.description: `scheduled`, `pending` (handed to the publisher, or a state in between), `published`, `failed`, `deleted` or `draft`.

post_date.description: Scheduled or actual publish time, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in the social account's own timezone (UTC when it has none).

post_link.description: Permalink on the network once published; empty before that, for Facebook stories, and when the post was later removed from the network.

fail_reason.description: Only present when `status` is `failed` and a reason was recorded; HTML tags removed.

post.fb_message: Summer sale starts today, pages first!

post.summary: Search Instagram places to tag a post with.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Searches Instagram places matching `search_text` through the workspace's connected Instagram business accounts. Pass the returned `id` and `name` as `in_location_id` and `in_location_name` on `/api/post_content`, the draft and queue calls or the library calls to tag the post with the place.

Live network call: Every call queries Instagram's Graph API through the account's token; results are not cached and count against Meta's own rate limits for that account.

Which account searches: The search runs through the Instagram business accounts the workspace owner has connected; `id` is validated but does not yet narrow which account's token is used. Results are the same places either way.

search_text.description: Place name or address fragment to search for.

id.description: Encrypted social account id of an Instagram business account of this workspace, from `/api/social_account_list`. Checked to be one (400 otherwise); see the note on how the search uses it.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

items.description: Matching places, as Instagram returned them; may be empty.

id.description: Instagram place id, the value for `in_location_id`.

city.description: City, empty when Instagram sent none.

country.description: Country, empty when Instagram sent none.

link.description: Facebook page link of the place, or empty.

400.description:
invalid_id: workspace_id is not a valid id. Get ids from /api/workspace_list. (workspace_id was sent but is not a valid encrypted id.)

invalid_id: id is not a valid id. (id is not a valid encrypted id.)

missing_param: search_text is required. (search_text missing or blank.)

invalid_param: id must be an Instagram business account. (id is not an Instagram business account (for example an account of another network).)

401.description: Authentication failed: token_required, token_invalid, token_expired, credentials_required or invalid_credentials.

workspace_not_found: Workspace not found or you do not have access to it. (The workspace does not exist, or you are not its owner or an active member.)

not_found: Social account not found in this workspace (id). (An id in id does not belong to the workspace owner or sits outside this workspace.)

conflict: Please connect an Instagram business account to this workspace to search locations. (The workspace has no Instagram business account.)

conflict: <the app's message> (The app refused the search, for example because the account needs reconnecting.)

post.summary: The link preview RecurPost would show for a URL: title, description, image and the other images on the page.
post.description:
Permission: your own account (no workspace).
Reads a public web page the way the composer does when a link is pasted and returns its title, description, the preview image and the other images found on the page, so an integration can pick an image or show the card before it calls `/api/post_content`. YouTube and Vimeo links get their video details. The page is fetched by RecurPost's servers during the call, through the same public-URL guard as media: private, loopback and reserved addresses are refused. No `workspace_id`.
A page that cannot be read (an error status such as 404, an empty body, a refused fetch) still answers 200: `preview.found` is `false`, the title, description and images are empty and `message` says so.

Fetched during the call: The page is downloaded while the request runs, so a slow site makes the call slow. Nothing is stored; pass the chosen image to `/api/post_content` as `image_url` yourself.

url.description: Public http or https address of the page. `http://` is prepended when the scheme is missing.

message.description: `Success`, or `The page could not be read.` when `preview.found` is false.

url.description: The page URL as resolved; the one you sent when the page gave none.

title.description: Page title, HTML entities decoded; empty when the page could not be read.

description.description: Page description, HTML entities decoded; empty when the page could not be read.

image_url.description: The preview image the composer would pick; empty when none.

items.description: Other images found on the page, blanks and duplicates removed.

found.description: `true` when the page gave a title, a description or an image; `false` otherwise.

preview.title: Plan a month of posts in one sitting
preview.description: Three ways to fill a content calendar without burning out.

post.summary: Shorten a link with one of your own URL shortener accounts.
post.description:
Permission: your own account (no workspace).
Shortens a public URL with a shortener account attached to your own RecurPost account (Bitly or a self-hosted Shlink, as set up under Settings or listed by `/api/shortener_accounts_list`). `shortener_id` picks the account; your first attached account is used when it is left out. A URL that is already short comes back as it is. No `workspace_id`: shortener accounts belong to the person who calls, not to a workspace.

Your own shorteners, not the workspace's: The shortener accounts are the caller's own, also when you work in someone else's workspace. A teammate's or the workspace owner's shorteners are not used.

url.description: Public http or https address to shorten. `http://` is prepended when the scheme is missing.

shortener_id.description: Encrypted id of one of your shortener accounts, from `/api/shortener_accounts_list`. Defaults to the first one.

url.description: The URL as you sent it.

short_url.description: The short link; the URL itself (with `http://` added when it had no scheme) when the shortener returned none.

shortener_id.description: Encrypted id of the shortener account used.

400.description:
missing_param: url is required. (url missing or blank.)

invalid_url: url must be a public http or https address. (url is not a URL, has another scheme, or its host resolves to a private, loopback or reserved address.)

invalid_id: shortener_id is not a valid id. (shortener_id is not a valid encrypted id.)

401.description: Authentication failed: token_required, token_invalid, token_expired, credentials_required or invalid_credentials.
