post.summary: Queued items of the workspace in a date window, one per account and time.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Returns the queued items (scheduled or pending, not yet published, failed or deleted), soonest first. `from` and `to` are dates in the workspace owner's timezone; they default to today and 30 days ahead. Narrow the list with `account_id` and `library_id`.
The `id` of each item is the encrypted queue item id the other queue endpoints take. `post_id` is shared by the items of one post on several accounts and is what `/api/post_status` and `/api/post_details` read.
For the same items laid out by day for a calendar view, empty days included, use `/api/calendar`.

Two timezones: `from` and `to` are read in the workspace owner's timezone, but each item's `post_date` is shown in its own social account's timezone. Convert before comparing items across accounts.

Failed posts are not here: The list holds items that are still to go out. Published and failed posts come from `/api/history_list`; a failed item can be retried with `/api/post_retry`.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When the workspace has show own posts on, a member who is not the owner sees only the one-off posts they created; posts that came from a library stay visible to everyone. Other members' one-off posts answer as if they did not exist (404).

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

account_id.description: Encrypted social account ids from `/api/social_account_list`: an array, a JSON array string, a comma-separated string or one id. At most 50. Only items on these accounts are returned.

library_id.description: Encrypted library ids from `/api/library_list`, in the same forms. At most 50. Only items coming from these libraries are returned.

from.description: First day of the window, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the owner's timezone. Defaults to today.

to.description: Last day of the window, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the owner's timezone, not before `from`. Defaults to 30 days after today, or to `from` when that lies further out.

total.description: Number of items in the window after the filters.

from.description: First day of the window actually used.

to.description: Last day of the window actually used.

id.description: Encrypted queue item id. Pass it to the other queue endpoints.

post_id.description: Encrypted id of the post this item publishes; shared by the items of one post on other accounts. Read it with `/api/post_status` or `/api/post_details`.

name.description: Account name as shown in RecurPost.

library.description: `{id, name}` of the library the item was taken from (encrypted id), or `null` for a one-off post.

message.description: The text this account publishes (the network's own text when the post was customised for it).

post.summary: One queued item by its id.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Returns one item of the queue in the same shape as `/api/queue_list`. The item must still be queued; a published, failed or removed item answers 404.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When the workspace has show own posts on, a member who is not the owner sees only the one-off posts they created; posts that came from a library stay visible to everyone. Other members' one-off posts answer as if they did not exist (404).

id.description: Encrypted queue item id from `/api/queue_list` or `accounts[].queue_item_id` of `/api/post_status`.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

item.description: The queue item, same fields as one entry of `items[]` in `/api/queue_list`: `id`, `post_id`, `account` (`id`, `name`, `network`), `library` (`id`, `name`, or null for a one-off post), `message`, `title`, `description`, `url`, `image_url`, `video_url`, `post_date`, `status`.

not_found: Queue item not found in this workspace (id). (An id in id does not belong to the workspace owner, sits outside this workspace, or is a one-off post of another member in a workspace that shows members only their own posts.)

429.description: Per-minute rate limit reached; see Retry-After.

post.summary: Move a queued item to a new time, change the post behind it, or both.
post.description:
Permission: moving the item needs Publish or schedule (`publish`); changing the content needs the owner, Edit others' post (`edit-others`) or Publish or schedule (`publish`), as in the app's queue editor; Write and edit their posts alone does not edit a scheduled post.
Send `schedule_date_time` to move the item, any content field of `/api/post_content` to change the post, or both together.
Time only: the item must be in status `scheduled`. When the new time falls on another day, the owner's daily post limit for that day is checked; then the time is written in place. Sending the item's current time changes nothing. The answer is `Post rescheduled`.
With content: a content change is partial. The stored post is read back as the fields of `/api/post_content` (what `/api/post_details` returns), the fields you send are laid over it, and the post is rebuilt from that and saved in place: it keeps its `post_id`, no copy is made, and every account the post is queued on takes the new content, exactly as Edit on the queue page does. Each account keeps its own time; only this item moves when `schedule_date_time` is sent. The answer is `Post updated` with the unchanged `post_id`.
Shared text and a network's own text: `message` is the text for every network; `fb_message`, `in_message` and the other per-network fields are that network's own text and win over `message` for it. `fb_message` alone changes Facebook's text and nothing else, `message` alone changes the shared text and leaves a network's own text in place. A field sent blank clears its stored value. Sending images or a video to a post with a Facebook background drops the background (it only applies to a post without media), unless `fb_background_id` is sent again, which is then refused.

One post, every account: A content change edits the post behind the item, so every account of that post (every queued item sharing its `post_id`) takes the new text, media and options, and the post id does not change. The labels on the post and its YouTube playlists stay as they are.

Timezones: A bare `schedule_date_time` is read in the workspace owner's timezone here, not the account's (unlike `/api/post_content` and `/api/post_retry`). Send an explicit offset to avoid ambiguity. `/api/queue_list` then shows the new time in the account's timezone.

Content fields: The content parameters are those of `/api/post_content` (without `yt_playlists`); see that endpoint for the rules per network. Any field other than `id`, `workspace_id`, `schedule_date_time` and `confirm` counts as content and switches the call to a content change; fields left out keep their stored value. Media you send is downloaded and hosted during the call; stored media is kept as it is.

Media fields replace the whole set: Sending any of `image_url`, `video_url` or `media_order` (or a network's `<prefix>_` versions) replaces that whole media set. The alt texts, Facebook AI image labels and Instagram user and product tags that pointed at the old images are dropped unless you send them again; a new `ln_document` drops the stored document title.

An item in the past needs a new time: The in-place save keeps only accounts whose time is still ahead. An item whose time has already passed answers 409 unless the request carries a new `schedule_date_time` with the content.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When the workspace has show own posts on, a member who is not the owner sees only the one-off posts they created; posts that came from a library stay visible to everyone. Other members' one-off posts answer as if they did not exist (404).

schedule_date_time.description: New time for this item, in the future. Required when no content field is sent. A value with an offset or `Z` (`2026-10-25T09:30:00+05:30`) is one exact moment; a bare `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (also with `T`, seconds optional) is read in the workspace owner's timezone. `shedule_date_time` is also read.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

message.description: New shared text for every network of the post. Left out, the stored text stays. A network's own text (`fb_message` and the rest) wins over it for that network. `\r\n` is normalised to `\n`.
message.example: Check out our summer sale! https://example.com/summer-sale

url.description: Link to share with the post. On a text post the page's title, description and image are fetched and saved as the link preview; when omitted, the first link found in `message` is used instead. When a Pinterest account is targeted, on an image or video post, it becomes the pin's destination link. `http://` is prepended when the scheme is missing. The host must be a public address.

image_url.description: Image URLs in display order: an array, a JSON array string, or one URL string (repeat `image_url[]` in form encoding). At most 20. Each must be a public http or https URL; it is downloaded and stored in the workspace owner's RecurPost media storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. A URL already in the owner's RecurPost storage (for example from `/api/media_list`) is used as it is, without a download. Together with `video_url` it makes a mixed post (images and the video in one carousel on Instagram and Threads; every other network posts what it takes by default).

video_url.description: A public mp4 or mov URL (Google Drive share links are resolved to the download URL). The file is downloaded and stored on RecurPost storage during the call, whatever `host_images_on_recurpost` says; a URL already in the owner's RecurPost storage skips the download. Needs a paid plan of the workspace owner.

media_order.description: The order of a mixed post's media as a list of the original URLs given in `image_url` and `video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when both images and a video are sent. Any URL not in `image_url` / `video_url` answers 400.

host_images_on_recurpost.description: Copy images and custom covers (`fb_thumb` and the others) to RecurPost storage, the default. `false`, `0`, `no` or `off` keeps your own image URLs instead: they are only checked to be public and must stay reachable until every post using them has been published. Videos and the LinkedIn document are always stored.

alt_text.description: Alternative text per shared image, in `image_url` order: an array, a JSON array string, or one string for the first image. At most 1000 characters each; blank entries are skipped. Saved on the Facebook, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and Bluesky tabs that post the shared images; Instagram, Google Business, YouTube and TikTok take no alt text.

first_comment.description: First comment posted right after the post, commonly hashtags. Used on Facebook, LinkedIn and Instagram unless that network's own first comment is given.

fb_message.description: Text for Facebook accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

tw_message.description: Text for Twitter/X accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

ln_message.description: Text for LinkedIn accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

in_message.description: Text for Instagram accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

gmb_message.description: Text for Google Business accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

pi_message.description: Text for Pinterest accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

yt_message.description: Text for YouTube accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. On YouTube this is the video description. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

tk_message.description: Text for TikTok accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

th_message.description: Text for Threads accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

bs_message.description: Text for Bluesky accounts when it should differ from `message`. A value equal to `message` is not a customisation. On a text post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. Sent blank, the network's own text is dropped and it posts `message`.

fb_image_url.description: Images for Facebook accounts instead of the shared media, same forms, rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 15 images on Facebook. Cannot be combined with `fb_video_url`. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. A blank value counts as not sent.

fb_video_url.description: A video for Facebook accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `fb_image_url`. A blank value counts as not sent.

fb_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `fb_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

tw_image_url.description: Images for Twitter/X accounts instead of the shared media, same forms, rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 4 images on Twitter/X. Cannot be combined with `tw_video_url`. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. A blank value counts as not sent.

tw_video_url.description: A video for Twitter/X accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `tw_image_url`. A blank value counts as not sent.

tw_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `tw_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

ln_image_url.description: Images for LinkedIn accounts instead of the shared media, same forms, rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 20 images on LinkedIn. Cannot be combined with `ln_video_url`. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. A blank value counts as not sent.

ln_video_url.description: A video for LinkedIn accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `ln_image_url`. A blank value counts as not sent.

ln_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `ln_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

in_image_url.description: Images for Instagram accounts instead of the shared media, same forms, rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 10 media in all, images and video together on Instagram. May be combined with `in_video_url` into a carousel; `in_media_order` sets the order. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. A blank value counts as not sent.

in_video_url.description: A video for Instagram accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. May be combined with `in_image_url` into a carousel. A blank value counts as not sent.

in_media_order.description: The order of Instagram's own media as a list of the URLs given in `in_image_url` and `in_video_url`. Media left out follow, video first. Only read when both are sent. Any other URL answers 400.

gmb_image_url.description: Images for Google Business accounts instead of the shared media, same forms, rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 1 image on Google Business. Cannot be combined with `gmb_video_url`. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. A blank value counts as not sent.

gmb_video_url.description: A video for Google Business accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `gmb_image_url`. A blank value counts as not sent.

pi_image_url.description: Images for Pinterest accounts instead of the shared media, same forms, rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 1 image on Pinterest. Cannot be combined with `pi_video_url`. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. A blank value counts as not sent.

pi_video_url.description: A video for Pinterest accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `pi_image_url`. A blank value counts as not sent.

pi_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `pi_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

yt_video_url.description: A video for YouTube accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. YouTube takes a video only; `yt_image_url` answers 400. A blank value counts as not sent.

tk_image_url.description: Images for TikTok accounts instead of the shared media, same forms, rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 10 images on TikTok. Cannot be combined with `tk_video_url`. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. A blank value counts as not sent.

tk_video_url.description: A video for TikTok accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `tk_image_url`. A blank value counts as not sent.

May be combined with `th_video_url` into a carousel; `th_media_order` sets the order. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. A blank value counts as not sent.

th_video_url.description: A video for Threads accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. May be combined with `th_image_url` into a carousel. A blank value counts as not sent.

th_media_order.description: The order of Threads's own media as a list of the URLs given in `th_image_url` and `th_video_url`. Media left out follow, video first. Only read when both are sent. Any other URL answers 400.

th_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `th_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

bs_image_url.description: Images for Bluesky accounts instead of the shared media, same forms, rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 4 images on Bluesky. Cannot be combined with `bs_video_url`. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. A blank value counts as not sent.

bs_video_url.description: A video for Bluesky accounts instead of the shared media, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `bs_image_url`. A blank value counts as not sent.

bs_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `bs_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

fb_post_type.description: Facebook post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`.

fb_thumb.description: Custom cover image for Facebook's video. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when Facebook posts no video.

fb_first_comment.description: Facebook first comment; overrides `first_comment` on Facebook.

fb_mentions.description: Facebook pages to mention, up to 10: page ids from `/api/mention_search`, as an array (or JSON array string, or comma-separated string) of ids or of objects with `page_id` and `name`. Write `@<page id>` in the text where each mention goes; with a `name` the stored text reads `@<name>`, the way the composer writes a picked mention. Saved as page mentions on the Facebook tab. An id that is not all digits answers 400.

fb_background_id.description: Facebook text background, from `/api/facebook_backgrounds` (letters, digits, underscore or dash, up to 64 characters). Only on a post whose Facebook tab has no images and no video; otherwise 400.

fb_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Facebook post as made with AI. Only `1` (or `true`) switches it on. On a reel Facebook shows its AI label; on an image post every image on the Facebook tab is labelled. Use `fb_ai_images` to label only some images or to give the provenance type.

fb_ai_images.description: Images to label as AI-generated photos on Facebook, named by the original URLs given in `image_url` (or `fb_image_url` when Facebook has its own images): an array of URL strings, or of objects with `image_url` and `provenance_type`. `provenance_type` defaults to `EXPLICIT` and takes any type Facebook's photo API knows, for example `EXPLICIT`, `EXPLICIT_AI_EDIT`, `C2PA`, `IPTC`, `INVISIBLE_WATERMARK` or `NONE` (case-insensitive). A URL that is not one of the post's Facebook images, or an unknown type, answers 400.

tw_made_with_ai.description: Label the post as made with AI on Twitter/X. Only `1` (or `true`) switches it on.

twitter_thread.description: Follow-up tweets posted as a thread under the main tweet on Twitter/X accounts: an array (or JSON array string) of objects, each with `message` and optionally `image_url` (up to 4) or `video_url` (one, not both). At most 25 items; each needs a message, an image or a video. Media is hosted like the main post's and a thread video needs the paid plan too. Each item counts as a post in the owner's daily limit when an X account is targeted. Other networks ignore it.

ln_document.description: Public URL of a document for a LinkedIn document (carousel) post: PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX, detected from the file itself, not its name; any other type answers 415. The file is downloaded and stored on RecurPost storage and the LinkedIn tab becomes a document post. Google Drive share links are resolved.

ln_document_title.description: Title shown on the LinkedIn document. Defaults to the file name without its extension.

ln_thumb.description: Custom cover image for LinkedIn's video, hosted like `fb_thumb`. Ignored when LinkedIn posts no video.

ln_first_comment.description: LinkedIn first comment; overrides `first_comment` on LinkedIn.

in_post_type.description: Instagram post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`. A reel needs a video.

in_reel_share_in_feed.description: Whether a reel also appears in the profile feed. Only `no` switches it off; read on reels only.

in_thumb.description: Custom cover image for an Instagram reel, hosted like `fb_thumb`. Only applied when `in_post_type` is `reel` and Instagram posts a video.

in_first_comment.description: Instagram first comment; overrides `first_comment` on Instagram.

in_location_id.description: Instagram place id to tag the post with (letters, digits or underscore, up to 64 characters). Take `id` and `name` from `/api/instagram_locations`; `in_location_name` is required with it.

in_location_name.description: Name of the place in `in_location_id`, required with it.

in_location_city.description: City of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_location_country.description: Country of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_image_tags.description: People to tag on images: an array (or JSON array string) of objects with `username` (leading `@` optional), `x` and `y` (fractions of the image width and height, 0 to 1) and `image` (1-based position in Instagram's images, default 1). A malformed entry or one pointing past the last image answers 400.

in_reel_tags.description: Usernames to tag on a reel, as an array, a JSON array string or a comma-separated string. Needs a video on Instagram's tab; answers 400 without one.

in_collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators, as an array, a JSON array string or a comma-separated string. At most 3; more answer 400.

in_audio_id.description: Music for an Instagram reel: a track id from `/api/instagram_audio_search`. Needs `in_post_type` `reel`, a video and `in_audio_account_id`; sent on any other post it answers 400.

in_audio_account_id.description: Encrypted id of the Instagram account the audio search ran for, from `/api/social_account_list`. Required with `in_audio_id`; must be an Instagram account of this workspace (404 otherwise).

in_audio_type.description: Kind of track, as the search returned it.

in_audio_title.description: Track title from the search, stored for display.

in_audio_artist.description: Artist from the search, stored for display.

in_audio_duration_ms.description: Track length in milliseconds from the search, a whole number; 0 when omitted.

in_audio_volume.description: Volume of the added track, 0 to 100.

in_video_volume.description: Volume of the video's own sound under the track, 0 to 100; 0 mutes it.

in_trial_reel.description: Publish the reel as an Instagram trial reel (shown to non-followers first): `manual` leaves sharing to everyone up to you, `performance` lets Instagram share it when it does well. Reels only; on another post type, or with another value, it answers 400.

in_product_tags.description: Shopping tags on images: an array (or JSON array string) of objects with `account_id` (encrypted Instagram account of this workspace), `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`), `image` (1-based position in Instagram's images, default 1), `x` and `y` (0 to 1, default 0.5) and optional `product_name` and `product_image` for display.

in_reel_product_tags.description: Shopping tags on a reel: an array (or JSON array string) of objects with `account_id` (encrypted Instagram account of this workspace), `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`) and optional `product_name` and `image_url` for display. Needs `in_post_type` `reel`; on another post type it answers 400.

in_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Instagram post as AI-generated. Only `1` (or `true`) switches it on.

pi_title.description: Pin title. The destination link of the pin is `url` or the first link in the text.
pi_title.example: Summer Sale - Best Deals of the Season

pi_ai_modified.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: the Pin's content was generated or modified with AI. Only `1` (or `true`) switches it on.

pi_synthetic_performer.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: a person shown or heard in the Pin is AI-generated. Only `1` (or `true`) switches it on.

gbp_cta.description: Call-to-action button on the Google Business post. Case-insensitive. An unknown value or `None` saves no button. On a link post with no button given, `Learn more` pointing at the link is set automatically.

gbp_cta_url.description: Link the button opens. With `gbp_cta=Offer` and no `gbp_redeem_offer_link`, this value doubles as the redeem link.

gbp_offer_title.description: Offer title; the offer fields are used when `gbp_cta` is `Offer`.

gbp_offer_start_date.description: Offer start, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. Stored as sent without a check; a value that is not a date makes the offer fail on Google.

gbp_offer_end_date.description: Offer end, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, after the start. Stored as sent without a check.

gbp_offer_coupon_code.description: Coupon code shown on the offer.

gbp_offer_terms.description: Terms and conditions of the offer.

yt_title.description: Video title. YouTube needs a video; `message` or `yt_message` is the description.

yt_category.description: Category name, matched exactly against the list. An unknown or missing name falls back to the default category of the workspace owner's YouTube settings.

yt_privacy_status.description: Video privacy, lower-cased and stored as given, so use one of the listed values. The YouTube options (category, tags, thumbnail, made for kids, licence, embedding, languages, recording date, AI label) are saved together with a privacy status: left out, it defaults to `public` when one of `yt_license`, `yt_embeddable`, `yt_default_language`, `yt_default_audio_language`, `yt_recording_date`, `yt_contains_synthetic_media=1` or `yt_playlists` is sent; with only the older options (`yt_category`, `yt_user_tags`, `yt_thumb`, `yt_video_made_for_kids`) and no privacy status, no options are stored and YouTube's defaults apply, as on the Zapier-era endpoint.

yt_thumb.description: Custom thumbnail for the YouTube video, hosted like `fb_thumb`. Ignored when YouTube posts no video.

yt_video_made_for_kids.description: Whether the video is made for kids. Only `yes` switches it on.

yt_license.description: Video licence. Any other value answers 400.

yt_embeddable.description: Whether other sites may embed the video. `0`, `no` or `false` switches it off.

yt_default_language.description: Language of the title and description, a BCP-47 code such as `en` or `hi`. Stored as sent.

yt_default_audio_language.description: Language spoken in the video, a BCP-47 code. Stored as sent.

yt_recording_date.description: Date the video was recorded, `YYYY-MM-DD`; another form answers 400.

yt_contains_synthetic_media.description: Tell viewers the video contains realistic content altered or generated with AI. Only `1` (or `true`) switches it on.

tk_privacy_status.description: Who can watch the TikTok video. Case-insensitive, spaces or underscores (`Public to Everyone` or `PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE`); any other value is saved as `Public to Everyone`. The TikTok options are saved together with a privacy status: left out, it defaults to `Public to Everyone` when `tk_auto_add_music`, `tk_thumb`, `tk_thumb_timestamp` or `tk_is_aigc=1` is sent; with only the older switches and no privacy status, no options are stored, as on the Zapier-era endpoint. `/api/tiktok_options` lists what the account allows.

tk_allow_comments.description: Allow comments on the TikTok video. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_duet.description: Allow duets. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_stitches.description: Allow stitches. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_promote_own_brand.description: `1` marks the video as promoting your own brand (TikTok's content disclosure).

tk_promote_other_brand.description: `1` marks the video as branded content for a third party.

tk_auto_add_music.description: `1` lets TikTok add music to a photo post.

tk_thumb.description: Custom cover image for TikTok's video, hosted like `fb_thumb`. Ignored when TikTok posts no video.

tk_thumb_timestamp.description: Frame of the video to use as cover, in milliseconds from the start; a whole number, otherwise 400.

tk_is_aigc.description: Add TikTok's AI-generated content label to the video. Only `1` (or `true`) switches it on.

bs_thumb.description: Custom cover image for Bluesky's video, hosted like `fb_thumb`. Ignored when Bluesky posts no video.

message.description: `Post rescheduled` after a time-only change, `Post updated` after a content change.

post_id.description: After a content change: the id of the post, unchanged. Absent after a time-only change.

Removes the given items from the queue. Every id must still be queued, or nothing is removed. Other accounts of the same post keep their items. Each item is removed on its own; the answer counts the removed ones and lists the ids the app refused. No `confirm` is needed.

post.summary: Move queued items to another day, keeping each item's time of day.
post.description:
Permission: Publish or schedule (`publish`) in the workspace.
Moves items to `to_date` the way dragging a day on the calendar does: every item keeps its time of day in its account's timezone, only the date changes. Pick the items either by `id` (one or several) or by `from_date`, which takes every queued item of that day, optionally narrowed by `account_ids` and `library_id`.
Items of one post that sit on one day are moved together in one step; a step the app refuses (daily post limit, past time, slot already taken) is reported in `failed` while the others still move. When nothing could be moved the first refusal is returned as the error.

Partial success is a 200: Check `failed` on every 200; a group the app refused stays on its old day while the rest moved.

Times are kept: Only the date changes. An item at 09:30 in its account's timezone is at 09:30 on `to_date`. Moving to today can hit the past-time refusal for items whose time of day has already passed.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When the workspace has show own posts on, a member who is not the owner sees only the one-off posts they created; posts that came from a library stay visible to everyone. Other members' one-off posts answer as if they did not exist (404).

account_ids.description: With `from_date`: encrypted social account ids (an array, a JSON array string, a comma-separated string or one id; at most 50) to limit the move to those accounts.

library_id.description: With `from_date`: one encrypted library id to limit the move to items from that library.

post.summary: Publish queued items of one post right away.
post.description:
Permission: Publish or schedule (`publish`) in the workspace.
Publishes the given items immediately. All ids must belong to one post (same `post_id`) and still be queued. The networks are called inside the request, so the call lasts as long as they take; the answer names each account as `published` or `failed` with the network's error. When every account failed the answer is a 409 that still carries the per-account list.

Long, synchronous request: Posting happens inside this call, one network after the other. Use a generous client timeout (a minute or more for videos) and do not retry blindly: a timed-out request may still have published.

Items that stay failed: A failed account keeps its item in status `failed`; retry it with `/api/post_retry`.

post.summary: Retry a failed queue item now or at a new time.
post.description:
Permission: Publish or schedule (`publish`) in the workspace.
Takes one item in status `failed`: its queue item id is `accounts[].queue_item_id` of `/api/post_status`, `queue_item_id` of `/api/history_list`, or `accounts[].id` of a `/api/queue_post_now` answer. Without `schedule_date_time` the item is published right away through the same path as `/api/queue_post_now`, with the app's retry flag, and the answer has the same per-account shape. With `schedule_date_time` the stored content is saved again through the app's retry save and the item goes back into the queue at that time, after the owner's daily post limit is checked.

Account timezone: Unlike `/api/queue_post_update`, a bare `schedule_date_time` here is read in the social account's timezone. Send an offset to be explicit.

Retry now is synchronous: Without a time the network is called inside the request; see the timeout note on `/api/queue_post_now`.

Retry later re-checks the content: A retry at a time rebuilds the post from its stored content, so the content checks of `/api/post_content` apply again; the daily post limit refusal comes back as 403 `plan_limit` with the app's text.

id.description: Encrypted queue item id of the failed post.

schedule_date_time.description: Time to retry at, in the future. A value with an offset or `Z` is one exact moment; a bare `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (also with `T`, seconds optional) is read in the social account's timezone (the owner's when the account has none). Omit to retry now. `shedule_date_time` is also read.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

message.description: `Post scheduled for retry.` when a time was given; otherwise the publish message, normally `Post shared successfully`.

post_id.description: Encrypted id of the post the item now belongs to (time given). The app may move the retried item to a post of its own, so this can differ from the post id before.

status.description: The item's status after the save, normally `scheduled` (time given).

post_date.description: The new time in the account's timezone (time given).

error.description: The reason recorded on the item, only on a failed account; `The network did not publish the post.` when none was recorded. (retried now)

post.summary: The queue laid out by day, every day of the range present, empty days included.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Returns the queued items between `start_date` and `end_date` grouped by day in the workspace owner's timezone, as a calendar view needs them: one entry per day of the range, in order, with its count and items, days without posts included with an empty list. Without dates the current week is returned, Monday to Sunday. The range may span at most 42 days (six calendar weeks). `account_ids` and `library_ids` narrow the items.
Each item is in the shape of `/api/queue_list`. Only queued items appear (scheduled or pending); published and failed posts are in `/api/history_list`.
For a flat, paginated list of the same items without the 42-day cap, use `/api/queue_list`.

Two clocks: Days are cut in the owner's timezone (`timezone` in the answer), while each item's `post_date` is shown in its account's timezone, as in `/api/queue_list`. An item can therefore sit under one date while its `post_date` reads another when the two zones differ.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When the workspace has show own posts on, a member who is not the owner sees only the one-off posts they created; posts that came from a library stay visible to everyone. Other members' one-off posts answer as if they did not exist (404).

start_date.description: First day, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the owner's timezone. Send both dates or neither; omitted together they default to this week's Monday and Sunday.

end_date.description: Last day, `YYYY-MM-DD`, on or after start_date and at most 41 days later.

account_ids.description: Encrypted social account ids to limit the items to: an array, a JSON array string, a comma-separated string or one id. At most 50.

library_ids.description: Encrypted library ids to limit the items to posts from those libraries, in the same forms. At most 50.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

start_date.description: First day of the range returned.

end_date.description: Last day of the range returned.

timezone.description: The owner's IANA timezone the days are cut in, for example `Asia/Kolkata`.

total.description: Items across the whole range.

count.description: Items on that day, 0 for an empty day.

items.description: The day's queue items, soonest first, each as `/api/queue_list` shows them: `id`, `post_id`, `account` (`id`, `name`, `network`), `library` (`id`, `name`, or null for a one-off post), `message`, `title`, `description`, `url`, `image_url`, `video_url`, `post_date`, `status`.

post.summary: Published and failed posts across every account of the workspace, newest first.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Returns the published and failed posts of the workspace in a date window, newest first, with the account each one went to and its status. The window defaults to the last 7 days and may span at most 90. Dates are read in the workspace owner's timezone and every `post_date` is shown in that timezone too.
Each entry shows the text and media of the network's own copy of the post (the per-network tab when the post was customised, the original otherwise), the ready-to-open `post_link` on the network, and `fail_reason` when the post failed.

Owner's timezone everywhere: Both the window and `post_date` use the workspace owner's timezone here, unlike `/api/history_data`, which uses the account's.

Filters run after the fetch: `library_id` and `failed_only` are applied to the whole window before paging, so `total_posts` already reflects them.

Only this workspace's accounts: Only posts on social accounts of this workspace are listed. A post the owner published on an account of another of their workspaces never appears here, even when it falls in the window.

Entry id: `id` is the encrypted post id, shared by the copies of one post on several accounts; tell them apart by `account.id` or `queue_item_id`. Use `post_link` to open the post; `post_url` is an older field that is empty or a profile link on some networks. Read the whole post, ready to send again, with `/api/post_details`.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When the workspace has show own posts on, a member who is not the owner sees only the one-off posts they created; posts that came from a library stay visible to everyone. Other members' one-off posts answer as if they did not exist (404).

post.summary: Posting history of one social account, built for polling.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Returns the published and failed posts of one social account. The call is stateless: without dates it returns the posts of the last 60 minutes, on every call alike, so a poller dedupes on `id` (with `queue_item_id` when one post went to several accounts). With `start_date` and `end_date` it returns up to 100 posts of that window, newest first, plus `total_posts` with the full count.
Dates and `post_date` are in the social account's timezone (UTC when the account has none). Each entry shows the text and media of the network's own copy of the post, the permalink on the network, the post type on Facebook and Instagram, and `fail_reason` on failed posts.
This is one of the Zapier-era endpoints: besides a Bearer token it takes `emailid` + `api_key` in the body (errors then come back as HTTP 200 with the status in the body) or as a Basic header. Key-in-body callers get `id` as the plain post id, as existing Zaps expect; Bearer and Basic callers get it encrypted.

Polling window: Without dates every call covers the 60 minutes before it; there is no "since your last call" marker any more. Poll at least once an hour and skip entries whose `id` (and `queue_item_id`) you have already seen. Posts older than an hour are only reachable with explicit dates.

100 posts per call: With dates the answer holds at most 100 posts, newest first, while `total_posts` counts them all. Split a larger window into smaller ranges, or use `/api/history_list`, which pages.

Account timezone: Dates are read and shown in the social account's timezone, not the owner's. Read the account's zone from `/api/social_account_list`.

Key-in-body calls: Called with `emailid` and `api_key` in the body, every error comes back as HTTP 200 with `status`, `error` and `code` in the body, and `id` is the plain post id. Bearer and Basic callers get real HTTP statuses and an encrypted `id`, the value `/api/post_status` and `/api/post_details` take.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When the workspace has show own posts on, a member who is not the owner sees only the one-off posts they created; posts that came from a library stay visible to everyone. Other members' one-off posts answer as if they did not exist (404).

Legacy endpoint: with body credentials errors arrive as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body field `status`. With a Bearer token or a Basic header it returns real HTTP status codes.

end_date.description: End of the window, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in the account's timezone. Must be sent together with `start_date`.

Permission: the workspace owner or its Workspace Manager.
Deletes one published item (`queue_item_id`, the `queue_item_id` of `/api/history_list` and `/api/post_status`) from the network it went out on. Only networks with a delete call are supported: Facebook pages and groups, X, LinkedIn profiles and companies, Pinterest, Google Business, YouTube and Bluesky. Facebook profiles, Instagram, TikTok and Threads answer 409; remove those posts on the network itself.
The item stays in the history with the deletion recorded: `/api/post_status` and `/api/history_list` then show it as `deleted` with an empty `post_link`. The call needs `confirm=true`; the item and network checks run first. The network's own error text is never relayed.

Not reversible: The post is gone from the network together with its likes, comments and shares. RecurPost keeps the history row and marks it deleted; the post's statistics stop updating.

post.summary: Copy a published post into one or more libraries as evergreen content.
post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace.
Copies post `post_id` (the `id` of a `/api/history_list` row, shared by every account the post went out on) into each library in `library_ids`, text and media included. Each copy is a new library post with its own id and counts toward the workspace owner's library post limit, which is checked for all copies before anything is copied.

No id cap on this call: Unlike most list parameters, `library_ids` has no 50-id limit here; every library named gets a copy and each copy counts against the plan.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When the workspace has show own posts on, a member who is not the owner sees only the one-off posts they created; posts that came from a library stay visible to everyone. Other members' one-off posts answer as if they did not exist (404).

post.summary: Create a content library in the workspace, seasonal or not.
post.description:
Permission: Manage timeslots (`lib-manage`) in the workspace.
Creates a library with a name, an optional calendar colour, the one-time-use flag and, when you send `seasonal_from` and `seasonal_to`, a seasonal window, so a seasonal library takes one call. The new library is active, sits in the workspace and has no schedule yet; attach one with `/api/schedule_create`. The answer is the full library as `/api/library_details` returns it.
As in the app, a new library needs room under the workspace owner's library post limit.

Season days are MM/DD on the API: `seasonal_from` and `seasonal_to` are sent and returned as zero-padded `MM/DD` (`02/01` is accepted, `2/1` is refused). The app stores the season as day/month; the API converts both ways. Days are checked against the current year, so `02/29` is only accepted in a leap year.

seasonal_to.description: Last day of the season as `MM/DD`. Required when seasonal_from is sent.

post.summary: Page through the active posts of one library.

Returns the active posts of a library, 20 per page by default, in the library's rotation order: the post due to publish next comes first. Draft posts are not included; see Drafts. An empty library answers 200 with an empty `content` list.
Each item is the post's original version. The per-network versions of a post come from `/api/library_content`.

post.summary: Add a recurring post to a content library.
post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace.
Adds one post to the library in `id`. Library content is published again and again by the schedules attached to the library, so there is no post time here; `content_livedate` and `content_expiredate` bound when the post may go out and `is_top_of_queue` makes it the next one.
The content fields are the ones of `/api/post_content`: `message`, `url`, `image_url` and `video_url`, the per-network prefixed overrides and options, and `twitter_thread`. The post is saved as one tab per network from these fields, including the Google Business button. `yt_playlists` is refused and reel music is not saved (see the notes).
The post counts against the workspace owner's library post limit, whoever calls. The answer carries the new post's encrypted `id`, the id `/api/library_content` and `/api/library_content_update` take.

Plan rules follow the workspace owner: The library post limit and the paid-plan check for video apply to the workspace owner's plan, not the caller's.

Dates are plain days: `content_livedate` and `content_expiredate` are stored as dates; any time part is discarded.

Images and a video together: A Bearer or Basic caller that sends `image_url` and `video_url` gets one mixed post: Instagram and Threads post them as one carousel in `media_order`, every other network posts what it posts by default. A caller with the key in the body (Zapier-era form) gets the video only and `image_url` is ignored, as those calls always did.

Reel music is not saved on library posts: `in_audio_id` and the other `in_audio_*` fields are checked as on `/api/post_content` (a malformed set answers 400) but library posts do not store reel music, so it is dropped. Add the music when the post is scheduled with `/api/post_content`.

No YouTube playlist on library posts: `yt_playlists` is only taken by `/api/post_content`; sending it here answers 400. Library posts use the channel's default.

Option checks: The option rules of `/api/post_content` (at most 20 images, 1000 characters of alt text, 3 collaborators, a location name with a location id, image tag positions, thread items) are checked here too and answer 400 before any media is fetched.

Per-network media: A network can post media of its own: `<prefix>_image_url` and `<prefix>_video_url` (`fb_`, `tw_`, `ln_`, `in_`, `gmb_`, `pi_`, `yt_`, `tk_`, `th_`, `bs_`) replace `image_url` / `video_url` on that network only and mark its tab as customised; a blank value counts as not sent. Each network keeps its own cap (Facebook 15, Twitter/X 4, LinkedIn 20, Instagram 10 in all, Google Business 1, Pinterest 1, TikTok 10, Threads 20 in all, Bluesky 4); only Instagram and Threads combine images with a video, ordered by `in_media_order` / `th_media_order`; YouTube takes `yt_video_url` only. A URL named by several networks is downloaded once. Covers (`fb_thumb`, `in_thumb`, `ln_thumb`, `yt_thumb`, `tk_thumb`, `bs_thumb`) apply to whichever video that network ends up with; `in_image_tags` and `in_product_tags` positions count in `in_image_url` when Instagram has its own images.

AI disclosure labels: Each network has the same switch as the composer's network tab: `fb_is_ai_generated` and `fb_ai_images` (Facebook), `tw_made_with_ai` (Twitter/X), `in_is_ai_generated` (Instagram), `pi_ai_modified` and `pi_synthetic_performer` (Pinterest), `yt_contains_synthetic_media` (YouTube) and `tk_is_aigc` (TikTok). Only `1` switches a label on, and a label marks that network's tab as customised. LinkedIn, Google Business, Threads and Bluesky have no label.

Bulk upload from a CSV: There is no CSV endpoint. The app's CSV import is this call applied once per row: map the sheet's columns to `message`, `url`, `image_url` or `video_url`, `content_livedate` and `content_expiredate`, and send one request per row into the same library `id`. Keep the calls sequential and inside your plan's per-minute allowance (see the rate-limit headers); a 429 says when to continue. Media must be public URLs.

Zapier-era endpoint: Besides a Bearer token, this endpoint takes `emailid` and `api_key` in the body (errors then come back as HTTP 200 with the status in the body) or as an `Authorization: Basic` header (real HTTP statuses).

Legacy endpoint: with body credentials errors arrive as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body field `status`. With a Bearer token or a Basic header it returns real HTTP status codes.

id.description: Encrypted library id from `/api/library_list`. Exactly one.

message.description: Post text. `\r\n` is normalised to `\n`. The first link in it is used for the link preview when `url` is omitted.
message.example: Check out our latest product! https://example.com/product

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

is_top_of_queue.description: `1` posts this content next on every account the library's schedules cover. Any other value means 0.

content_livedate.description: First day the post may go out, `YYYY-MM-DD`; kept as a draft until then. A datetime such as `2026-11-01T00:00:00+05:30` keeps its date part (the first ten characters); any other value answers 400. Blank means active at once.

content_expiredate.description: Last day the post may go out, `YYYY-MM-DD`; a datetime keeps its date part. Must be on or after `content_livedate` when both are sent; any other value answers 400. Blank means it never expires.

url.description: Link to share with the post. On a text post the page's title, description and image are fetched and saved as the link preview; when omitted, the first link found in `message` is used instead. On an image or video post the link is not saved (library posts carry no Pinterest destination link). `http://` is prepended when the scheme is missing. The host must be a public address.

image_url.description: Image URLs, in display order. Send a JSON array (or repeat `image_url[]` in form encoding); a single string is accepted as a one-item list. At most 20 images. Each URL must be a publicly reachable http or https URL and answer an image content type. URLs already on RecurPost storage (for example from `/api/media_list`) are used as they are; every other URL is copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. With `video_url` as well, a Bearer or Basic caller gets one mixed post (images and the video, ordered by `media_order`; a network that cannot mix posts what it posts by default); a caller with the key in the body gets the video only and `image_url` is ignored, as before.

video_url.description: A public mp4 or mov URL (Google Drive share links are accepted and resolved to the download URL). The file is downloaded and stored on RecurPost storage, so the call takes as long as the download; a URL already on RecurPost storage skips the download. Needs a paid plan of the workspace owner.

media_order.description: The order of a mixed post's media as a list of the original URLs given in `image_url` and `video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when images and a video are sent together by a Bearer or Basic caller (see `image_url`). Any URL not in `image_url` / `video_url` answers 400.

host_images_on_recurpost.description: Copy images and custom thumbnails to RecurPost storage (the default). Send `false`, `0` or the form string `"false"` to keep your own URLs instead; they must then stay reachable until every post using them has been published.

alt_text.description: Alternative text per image, in `image_url` order; a single string applies to the first image. At most 1000 characters each. Saved on the Facebook, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and Bluesky tabs; Instagram does not take alt text here.

fb_image_url.description: Images for Facebook accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 15 images on Facebook. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `fb_video_url`.

fb_video_url.description: A video for Facebook accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `fb_image_url`.

fb_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `fb_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

tw_image_url.description: Images for Twitter/X accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 4 images on Twitter/X. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `tw_video_url`.

tw_video_url.description: A video for Twitter/X accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `tw_image_url`.

tw_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `tw_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

ln_image_url.description: Images for LinkedIn accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 20 images on LinkedIn. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `ln_video_url`.

ln_video_url.description: A video for LinkedIn accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `ln_image_url`.

ln_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `ln_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

in_image_url.description: Images for Instagram accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 10 media in all, images and video together on Instagram. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. May be combined with `in_video_url` into a carousel; `in_media_order` sets the order.

in_video_url.description: A video for Instagram accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. May be combined with `in_image_url` into a carousel.

in_media_order.description: The order of Instagram's own media as a list of the URLs given in `in_image_url` and `in_video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when both are sent. Any other URL answers 400.

gmb_image_url.description: Images for Google Business accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 1 image on Google Business. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `gmb_video_url`.

gmb_video_url.description: A video for Google Business accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `gmb_image_url`.

pi_image_url.description: Images for Pinterest accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 1 image on Pinterest. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `pi_video_url`.

pi_video_url.description: A video for Pinterest accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `pi_image_url`.

pi_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `pi_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

yt_video_url.description: A video for YouTube accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. YouTube takes a video only, so there is no `yt_image_url`.

tk_image_url.description: Images for TikTok accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 10 images on TikTok. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `tk_video_url`.

tk_video_url.description: A video for TikTok accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `tk_image_url`.

th_image_url.description: Images for Threads accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 20 media in all, images and video together on Threads. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. May be combined with `th_video_url` into a carousel; `th_media_order` sets the order.

th_video_url.description: A video for Threads accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. May be combined with `th_image_url` into a carousel.

th_media_order.description: The order of Threads's own media as a list of the URLs given in `th_image_url` and `th_video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when both are sent. Any other URL answers 400.

th_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `th_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

bs_image_url.description: Images for Bluesky accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 4 images on Bluesky. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `bs_video_url`.

bs_video_url.description: A video for Bluesky accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `bs_image_url`.

bs_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `bs_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

fb_message.description: Text for Facebook accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_message.description: Text for Twitter/X accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_made_with_ai.description: Label the post as made with AI on Twitter/X. X shows the label on the post.

twitter_thread.description: Follow-up tweets saved with the library post and posted as a thread under the main tweet on Twitter/X accounts each time it publishes. A JSON array of objects, each with `message` and optionally `image_url` (up to 4) or `video_url` (one, not both). At most 25 items; each item needs a message, an image or a video. Media is hosted like the main post's. Other networks ignore it.

ln_message.description: Text for LinkedIn accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

in_message.description: Text for Instagram accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

gmb_message.description: Text for Google Business accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

pi_message.description: Text for Pinterest accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

yt_message.description: Text for YouTube accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. On YouTube this is the video description.

tk_message.description: Text for TikTok accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

th_message.description: Text for Threads accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

bs_message.description: Text for Bluesky accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

first_comment.description: First comment posted right after the post, commonly hashtags. Applied on Facebook Pages, LinkedIn and Instagram feed posts unless a network-specific first comment is given.

fb_first_comment.description: Facebook first comment; overrides `first_comment` on Facebook.

ln_first_comment.description: LinkedIn first comment; overrides `first_comment` on LinkedIn.

in_first_comment.description: Instagram first comment (feed posts only); overrides `first_comment` on Instagram.

fb_post_type.description: Facebook post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`.

fb_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on Facebook. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

fb_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Facebook post as made with AI. On a reel (`fb_post_type=reel`) Facebook shows its AI label on the reel; on an image post every image on the Facebook tab is labelled as an AI-generated photo, declared by you. Use `fb_ai_images` to label only some images or to give the provenance type.

fb_ai_images.description: Images to label as AI-generated photos on Facebook, named by the original URLs given in `image_url` (or `fb_image_url` when Facebook has its own images). A JSON array of URL strings, or of objects with `image_url` and `provenance_type`: `EXPLICIT` (declared by you, the default), `EXPLICIT_AI_EDIT` (edited with AI), `C2PA` (content credentials in the file), `IPTC` (IPTC AI metadata in the file) or `INVISIBLE_WATERMARK`. Labels the Facebook tab on its own, without `fb_is_ai_generated`. A URL that is not one of the post's Facebook images, or any other provenance type, answers 400.

ln_document.description: Public URL of a document to post as a LinkedIn document (carousel) post: PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX, detected from the file bytes, not the file name. The file is downloaded and stored on RecurPost storage and the LinkedIn tab becomes a document post. A file of another type is left as given and ignored by the publisher. Google Drive share links are resolved.

ln_document_title.description: Title shown on the LinkedIn document. Defaults to the file name without its extension.

ln_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on LinkedIn. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

in_post_type.description: Instagram post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`. A reel needs a `video_url`.

in_reel_share_in_feed.description: Whether a reel also appears in the profile feed. Only read when `in_post_type` is `reel`.

in_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for an Instagram reel. Only applied when `in_post_type` is `reel` and the post has a `video_url`; copied to RecurPost storage because Meta fetches it at publish time.

in_location_id.description: Instagram place id to tag the post with. Take `id` and `name` from `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_location_city.description: City of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_location_country.description: Country of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_image_tags.description: People to tag on feed images. A JSON array of objects with `username`, `x` and `y` (fractions of the image width and height between 0 and 1) and `image` (1-based position in `image_url`, default 1). The leading `@` is optional.

in_reel_tags.description: Usernames to tag on a reel, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. Only saved when the post has a `video_url`.

in_collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. At most 3.

in_trial_reel.description: Publish the reel as a trial reel, shown to non-followers first. `manual`: you decide in Instagram when to share it with followers; `performance`: Instagram shares it when it does well. Reels only.

in_product_tags.description: Instagram product tags on images: objects with `account_id` (encrypted, the account whose catalog holds the product), `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`), `image` (1-based position in `image_url`), `x` and `y` (0 to 1, default 0.5), and optionally `product_name` and `product_image`.

in_reel_product_tags.description: Products tagged on a reel: objects with `account_id` (encrypted) and `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`), optionally `product_name` and `image_url`. Reels only.

in_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Instagram post as AI-generated. Instagram shows its AI label on the post.

pi_title.description: Pin title. The destination link of the pin is `url` or the first link in the text.
pi_title.example: Summer Sale - Best Deals of the Season

pi_ai_modified.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: the Pin's content was generated or modified with AI.

pi_synthetic_performer.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: a person shown or heard in the Pin is AI-generated.

gbp_cta.description: Call-to-action button on the Google Business post. Case-insensitive. An unknown value or `None` saves no button. On a link post with no CTA given, `Learn more` pointing at the link is set automatically.

gbp_cta_url.description: Link the button opens. Not used for `Call now`. With `gbp_cta=Offer` and no `gbp_redeem_offer_link`, this value doubles as the redeem link.

gbp_offer_title.description: Offer title; offer fields are used when `gbp_cta` is `Offer`.

gbp_offer_coupon_code.description: Coupon code shown on the offer.

gbp_offer_terms.description: Terms and conditions of the offer.

yt_title.description: Video title. YouTube needs a `video_url`; `message` or `yt_message` is the description.

yt_category.description: Category name, matched exactly against the list. An unknown or missing name falls back to the default category of the workspace owner's YouTube settings (Entertainment when none is set).

yt_privacy_status.description: Video privacy. Lower-cased and stored as given; use one of the listed values. When it is left out but one of `yt_license`, `yt_embeddable`, `yt_default_language`, `yt_default_audio_language`, `yt_recording_date` or `yt_contains_synthetic_media` is sent, `public` is saved.

yt_thumb.description: Custom thumbnail URL for the YouTube video. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off.

yt_video_made_for_kids.description: Whether the video is made for kids. Only `yes` switches it on.

yt_contains_synthetic_media.description: Tell viewers the video contains realistic content that was altered or generated with AI. YouTube shows a label on the video.

yt_license.description: Video license: `youtube` (standard YouTube license) or `creativeCommon`. Any other value answers 400.

yt_embeddable.description: Whether the video may be embedded on other sites. `0`, `no` or `false` switches it off; anything else keeps it on.

yt_default_language.description: Language of the video's title and description, as a language code such as `en`. Saved as given.

yt_default_audio_language.description: Language spoken in the video, as a language code such as `en-US`. Saved as given.

yt_recording_date.description: Date the video was recorded, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Any other format answers 400.

tk_privacy_status.description: Who can watch the TikTok video. Case-insensitive, spaces or underscores. Any other value is saved as `Public to Everyone`; omitted leaves it unset, unless `tk_auto_add_music`, `tk_thumb`, `tk_thumb_timestamp` or `tk_is_aigc` is sent, which saves the default. `/api/tiktok_options` lists what the account allows.

tk_allow_comments.description: Allow comments on the TikTok video. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_duet.description: Allow duets. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_stitches.description: Allow stitches. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_promote_own_brand.description: Set to `1` to mark the video as promoting your own brand (TikTok's content disclosure).

tk_promote_other_brand.description: Set to `1` to mark the video as branded content for a third party.

tk_is_aigc.description: Add TikTok's AI-generated content label to the video.

tk_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the TikTok video. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when TikTok has no video.

tk_thumb_timestamp.description: Frame of the video TikTok uses as the cover, in milliseconds from the start. A value that is not a whole number answers 400.

tk_auto_add_music.description: Set to `1` to let TikTok add music to the post.

bs_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on Bluesky. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when Bluesky has no video.

fb_mentions.description: Facebook pages to mention, at most 10: page ids from `/api/mention_search`, as a list of ids or of `{page_id, name}` objects. Write each page in the text as `@<page id>`; the publisher turns it into the page's mention on Facebook pages.

fb_background_id.description: Facebook text background for a post without `image_url` or `video_url`: an id from `/api/facebook_backgrounds` (letters, digits, underscore or dash, up to 64 characters). Applied on Facebook pages only.

example.message: Check out our latest product! https://example.com/product

id.description: Encrypted id of the new library post. Added on top of the legacy body, which is otherwise unchanged.

400.description:
invalid_id: workspace_id is not a valid id. Get ids from /api/workspace_list. (workspace_id is sent and is not a valid encrypted workspace id.)

missing_param: id is required. (id is missing or blank.)

invalid_id: id is not a valid id. (id is not a valid encrypted id.)

missing_param: message is required. (message is missing or blank.)

invalid_param: content_livedate must be a date like 2026-10-20. (content_livedate is not YYYY-MM-DD (or a datetime starting with one).)

invalid_param: content_expiredate must be a date like 2026-10-20. (content_expiredate is not YYYY-MM-DD (or a datetime starting with one).)

invalid_param: content_expiredate must be on or after content_livedate. (Both dates are sent and the expiry is before the live date.)

invalid_param: yt_playlists is only taken by /api/post_content; library posts use the channel's default. (yt_playlists is sent.)

invalid_param: image_url takes at most 20 images. (More than 20 image URLs.)

invalid_param: media_order may only hold the URLs given in image_url and video_url. (A mixed post (images and a video) names a URL in media_order that is not in image_url or video_url.)

invalid_param: yt_image_url is not accepted; YouTube takes yt_video_url only. (Images sent for YouTube.)

invalid_param: <prefix>_image_url and <prefix>_video_url cannot be combined; only Instagram and Threads take images and a video together. (Images and a video for one network other than Instagram or Threads.)

invalid_param: <prefix>_image_url takes at most <n> images for <network>. (More images than that network allows.)

invalid_param: <prefix>_image_url and <prefix>_video_url take at most <n> media items together for <network>. (Instagram (10) or Threads (20): images and video together over the cap.)

invalid_param: <prefix>_media_order may only hold the URLs given in <prefix>_image_url and <prefix>_video_url. (A per-network order names a URL outside that network's own media.)

invalid_param: <name> entries may have at most 1000 characters. (An `alt_text` or `<prefix>_alt_text` entry is longer than 1000 characters.)

invalid_param: fb_mentions takes at most 10 pages. (More than 10 pages in fb_mentions.)

invalid_param: fb_mentions holds page ids from mention_search, as a list or as {page_id, name} items. (An fb_mentions entry is not a numeric page id.)
