invalid_param: in_location_name is required with in_location_id; both come from instagram_locations. (in_location_id without in_location_name, or an in_location_id that is not a plain place id.)

invalid_param: in_collaborators takes at most 3 usernames. (More than 3 collaborators.)

invalid_param: in_reel_product_tags entries need account_id and product_id, on in_post_type reel only. (An in_reel_product_tags entry is malformed or in_post_type is not reel.)

invalid_id: <param> is not a valid id. (The `account_id` of an in_product_tags or in_reel_product_tags entry is not a valid encrypted id.)

invalid_param: twitter_thread takes at most 25 further tweets. (More than 25 thread items.)

invalid_param: twitter_thread item <n> needs a message, image_url or video_url. (A thread item is empty or not an object.)

invalid_param: twitter_thread item <n> may carry up to 4 images or one video, not both. (A thread item has more than 4 images, or images and a video.)

invalid_param: yt_license must be youtube or creativeCommon. (yt_license has another value.)

invalid_param: yt_recording_date must be a date like 2026-10-20. (yt_recording_date is not YYYY-MM-DD.)

invalid_param: tk_thumb_timestamp must be a whole number of milliseconds. (tk_thumb_timestamp is not a whole number.)

invalid_url: Invalid url parameter supplied. (url (or the first link in the text) is not a URL.)

invalid_url: <param> is not allowed: <url>. Send a publicly reachable http or https URL. (A link, image, video, cover or ln_document URL is not http/https or its host resolves to a private, loopback or reserved address (also checked on every redirect).)

invalid_url: <param> is not allowed: <url>. The host could not be resolved. (The host of a media or link URL does not resolve.)

invalid_url: <param> redirects too many times: <url>. (A media URL redirects more than 5 times.)

request_failed: Content validation failed! (The app's content validator refused one or more network tabs (text too long, media the network does not accept, a reel without video, ...). Unlike `/api/library_content_update`, no `error_details` come with it.)

request_failed: <message from the app> (The app refused the call for another reason; its own text is relayed.)

401.description: Authentication failed: token_required, token_invalid, token_expired, credentials_required or invalid_credentials.

403.description:
permission_denied: Your role in this workspace does not allow this action (Manage content). (Your role in the workspace lacks the Manage content permission. The body also carries `permission`: `lib-upload`.)

plan_limit: The limit of the user's RecurPost plan has exhausted. (The workspace owner's libraries already hold as many posts as the plan allows.)

plan_restriction: You are not allowed to upload video file in your current plan. Please upgrade your RecurPost plan. (A video (shared, per network or in twitter_thread) is sent while the workspace owner is on a free plan.)

permission_denied: You have maximum allowed number of updates in your library. Please upgrade your plan or delete few updates to add new ones. (The app's own post limit check refused the post (wording of the upgrade text varies by plan).)

404.description:
workspace_not_found: Workspace not found or you do not have access to it. (workspace_id (or your default workspace) is not a workspace you own or are an active member of.)

not_found: Library not found in this workspace (id). (id is not a library of this workspace (another account's id, or one that sits in another workspace).)

not_found: Instagram account not found in this workspace (<param>). (The account_id of a product tag or in_audio_account_id is not one of the workspace owner's Instagram accounts.)

not_found: The provided library is not found in the user's RecurPost account. (The app could not find the library.)

415.description:
unsupported_media: <param> is not an image (detected content type: <type>). Send an image URL. (An image or cover URL answers a non-image content type.)

unsupported_media: <param> did not return a recognizable image. (An image or cover URL could not be read as an image.)

unsupported_media: <param> is not a video (detected content type: <type>). Send an mp4 or mov URL. (A video URL answers a non-video content type.)

unsupported_media: Invalid video format (detected: <type>). Supported formats: mp4, mov. (A video URL is neither mp4 nor mov by extension or content type. For a per-network video the text reads "Invalid video format in <param> ...".)

unsupported_media: ln_document must be a PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX file (detected: <type>). (The downloaded ln_document is another file type.)

422.description:
media_failed: The media URL could not be downloaded: <url> (A video or ln_document URL could not be read.)

media_failed: Failed to upload <param>. The URL was reachable but the file could not be processed. (An image, video, cover or document could not be stored.)

429.description: Per-minute rate limit reached; see Retry-After.

500.description: internal_error: Something went wrong. Please try again later. (The app gave no usable answer.)

post.summary: Change some fields of a library post; fields left out keep their values.
post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace.
Changes the library post `id` inside library `library_id` the way the library editor of the app does: the fields you send are laid over the stored post and every field you leave out keeps its value. To clear a field, send it blank (`"first_comment": ""`) or switch it off (`"tw_made_with_ai": 0`). It takes the content fields of `/api/add_content_in_library`; `/api/library_content` returns the stored post in those names under `post`.
A media field (`image_url`, `video_url`, `media_order`, or the same with a network prefix) replaces that whole media set, and drops the alt texts, AI image labels and Instagram tags of the old images unless they are sent again. Media you do not send stays at its stored URLs.
The post keeps its id, its place in the library, its labels and its variations. `content_livedate` and `content_expiredate` keep their values unless sent; a live date in the future makes the post a draft, clearing it makes a draft active. The post may be an active post or a draft of the library.

Full replacement: This is not a patch. Media, per-network messages, first comments, covers and options not present in the request are dropped; images already on RecurPost storage must be sent again by their URL (they are kept as they are, nothing is re-downloaded). Labels stay as they are.

Images and a video together: A Bearer or Basic caller that sends `image_url` and `video_url` gets one mixed post: Instagram and Threads post them as one carousel in `media_order`, every other network posts what it posts by default. A caller with the key in the body (Zapier-era form) gets the video only and `image_url` is ignored, as those calls always did.

Reel music is not saved on library posts: `in_audio_id` and the other `in_audio_*` fields are checked as on `/api/post_content` (a malformed set answers 400) but library posts do not store reel music, so it is dropped. Add the music when the post is scheduled with `/api/post_content`.

No YouTube playlist on library posts: `yt_playlists` is only taken by `/api/post_content`; sending it here answers 400. Library posts use the channel's default.

Option checks: The option rules of `/api/post_content` (at most 20 images, 1000 characters of alt text, 3 collaborators, a location name with a location id, image tag positions, thread items) are checked here too and answer 400 before any media is fetched.

Per-network media: A network can post media of its own: `<prefix>_image_url` and `<prefix>_video_url` (`fb_`, `tw_`, `ln_`, `in_`, `gmb_`, `pi_`, `yt_`, `tk_`, `th_`, `bs_`) replace `image_url` / `video_url` on that network only and mark its tab as customised; a blank value counts as not sent. Each network keeps its own cap (Facebook 15, Twitter/X 4, LinkedIn 20, Instagram 10 in all, Google Business 1, Pinterest 1, TikTok 10, Threads 20 in all, Bluesky 4); only Instagram and Threads combine images with a video, ordered by `in_media_order` / `th_media_order`; YouTube takes `yt_video_url` only. A URL named by several networks is downloaded once. Covers (`fb_thumb`, `in_thumb`, `ln_thumb`, `yt_thumb`, `tk_thumb`, `bs_thumb`) apply to whichever video that network ends up with; `in_image_tags` and `in_product_tags` positions count in `in_image_url` when Instagram has its own images.

AI disclosure labels: Each network has the same switch as the composer's network tab: `fb_is_ai_generated` and `fb_ai_images` (Facebook), `tw_made_with_ai` (Twitter/X), `in_is_ai_generated` (Instagram), `pi_ai_modified` and `pi_synthetic_performer` (Pinterest), `yt_contains_synthetic_media` (YouTube) and `tk_is_aigc` (TikTok). Only `1` switches a label on, and a label marks that network's tab as customised. LinkedIn, Google Business, Threads and Bluesky have no label.

library_id.description: Encrypted id of the library the post belongs to (active or as a draft), from `/api/library_list`.

message.description: New post text; left out, the stored text stays. `\r\n` is normalised to `\n`.
message.example: Updated: our latest product is now 20% off! https://example.com/product

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

is_top_of_queue.description: Read but without effect on an update: the app's edit ignores it. Use `/api/library_content_order_move` to move the post.

content_livedate.description: First day the post may go out, `YYYY-MM-DD`; kept as a draft until then. A datetime such as `2026-11-01T00:00:00+05:30` keeps its date part (the first ten characters); any other value answers 400. Left out, the stored date stays; blank clears it.

content_expiredate.description: Last day the post may go out, `YYYY-MM-DD`; a datetime keeps its date part. Must be on or after `content_livedate` when both are sent; any other value answers 400. Left out, the stored date stays; blank clears it.

url.description: Link to share with the post. On a text post the page's title, description and image are fetched and saved as the link preview; when omitted, the first link found in `message` is used instead. On an image or video post the link is not saved (library posts carry no Pinterest destination link). `http://` is prepended when the scheme is missing. The host must be a public address.

image_url.description: Image URLs, in display order. Send a JSON array (or repeat `image_url[]` in form encoding); a single string is accepted as a one-item list. At most 20 images. Each URL must be a publicly reachable http or https URL and answer an image content type. URLs already on RecurPost storage (for example from `/api/media_list`) are used as they are; every other URL is copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. With `video_url` as well, a Bearer or Basic caller gets one mixed post (images and the video, ordered by `media_order`; a network that cannot mix posts what it posts by default); a caller with the key in the body gets the video only and `image_url` is ignored, as before.

video_url.description: A public mp4 or mov URL (Google Drive share links are accepted and resolved to the download URL). The file is downloaded and stored on RecurPost storage, so the call takes as long as the download; a URL already on RecurPost storage skips the download. Needs a paid plan of the workspace owner.

media_order.description: The order of a mixed post's media as a list of the original URLs given in `image_url` and `video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when images and a video are sent together by a Bearer or Basic caller (see `image_url`). Any URL not in `image_url` / `video_url` answers 400.

host_images_on_recurpost.description: Copy images and custom thumbnails to RecurPost storage (the default). Send `false`, `0` or the form string `"false"` to keep your own URLs instead; they must then stay reachable until every post using them has been published.

alt_text.description: Alternative text per image, in `image_url` order; a single string applies to the first image. At most 1000 characters each. Saved on the Facebook, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and Bluesky tabs; Instagram does not take alt text here.

fb_image_url.description: Images for Facebook accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 15 images on Facebook. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `fb_video_url`.

fb_video_url.description: A video for Facebook accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `fb_image_url`.

fb_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `fb_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

tw_image_url.description: Images for Twitter/X accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 4 images on Twitter/X. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `tw_video_url`.

tw_video_url.description: A video for Twitter/X accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `tw_image_url`.

tw_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `tw_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

ln_image_url.description: Images for LinkedIn accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 20 images on LinkedIn. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `ln_video_url`.

ln_video_url.description: A video for LinkedIn accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `ln_image_url`.

ln_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `ln_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

in_image_url.description: Images for Instagram accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 10 media in all, images and video together on Instagram. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. May be combined with `in_video_url` into a carousel; `in_media_order` sets the order.

in_video_url.description: A video for Instagram accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. May be combined with `in_image_url` into a carousel.

in_media_order.description: The order of Instagram's own media as a list of the URLs given in `in_image_url` and `in_video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when both are sent. Any other URL answers 400.

gmb_image_url.description: Images for Google Business accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 1 image on Google Business. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `gmb_video_url`.

gmb_video_url.description: A video for Google Business accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `gmb_image_url`.

pi_image_url.description: Images for Pinterest accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 1 image on Pinterest. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `pi_video_url`.

pi_video_url.description: A video for Pinterest accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `pi_image_url`.

pi_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `pi_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

yt_video_url.description: A video for YouTube accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. YouTube takes a video only, so there is no `yt_image_url`.

tk_image_url.description: Images for TikTok accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 10 images on TikTok. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `tk_video_url`.

tk_video_url.description: A video for TikTok accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `tk_image_url`.

th_image_url.description: Images for Threads accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 20 media in all, images and video together on Threads. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. May be combined with `th_video_url` into a carousel; `th_media_order` sets the order.

th_video_url.description: A video for Threads accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. May be combined with `th_image_url` into a carousel.

th_media_order.description: The order of Threads's own media as a list of the URLs given in `th_image_url` and `th_video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when both are sent. Any other URL answers 400.

th_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `th_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

bs_image_url.description: Images for Bluesky accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 4 images on Bluesky. A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `bs_video_url`.

bs_video_url.description: A video for Bluesky accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). A blank value counts as not sent. Otherwise it replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `bs_image_url`.

bs_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `bs_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

fb_message.description: Text for Facebook accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_message.description: Text for Twitter/X accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_made_with_ai.description: Label the post as made with AI on Twitter/X. X shows the label on the post.

twitter_thread.description: Follow-up tweets saved with the library post and posted as a thread under the main tweet on Twitter/X accounts each time it publishes. A JSON array of objects, each with `message` and optionally `image_url` (up to 4) or `video_url` (one, not both). At most 25 items; each item needs a message, an image or a video. Media is hosted like the main post's. Other networks ignore it.

ln_message.description: Text for LinkedIn accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

in_message.description: Text for Instagram accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

gmb_message.description: Text for Google Business accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

pi_message.description: Text for Pinterest accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

yt_message.description: Text for YouTube accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. On YouTube this is the video description.

tk_message.description: Text for TikTok accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

th_message.description: Text for Threads accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

bs_message.description: Text for Bluesky accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

first_comment.description: First comment posted right after the post, commonly hashtags. Applied on Facebook Pages, LinkedIn and Instagram feed posts unless a network-specific first comment is given.

fb_first_comment.description: Facebook first comment; overrides `first_comment` on Facebook.

fb_mentions.description: Facebook pages to mention, at most 10: page ids from `/api/mention_search`, as a list of ids or of `{page_id, name}` objects. Write each page in the text as `@<page id>`; the publisher turns it into the page's mention on Facebook pages.

fb_background_id.description: Facebook text background for a post without `image_url` or `video_url`: an id from `/api/facebook_backgrounds` (letters, digits, underscore or dash, up to 64 characters). Applied on Facebook pages only.

ln_first_comment.description: LinkedIn first comment; overrides `first_comment` on LinkedIn.

in_first_comment.description: Instagram first comment (feed posts only); overrides `first_comment` on Instagram.

fb_post_type.description: Facebook post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`.

fb_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on Facebook. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

fb_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Facebook post as made with AI. On a reel (`fb_post_type=reel`) Facebook shows its AI label on the reel; on an image post every image on the Facebook tab is labelled as an AI-generated photo, declared by you. Use `fb_ai_images` to label only some images or to give the provenance type.

fb_ai_images.description: Images to label as AI-generated photos on Facebook, named by the original URLs given in `image_url` (or `fb_image_url` when Facebook has its own images). A JSON array of URL strings, or of objects with `image_url` and `provenance_type`: `EXPLICIT` (declared by you, the default), `EXPLICIT_AI_EDIT` (edited with AI), `C2PA` (content credentials in the file), `IPTC` (IPTC AI metadata in the file) or `INVISIBLE_WATERMARK`. Labels the Facebook tab on its own, without `fb_is_ai_generated`. A URL that is not one of the post's Facebook images, or any other provenance type, answers 400.

ln_document.description: Public URL of a document to post as a LinkedIn document (carousel) post: PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX, detected from the file bytes, not the file name. The file is downloaded and stored on RecurPost storage and the LinkedIn tab becomes a document post. A file of another type is left as given and ignored by the publisher. Google Drive share links are resolved.

ln_document_title.description: Title shown on the LinkedIn document. Defaults to the file name without its extension.

ln_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on LinkedIn. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

in_post_type.description: Instagram post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`. A reel needs a `video_url`.

in_reel_share_in_feed.description: Whether a reel also appears in the profile feed. Only read when `in_post_type` is `reel`.

in_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for an Instagram reel. Only applied when `in_post_type` is `reel` and the post has a `video_url`; copied to RecurPost storage because Meta fetches it at publish time.

in_location_id.description: Instagram place id to tag the post with. Take `id` and `name` from `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_location_city.description: City of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_location_country.description: Country of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_image_tags.description: People to tag on feed images. A JSON array of objects with `username`, `x` and `y` (fractions of the image width and height between 0 and 1) and `image` (1-based position in `image_url`, default 1). The leading `@` is optional.

in_reel_tags.description: Usernames to tag on a reel, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. Only saved when the post has a `video_url`.

in_collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. At most 3.

in_trial_reel.description: Publish the reel as a trial reel, shown to non-followers first. `manual`: you decide in Instagram when to share it with followers; `performance`: Instagram shares it when it does well. Reels only.

in_product_tags.description: Instagram product tags on images: objects with `account_id` (encrypted, the account whose catalog holds the product), `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`), `image` (1-based position in `image_url`), `x` and `y` (0 to 1, default 0.5), and optionally `product_name` and `product_image`.

in_reel_product_tags.description: Products tagged on a reel: objects with `account_id` (encrypted) and `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`), optionally `product_name` and `image_url`. Reels only.

in_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Instagram post as AI-generated. Instagram shows its AI label on the post.

pi_title.description: Pin title. The destination link of the pin is `url` or the first link in the text.
pi_title.example: Summer Sale - Best Deals of the Season

pi_ai_modified.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: the Pin's content was generated or modified with AI.

pi_synthetic_performer.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: a person shown or heard in the Pin is AI-generated.

gbp_cta.description: Call-to-action button on the Google Business post. Case-insensitive. An unknown value or `None` saves no button. On a link post with no CTA given, `Learn more` pointing at the link is set automatically.

gbp_cta_url.description: Link the button opens. Not used for `Call now`. With `gbp_cta=Offer` and no `gbp_redeem_offer_link`, this value doubles as the redeem link.

gbp_offer_title.description: Offer title; offer fields are used when `gbp_cta` is `Offer`.

gbp_offer_coupon_code.description: Coupon code shown on the offer.

gbp_offer_terms.description: Terms and conditions of the offer.

yt_title.description: Video title. YouTube needs a `video_url`; `message` or `yt_message` is the description.

yt_category.description: Category name, matched exactly against the list. An unknown or missing name falls back to the default category of the workspace owner's YouTube settings (Entertainment when none is set).

yt_privacy_status.description: Video privacy. Lower-cased and stored as given; use one of the listed values. When it is left out but one of `yt_license`, `yt_embeddable`, `yt_default_language`, `yt_default_audio_language`, `yt_recording_date` or `yt_contains_synthetic_media` is sent, `public` is saved.

yt_thumb.description: Custom thumbnail URL for the YouTube video. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off.

yt_video_made_for_kids.description: Whether the video is made for kids. Only `yes` switches it on.

yt_contains_synthetic_media.description: Tell viewers the video contains realistic content that was altered or generated with AI. YouTube shows a label on the video.

yt_license.description: Video license: `youtube` (standard YouTube license) or `creativeCommon`. Any other value answers 400.

yt_embeddable.description: Whether the video may be embedded on other sites. `0`, `no` or `false` switches it off; anything else keeps it on.

yt_default_language.description: Language of the video's title and description, as a language code such as `en`. Saved as given.

yt_default_audio_language.description: Language spoken in the video, as a language code such as `en-US`. Saved as given.

yt_recording_date.description: Date the video was recorded, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Any other format answers 400.

tk_privacy_status.description: Who can watch the TikTok video. Case-insensitive, spaces or underscores. Any other value is saved as `Public to Everyone`; omitted leaves it unset, unless `tk_auto_add_music`, `tk_thumb`, `tk_thumb_timestamp` or `tk_is_aigc` is sent, which saves the default. `/api/tiktok_options` lists what the account allows.

tk_allow_comments.description: Allow comments on the TikTok video. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_duet.description: Allow duets. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_stitches.description: Allow stitches. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_promote_own_brand.description: Set to `1` to mark the video as promoting your own brand (TikTok's content disclosure).

tk_promote_other_brand.description: Set to `1` to mark the video as branded content for a third party.

tk_is_aigc.description: Add TikTok's AI-generated content label to the video.

tk_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the TikTok video. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when TikTok has no video.

tk_thumb_timestamp.description: Frame of the video TikTok uses as the cover, in milliseconds from the start. A value that is not a whole number answers 400.

tk_auto_add_music.description: Set to `1` to let TikTok add music to the post.

bs_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on Bluesky. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when Bluesky has no video.

post.summary: Find active library posts whose text, link title, variation or network version contains a phrase.
post.description:
Permission: Content library (`library`) in the workspace.
Searches the active posts of one library, or of every library in the workspace when `library_id` is left out. A post matches when its text, its link title, one of its message variations or one of its per-network messages contains `search_text` (case-insensitive substring). Draft posts are not searched.
Each result is a `/api/library_content_list` item plus the library it sits in. No match answers 200 with an empty `content` list.

post.summary: Move posts out of one library into one or more other libraries.
post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace.
Moves each post in `content_ids` from `from_library_id` into every library in `to_library_ids`. Posts are handled one at a time, so a refused post is reported in `failed` with its own status and the others still move. The call is an error only when no post moved; the answer is then the first failure's status and message.
The post gets a new id in every destination. The id you sent stops being valid after the move; read the new ones from `moved[].new_ids`.

Ids change: Moving creates a fresh post in each destination and removes the original, so every reference you hold to the old id (variations, queue lookups, your own database) must be updated from `new_ids`. With several destinations the order of `new_ids` is not guaranteed to follow `to_library_ids`; read each new post to see which library it is in.

Active posts only: Drafts cannot be moved with this endpoint; a draft id is reported in `failed` with status 404.

content_ids.description: Encrypted post ids to move: one id, a comma-separated string or an array, at most 50. `id` is accepted as an alias when `content_ids` is blank. Every id must be a library post of the workspace (400 / 404 otherwise); only active posts of `from_library_id` are moved, the others are reported in `failed`.

from_library_id.description: Encrypted id of the library the posts sit in now, from `/api/library_list`. A post that is not active in this library is reported in `failed` with status 404.

to_library_ids.description: Encrypted ids of the destination libraries: one id, a comma-separated string or an array, at most 50, without `from_library_id`.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

status.description: 200 when at least one post moved.

id.description: The post id you sent. It no longer resolves after the move.

new_ids.description: Encrypted ids the post now has, one per destination library.

id.description: A post that did not move.

status.description: Why: 404 not active in the source library, 409 one-time-use conflict, 400 other refusal.

failed.error: The post is not in the source library.

post.summary: Copy posts from one library into one or more other libraries.
post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace.
Copies each post in `content_ids` from `from_library_id` into every library in `to_library_ids`. The original stays where it is. Posts are handled one at a time, so a refused post is reported in `failed` with its own status and the others are still copied. post.summary: Delete one or more posts from a library.
post.description:
Permission: Delete content (`lib-delete`) in the workspace.
Deletes the active posts in `id` from the library `library_id`. Every id is checked first: all must be library posts of the workspace and all must be active in that library, otherwise nothing is deleted. The deletion is permanent; the post, its per-network versions and its variations are removed. The call needs `confirm=true`.

No undo: Deleted posts cannot be restored through the API. Duplicate ids in the list are counted once. Drafts are not deleted by this endpoint.

library_id.description: Encrypted id of the library the posts sit in, from `/api/library_list`.

id.description: Encrypted post ids to delete: one id, a comma-separated string or an array, at most 50. A value that is not a valid id answers 400.

confirm.description: Must be `true`; without it the call answers 400 and deletes nothing.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

deleted_count.description: Number of distinct post ids deleted.

post.summary: Move a post to a position in a library's publishing order.
post.description:
Permission: Manage timeslots (`lib-manage`) in the workspace.
Puts `content_id` at `position` (1 publishes next) and shifts the posts in between. Answers with the complete new order, one row per post with its position and encrypted id. Each account's place in that order is read and changed with `/api/library_pointers_list` and `/api/library_pointers_set`.
Moving a post to the position it already has changes nothing and still answers 200 with the order.

Order versus pointers: The order is the library's. Every account connected to the library has its own pointer into it (`/api/library_pointers_list`), so moving a post to position 1 makes it the next post for accounts whose pointer is at the start; an account further down the order reaches it on its next cycle.

Order with gaps: Some older libraries store their order with gaps. A move on such a library answers 409 instead of corrupting the order; `/api/library_content_order_shuffle` renumbers the order, after which moves work.

post.summary: Change a draft of a library field by field.
post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace.
A draft is a library post with a live date in the future: it sits in the library but is not scheduled until that day. This call changes the fields you send over the draft's current values; a field left out keeps its value. The draft must keep a live date; clear it with `/api/library_drafts_publish`.
The content fields here are the simple ones of a library post (one message, one link, the main images, one video); per-network tabs are not touched. For a full rewrite use `/api/library_content_update`.

Patch semantics, unlike library_content_update: The fields you send merge over the draft's current values, so you can change one field alone. `/api/library_content_update` is a full replacement; use it to rewrite per-network tabs.

Main media only: `image_url` and `video_url` replace the post's main media, the media every network uses unless it has its own. Per-network media set in the app are not touched. The files are downloaded and hosted by RecurPost before the draft is saved, so a large video takes a while.

post.summary: Count how often a text appears across the posts of a library or workspace.
post.description:
Permission: Content library (`library`) in the workspace.
Find-and-replace over the posts of one library (`library_id`) or of every library of the workspace (no `library_id`). This call counts how often `search_text` appears, split into post messages, X variations and per-network messages. Run it before `/api/library_bulk_edit_replace`, which uses the same counting.
`include_variations` extends the operation to the X message variations of the posts and `include_customized` to the per-network messages; both are off by default, so only the main message is counted or changed.

Places, not occurrences: `counts.posts`, `counts.variations` and `counts.customized` count the messages that hold the text, which is what a replace rewrites. `counts.matches` counts every occurrence, so it is higher when a message holds the text more than once.

search_text.description: Text to look for, 1 to 500 characters (leading and trailing spaces are trimmed).

library_id.description: Encrypted library id from `/api/library_list` to limit the operation to one library. Without it every library of the workspace is in scope.

include_variations.description: `true` also counts or changes the X message variations of the posts.

include_customized.description: `true` also counts or changes the per-network messages.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

matches.description: Every occurrence of the text in the messages counted.

posts.description: Posts whose message (or X thread) holds the text.

variations.description: X message variations that hold the text (0 unless include_variations).

customized.description: Per-network messages that hold the text (0 unless include_customized).

post.summary: Add time slots for a library on one or several accounts.
post.description:
Permission: Manage timeslots (`lib-manage`) in the workspace.
Adds the same set of slots for `library_id` on every account in `account_id`. Each slot has a `frequency` of `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`, a `day` (1 to 7 for weekly, 1 to 31 for monthly, not read for daily) and either a fixed `time` as `HH:MM` or `best_time` true. A daily slot is stored as seven weekly slots, one per weekday.
Slots are checked against the plan's slot limits before anything is created. When a slot falls later today and the library is active, the app queues the library's next post for it straight away.

Times are local to the account: `time` is read in each account's timezone (the workspace owner's when the account has none). The same request on accounts in different zones publishes at the same local hour in each.

Duplicates: Adding a slot that already exists for the same library, account, day and time creates a second one; delete the extra with `/api/schedule_delete`.

slots.description: 1 to 50 slot objects (an array, or a JSON string holding one). Each has `frequency` (`daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`, case-insensitive), `day` (1 Monday to 7 Sunday for weekly, 1 to 31 for monthly; not read for daily), and `time` as 24-hour `HH:MM` in the account's timezone or `best_time` true. A weekly slot may add `week_of_month`: 1 to 4 for that week only, 99 for the last week of the month, 0 or omitted for every week; any other value, or a non-zero value on a daily or monthly slot, answers 400.

post.summary: Move one slot to another day or time.
post.description:
Permission: Manage timeslots (`lib-manage`) in the workspace.
Moves an existing slot to a new `day` and `time`, or to the account's best time with `best_time=true`, keeping its library and account. The day must fit the slot's frequency: 1 to 7 for a weekly slot, 1 to 31 for a monthly one. As in the app, the posts already queued from the old slot are cancelled, and when the new slot falls later today it is filled at once.

Queued posts are cancelled: Posts the old slot had already placed in the queue are removed and the libraries pick again for the new slot. Edited queue posts from that slot are lost too, as when the slot is dragged on the Schedules page.

Week of month is kept: A weekly slot limited to one week of the month keeps that limit; this call changes only the day and the time.

best_time.description: `true` publishes at the account's calculated best time instead of a fixed time; `time` is then ignored. Accepts `true`/`false`, `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`; any other value answers 400.

post.summary: Attach an RSS feed to a library and fetch its current articles.
post.description:
Permission: Manage timeslots (`lib-manage`) in the workspace.
Reads the feed at `url`, attaches it to `library_id` and stores its current articles for that library: waiting for approval, or straight into the library with `auto_approve`. The feed is fetched during the call, so it can take several seconds. From then on new articles are picked up by RecurPost's periodic feed check.
`message_template` is the text of every post made from an article. It may contain placeholders written as `{|||name|||}`, which are replaced per article: `{|||title|||}`, `{|||description|||}`, `{|||post_url|||}`, `{|||link|||}`, `{|||pubDate|||}`, `{|||author|||}` and `{|||categories|||}`. YouTube addresses (channels, playlists, videos and their XML feeds) are refused: the items would be links whose title the reader takes from YouTube pages, which YouTube does not reliably serve to servers.

Articles link to their page: Every post made from an article links to the article's own URL, so the networks that show link previews show the article. `message_template` is the text above that link; leave it out to post the link alone.

Auto approve acts at once: With `auto_approve` true the articles fetched during this call are added to the library immediately, each taking a library post slot on the plan.

url.description: Public http or https address of the RSS or Atom feed, or of a page that links to one. YouTube addresses are refused.

library_id.description: Encrypted id of the library the articles go into, from `/api/library_list`.

message_template.description: Post text built for each article, at most 5000 characters, with `{|||name|||}` placeholders (see above). Left out or blank, each article is posted as its link alone, with the preview the network builds from the page.

auto_approve.description: `true` adds articles to the library without review, including the ones fetched now; `false` (default) leaves them waiting in `/api/feed_items`.

top_of_queue.description: `true` places approved articles at the front of the library's queue so they publish next. Default `false`.

host_images.description: `true` stores the feed's Host images setting, as the web's "Host Images on RecurPost?" box. It copies images that a feed maps into a post's Image(s) to RecurPost storage; the API maps no image field, so posts made from articles are link posts whose preview image stays the article's own image URL, as on the web when no image is mapped. Default `false`.

live_date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` or blank. Posts made from the feed stay drafts and start publishing on this date.

expire_date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` or blank, on or after `live_date`. Posts made from the feed stop recurring after this date.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

id.description: Encrypted feed id. Use it with `library_id` in the other feed calls.

post.summary: Change a feed's settings in one library, or move it to another library.
post.description:
Permission: Manage timeslots (`lib-manage`) in the workspace.
Changes how feed `id` fills library `library_id`. Every setting is optional and a setting left out keeps its value: `auto_approve`, `top_of_queue`, `host_images`, `live_date`, `expire_date` and `message_template` (with the `{|||name|||}` placeholders of `/api/feed_create`). `new_library_id` moves the feed, with its waiting items, to another library of the workspace. The answer is the feed's settings after the change.

An auto-approving feed takes in its backlog: Every update that leaves the feed auto-approving (`auto_approve` sent true, or already on and left out) moves the items waiting in `/api/feed_items` into the library, as many as the workspace owner's library post limit leaves room for; the rest keep waiting. Decide the backlog with `/api/feed_item_approve` and `/api/feed_item_reject` first if you want to keep some out.

top_of_queue.description: `true` places approved articles at the front of the library's queue. A value that is not a boolean counts as not sent.

host_images.description: `true` stores the feed's Host images setting, as the web's "Host Images on RecurPost?" box. It copies images that a feed maps into a post's Image(s) to RecurPost storage; the API maps no image field, so posts made from articles are link posts whose preview image stays the article's own image URL, as on the web when no image is mapped. post.summary: Fetch the feed now and store its new articles.
post.description:
Permission: Manage timeslots (`lib-manage`) in the workspace.
Reads feed `id` from its source right away instead of waiting for RecurPost's periodic check, and stores the articles not seen before: as waiting items for `/api/feed_items`, or straight into library `library_id` when the feed auto-approves. The remote feed is fetched during the call, so it can take a few seconds and is limited to one refresh per feed per minute.

The minute is the clock minute: The refresh counter is per UTC clock minute, not a rolling 60 seconds: two refreshes a few seconds apart are refused only when both fall in the same minute. A refused call still counts.

post.summary: Page through the stored posts one account has published that are not yet imported, 50 per page.
post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace, and the workspace owner must be on a paid plan.
Lists the posts published on the network by one account that RecurPost has stored and that are not imported yet. The network is only asked while nothing is stored for the account (the first call can then take a few seconds); after that the call reads the stored list, and `/api/import_posts_more` and `/api/import_refresh` fetch more. Posts already moved into a library are left out. The list is fixed at 50 posts per page; there is no `per_page` parameter.
Each item's `id` is an encrypted string that `/api/import_to_library` takes in `ids`. Ids are only valid together with the same `account_id`.

The network is asked once: Only the first call for an account (nothing stored yet) pulls posts from the network. Later calls read what is stored; call `/api/import_refresh` for newer posts and `/api/import_posts_more` for older ones.

Empty result is not an error: An account with nothing left to import answers 200 with `items: []`, `total: 0` and `total_pages: 0`.

Instagram videos with licensed audio: Instagram omits the media URL of videos that use copyrighted audio. Such posts come back with `type: photo` and only their thumbnail in `image`.

post.summary: Move a batch of fetched posts into a library, with optional caption and per-network customisation.
post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace, and the workspace owner must be on a paid plan.
Copies the given posts of one account into a library as new library posts. Media is downloaded from the network and re-uploaded to your RecurPost storage. Posts that were imported disappear from `/api/import_posts`.
Before anything is written the endpoint checks the library content limit of the workspace owner: when the batch would pass it, the whole batch is refused with 403 and nothing is imported. The library posts are created on the owner's account. `imported_count` is the number of posts the library really gained; posts whose network media could not be read count in `failed_count`.
customize is an optional JSON object (or a JSON string) shaped like the plugin's customise step:
- Caption keys at the top level: `prefix`, `suffix`, `hashtags` (array), `first_comment`. They apply to every imported post. Prefix, caption, suffix and hashtags are joined with blank lines; a hashtag without `#` gets one.
- `networks`: an object keyed by network short code with that network's posting options. Known keys are `fb`, `ig`, `ln`, `pi`, `gmb`, `tk` and `yt`; other networks and unknown option keys are dropped, and every known option is checked (400 on a bad value). Sending any network switches the library post to customised per-network settings.

The generic `first_comment` is stored for Facebook pages, LinkedIn and Instagram feed posts; a `first_comment` under `networks.fb`, `networks.ln` or `networks.ig` overrides it for that network. `tk` and `yt` options are applied only to imported posts that carry a video. Any other top-level key of `customize` is dropped.

Size the batch to the allowance: The pre-check compares the number of ids with `plan limit - library posts already stored` for the workspace owner. On free plans variations and per-network captions count towards the stored total. The 403 message does not say how much room is left, so keep batches small when the library is close to its limit.

Counted, not assumed: The app reports success even for posts whose media it could not read from the network (and still marks them imported). `imported_count` and `failed_count` come from counting the library before and after the call.

Slow for media-heavy batches: Every image and video is downloaded from the network and re-uploaded to your media storage during the call. Keep batches small when the posts carry videos or carousels.

account_id.description: Encrypted account id the posts were listed from with `/api/import_posts`.

library_id.description: Encrypted id of the library to add the posts to. Get ids from `/api/library_list`.

ids.description: Encrypted `items[].id` values from `/api/import_posts` for the same `account_id`, up to 50: an array, a JSON array string or a comma-separated string. Duplicates are dropped. Every id must be a post of that account that is not imported yet.

customize.description: Caption and per-network options applied to every post of the batch, as a JSON object or a JSON string. See the description for the structure and the nested keys below. Omit it to import the posts as they are.

prefix.description: Text placed before the imported caption, separated by a blank line. Up to 5000 characters.

suffix.description: Text placed after the imported caption, separated by a blank line. Up to 5000 characters.

hashtags.description: Hashtags appended after the suffix on one line, space separated, as an array or a comma-separated string. Each entry is trimmed and prefixed with `#` when it does not start with one; blank entries are dropped.

first_comment.description: First comment stored for Facebook pages, LinkedIn and Instagram feed posts unless a network-specific one is given. Up to 5000 characters.

post_type.description: Facebook post types as integers: `1` Feed, `2` Reel, `3` Story, as an array or a comma-separated string. Any combination of the three is accepted; any other value is refused. Empty or missing means Feed.

share_as_feed.description: `1` to also share a Reel to the feed, `0` not to. A JSON boolean is accepted too.

trial_reel.description: Publish Reels as trial reels. `MANUAL` keeps them as trials until you graduate them, `SS_PERFORMANCE` lets Instagram graduate them on performance. Empty string or omitted means no trial reel.

post.summary: Pull the posts published since the last fetch, or clear the stored list and start over.

Asks the network for the posts of `account_id` published after the last fetch and adds them to the list `/api/import_posts` reads. post.summary: Read the watermark of a social account or of the workspace.
post.description:
Permission: with `scope=account`, Edit social account settings (`manage-accounts`) in the workspace, as the watermark sits in the account's Settings modal; with `scope=workspace`, Workspace settings (`workspace-settings`), which the workspace owner and its Workspace Manager always hold.
A watermark is stamped on every image at posting time. It is set on one social account (`scope=account`) or on the workspace (`scope=workspace`), in which case every account of the workspace without its own watermark inherits it.
This call reads the current settings: of `account_id` when it is sent, otherwise of the workspace (so `{}` or a bare `workspace_id` reads the workspace watermark). For an account the answer also says which workspace watermark it would inherit and whether it opted out of it; for the workspace it counts the accounts that inherit the watermark.

Two answer shapes: With `scope=account` the answer has `settings`, `inherited_from_workspace` and `opted_out`. With `scope=workspace` it has `settings` (without `from_workspace`) and `accounts`.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

post.summary: Remove the watermark of a social account or of the workspace.
post.description:
Permission: with `scope=account`, Edit social account settings (`manage-accounts`) in the workspace; with `scope=workspace`, Workspace settings (`workspace-settings`), which the workspace owner and its Workspace Manager always hold.
A watermark is stamped on every image at posting time. It is set on one social account (`scope=account`, the default) or on the workspace (`scope=workspace`), in which case every account of the workspace without its own watermark inherits it.

post.summary: Add a product to a catalog on Meta, or change one.
post.description:
Permission: workspace owner only.
The product catalog behind Instagram product tags (`in_product_tags` and `in_reel_product_tags` on `/api/post_content`; products are read with `/api/instagram_products`). Every call acts through Instagram business account `account_id`.
Meta's own refusals come back as 400 with Meta's reason; an account whose token Meta no longer accepts answers 409 with `reconnect_required: true`.
Adds a product to `catalog_id`, or changes product `product_id`; send one of the two. Meta takes the whole product every time, so `name`, `price`, `currency`, `url` and `image_url` are required both for a new product and for a change.

Changes happen on Meta: Catalogs and products live in Meta's Commerce Manager, not in RecurPost. A new catalog must be connected to the Instagram shop in Commerce Manager before its products can be tagged, and Meta reviews new products for a few minutes before `/api/instagram_products` lists them.

A change replaces the product: Meta receives every field on a change. Send the whole product, as `/api/instagram_products` returns it, with your changes; a `description` left out is cleared and `availability` goes back to `in stock`. On a change Meta's refusal reads We couldn't update this product. followed by Meta's reason.

account_id.description: Encrypted id of an Instagram business account of the workspace, from `/api/social_account_list`.

price.description: The price as a number of the currency's units, 0 or more, for example `12.50`.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code; case-insensitive, sent upper case.

url.description: The product page, starting with http:// or https://, up to 2000 characters.

post.summary: List library posts in the approval flow: waiting on you, sent by you, or rejected.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace (no role permission is checked). Each scope lists only the posts where you are the author or a reviewer.
Returns library posts in the approval flow for one scope: `to_review` (sent to you and still waiting, the default), `submitted` (sent by you and still waiting) or `rejected` (sent by you and turned down, with the reviewers' comments) or `rejected_by_you` (posts of others you turned down as a reviewer). Narrow to one library with `library_id`.
Each item carries the post's original content, the library it belongs to, who submitted it and when, every reviewer with their decision, and the comment count. The app returns the full set; this endpoint pages it for you, so `total` is the size of the whole scope.

Counts are scope-independent: `counts` always holds all four numbers for the caller in the workspace, whichever scope was asked for; only `items` and `total` follow the scope.

Larger pages than elsewhere: This list allows `per_page` up to 100 rather than the usual 50; a larger value is capped at 100 instead of refused.

Comments per scope: `comments_count` is present on the scopes `rejected` and `rejected_by_you`; the thread itself (`comments`) only on `rejected`. `submitted_at` is in the workspace owner's timezone, `comments[].at` is UTC as stored.

post.summary: Approve a waiting library post into its library.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace (no role permission is checked). You must be one of the post's reviewers.
Records your approval of a post that is waiting for it: the post moves into its library's rotation. You must be one of the post's reviewers and the post must still be waiting.

Decisions are final: Once decided, the post cannot be decided again through the API: an approved post leaves the approval flow (a second call answers 404), a rejected one answers 409. The author comments on a rejected post with `/api/approval_comment`, rewrites it with `/api/approval_edit` and sends it back with `/api/approval_resend`.

Approval counts against the plan: An approved post joins the library like any other post, so the owner's library post limit applies at the moment of approval, not when the author submitted it.

post.summary: Rewrite a post that is waiting for approval or was rejected, as its author or a reviewer; a reviewer may approve it in the same call.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace (no role permission is checked). You must be the post's author or one of its reviewers; `approve=true` needs a reviewer.
Replaces the content of a post in the approval flow, waiting or rejected, with the same content fields `/api/library_content_update` takes: the whole post is rewritten, so send every field you want kept. The caller must be the post's author or one of its reviewers. With `approve=true` a reviewer saves and approves in one step, which puts the post into the library's rotation and counts against the owner's library post limit. Without it the post stays where it is in the flow: a rejected post goes back to its reviewers with `/api/approval_resend`.

Whole post: As with `/api/library_content_update`, fields left out are cleared, not kept. Read the post first with `/api/library_content`.

Per-network media: A network can post media of its own: `<prefix>_image_url` and `<prefix>_video_url` (`fb_`, `tw_`, `ln_`, `in_`, `gmb_`, `pi_`, `yt_`, `tk_`, `th_`, `bs_`) replace `image_url` / `video_url` on that network only and mark its tab as customised. Each network keeps its own cap (Facebook 15, Twitter/X 4, LinkedIn 20, Instagram 10 in all, Google Business 1, Pinterest 1, TikTok 10, Threads 20 in all, Bluesky 4); only Instagram and Threads combine images with a video, ordered by `in_media_order` / `th_media_order`; YouTube takes `yt_video_url` only. A URL named by several networks is downloaded once. Covers (`fb_thumb` and the others) apply to whichever video that network ends up with; `in_image_tags` and `in_product_tags` positions count in `in_image_url` when Instagram has its own images. An empty override is ignored: that network keeps the shared media.

message.description: New post text. `\r\n` is normalised to `\n`.
message.example: Updated: our latest product is now 20% off! https://example.com/product

url.description: Link to share with the post. On a text post the page's title, description and image are fetched and saved as the link preview; when omitted, the first link found in `message` is used instead. On a Pinterest account the value becomes the pin's destination link. `http://` is prepended when the scheme is missing. The host must be a public address.

image_url.description: Image URLs, in display order. Send a JSON array (or repeat `image_url[]` in form encoding); a single string is accepted as a one-item list. At most 20 images. Each URL must be a publicly reachable http or https URL and answer an image content type. URLs already on RecurPost storage (for example from `/api/media_list`) are used as they are; every other URL is copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. May be combined with `video_url` into a mixed post, ordered by `media_order`.

th_image_url.description: Images for Threads accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 20 media in all, images and video together on Threads. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. May be combined with `th_video_url` into a carousel; `th_media_order` sets the order.

th_video_url.description: A video for Threads accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. May be combined with `th_image_url` into a carousel.

th_media_order.description: The order of Threads's own media as a list of the URLs given in `th_image_url` and `th_video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when both are sent. Any other URL answers 400.

bs_image_url.description: Images for Bluesky accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 4 images on Bluesky. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `bs_video_url`.

bs_video_url.description: A video for Bluesky accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `bs_image_url`.

bs_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `bs_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

fb_message.description: Text for Facebook accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_message.description: Text for Twitter/X accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_made_with_ai.description: Label the post as made with AI on Twitter/X. X shows the label on the post.

ln_message.description: Text for LinkedIn accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

in_message.description: Text for Instagram accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

gmb_message.description: Text for Google Business accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

pi_message.description: Text for Pinterest accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

yt_message.description: Text for YouTube accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. On YouTube this is the video description.

tk_message.description: Text for TikTok accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

th_message.description: Text for Threads accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

bs_message.description: Text for Bluesky accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

first_comment.description: First comment posted right after the post, commonly hashtags. Applied on Facebook Pages, LinkedIn and Instagram feed posts unless a network-specific first comment is given.

fb_first_comment.description: Facebook first comment; overrides `first_comment` on Facebook.

fb_mentions.description: Facebook pages to mention, at most 10: page ids from `/api/mention_search`, as a list of ids or of `{page_id, name}` objects. Write each page in the text as `@<page id>`; the publisher turns it into the page's mention on Facebook pages.

fb_background_id.description: Facebook text background for a post without `image_url` or `video_url`: an id from `/api/facebook_backgrounds` (letters, digits, underscore or dash, up to 64 characters). Applied on Facebook pages only.

ln_first_comment.description: LinkedIn first comment; overrides `first_comment` on LinkedIn.

in_first_comment.description: Instagram first comment (feed posts only); overrides `first_comment` on Instagram.

fb_post_type.description: Facebook post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`.

fb_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on Facebook. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

fb_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Facebook post as made with AI. On a reel (`fb_post_type=reel`) Facebook shows its AI label on the reel; on an image post every image on the Facebook tab is labelled as an AI-generated photo, declared by you. Use `fb_ai_images` to label only some images or to give the provenance type.

fb_ai_images.description: Images to label as AI-generated photos on Facebook, named by the original URLs given in `image_url` (or `fb_image_url` when Facebook has its own images). A JSON array of URL strings, or of objects with `image_url` and `provenance_type`: `EXPLICIT` (declared by you, the default), `EXPLICIT_AI_EDIT` (edited with AI), `C2PA` (content credentials in the file), `IPTC` (IPTC AI metadata in the file) or `INVISIBLE_WATERMARK`. Labels the Facebook tab on its own, without `fb_is_ai_generated`. A URL that is not one of the post's Facebook images, or any other provenance type, answers 400.

ln_document.description: Public URL of a document to post as a LinkedIn document (carousel) post: PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX, detected from the file bytes, not the file name. The file is downloaded and stored on RecurPost storage and the LinkedIn tab becomes a document post. A file of another type is left as given and ignored by the publisher. Google Drive share links are resolved.

ln_document_title.description: Title shown on the LinkedIn document. Defaults to the file name without its extension.

ln_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on LinkedIn. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

in_post_type.description: Instagram post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`. A reel needs a `video_url`.

in_reel_share_in_feed.description: Whether a reel also appears in the profile feed. Only read when `in_post_type` is `reel`.

in_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for an Instagram reel. Only applied when `in_post_type` is `reel` and the post has a `video_url`; copied to RecurPost storage because Meta fetches it at publish time.

in_location_id.description: Instagram place id to tag the post with. Take `id` and `name` from `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_location_city.description: City of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_location_country.description: Country of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_image_tags.description: People to tag on feed images. A JSON array of objects with `username`, `x` and `y` (fractions of the image width and height between 0 and 1) and `image` (1-based position in `image_url`, default 1). The leading `@` is optional.

in_reel_tags.description: Usernames to tag on a reel, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. Only saved when the post has a `video_url`.

in_collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. At most 3.

in_trial_reel.description: Publish the reel as a trial reel, shown to non-followers first. `manual`: you decide in Instagram when to share it with followers; `performance`: Instagram shares it when it does well. Reels only.

in_product_tags.description: Instagram product tags on images: objects with `account_id` (encrypted, the account whose catalog holds the product), `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`), `image` (1-based position in `image_url`), `x` and `y` (0 to 1, default 0.5), and optionally `product_name` and `product_image`.

in_reel_product_tags.description: Products tagged on a reel: objects with `account_id` (encrypted) and `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`), optionally `product_name` and `image_url`. Reels only.

in_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Instagram post as AI-generated. Instagram shows its AI label on the post.

pi_ai_modified.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: the Pin's content was generated or modified with AI.

pi_synthetic_performer.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: a person shown or heard in the Pin is AI-generated.

gbp_cta.description: Call-to-action button on the Google Business post. Case-insensitive. An unknown value or `None` saves no button. On a link post with no CTA given, `Learn more` pointing at the link is set automatically.

gbp_cta_url.description: Link the button opens. Not used for `Call now`. With `gbp_cta=Offer` and no `gbp_redeem_offer_link`, this value doubles as the redeem link.

yt_thumb.description: Custom thumbnail URL for the YouTube video. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off.

yt_video_made_for_kids.description: Whether the video is made for kids. Only `yes` switches it on.

yt_contains_synthetic_media.description: Tell viewers the video contains realistic content that was altered or generated with AI. YouTube shows a label on the video.

tk_privacy_status.description: Who can watch the TikTok video. Case-insensitive, spaces or underscores. Any other value, or none, is saved as `Public to Everyone`; the other TikTok options and the AI label are kept either way. `/api/tiktok_options` lists what the account allows.

tk_allow_comments.description: Allow comments on the TikTok video. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_duet.description: Allow duets. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_stitches.description: Allow stitches. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_promote_other_brand.description: Set to `1` to mark the video as branded content for a third party.

tk_is_aigc.description: Add TikTok's AI-generated content label to the video.

post.summary: Send a rejected post back to its reviewers.

Permission: any active member of the workspace (no role permission is checked). You must be the post's author.
Puts a rejected post back in front of its reviewers: it returns to waiting, the reviewers get the approval request mail again, and a fresh decision is recorded with `/api/approval_approve` or `/api/approval_reject`. Only the post's author may do this, and only for a rejected post. Rewrite the post first with `/api/approval_edit`; this call sends the content as it stands.

Sends mail to every reviewer: Each successful call mails the reviewers again. The post goes back to `submitted` in `/api/approval_list` and the reviewers see it under `to_review`.

post.summary: Columns and cards of the board, for one workspace or for every workspace of the owner you belong to.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace. Every member may open the board; `can_create` and the actions of `/api/workflow_card` say what your role may do on it.
Returns the board of the workspace owner: its columns (Ideas, the owner's stages, Scheduled) with the cards in each, the team members who can be assigned, and the workflow settings.
Scoping. The board is the owner's, not yours. `workspace_id` (or your default workspace when omitted) picks the owner; the board then spans every workspace of that owner you are an active member of. The owner's signup default workspace is kept off the board while other workspaces exist, as on the dashboard; passing its id is the same as passing none. When you pass any other `workspace_id` only that workspace's cards are returned; otherwise all board workspaces are. `workspace_ids`, when sent, picks the workspaces instead (`workspace_id` then only picks the owner). Every card carries its own `workspace_id`.
Card shape. This is the full card object; `/api/workflow_card`, the idea and post create and edit calls and `/api/workflow_card_move` return the same fields.

Whose board: Team members see the board of the owner whose workspace they pass. Your own signup workspace is the default when you omit `workspace_id`, so as a team member pass the agency's `workspace_id` to reach their board.

Timezones: `target_date` is the owner's wall clock as typed. `schedule.first_at` and the schedule times of `/api/workflow_card` are converted to the owner's timezone. `created_at` and `updated_at` are the app's stored UTC values.

Ids: Card, stage, label, member, account, activity and post ids are encrypted strings. A missing id (the stage of an idea, the post of an unscheduled card) is an empty string.

Workspaces that show members only their own posts: When a card's workspace has show own posts on, a member who does not own that workspace gets only the cards they created or are assigned to; the other cards of that workspace are left out of `columns[].cards` and the counts. The owner sees every card.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`. When given, the board shows this workspace only; the owner's signup default workspace (`is_default` in the list) gives the whole board instead, the same as leaving it out.

workspace_ids.description: Encrypted workspace ids (array, JSON array string or comma-separated) to show instead of the default selection. Every id must be a board workspace you belong to, else 403. When sent it wins over the narrowing by `workspace_id`.

has_workflow.description: false when the owner has not set up a workflow yet; the body then holds only `status`, `message`, `has_workflow`, `workspaces` and an empty `columns`.

items.description: Board workspaces you belong to, by name.

selected.description: true when this workspace's cards are in the response.

items.description: Board columns in order: Ideas (when enabled), each stage, Scheduled.

name.description: Column name as the owner named the stage.

stage_id.description: Encrypted stage id to use in `stage_id`, `to` and `return_stage_id`; empty string for Ideas and Scheduled.

color.description: Stage colour name; blank for Ideas and Scheduled.

items.description: Cards in the column, in board order. Each is a card object as described below.

workspace_id.description: Encrypted id of the workspace the card belongs to.

stage_id.description: Encrypted id of the stage the card is in; empty string for an idea or a card in Scheduled.

title.description: Card title.

items.description: Platform keys the card targets: `instagram`, `facebook`, `linkedin`, `twitter`, `google`, `pinterest`, `youtube`, `tiktok`, `threads`, `bluesky`.
Encrypted ids of the social accounts the card will publish to.

target_date.description: Target date in the owner's wall clock, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`; blank when none.

assignee.description: `{id, name}` of the person assigned (encrypted id), or null.

items.description: Labels on the card: `{id, name, color}`, `id` encrypted.
Attached files: `{url, type}` with type `image` or `video`.

status.description: Review state the app keeps on the card, for example `open`, `pending_review`, `awaiting_client`, `changes_requested`, `approved` or `scheduled`; `open` when the app stores none.

client_approval.description: true when the card is shared with the client for approval.

urgent.description: true when an urgent client approval was requested.

source.description: `team`, or `client` for ideas the client suggested.

count.description: Number of schedule slots on the card.

first_at.description: Earliest slot in the owner's timezone, or null.
