created_by.description: `{id, name}` of the creator (encrypted id), or null when there is none (client-suggested ideas).

created_at.description: Creation time as stored by the app (UTC).

updated_at.description: Last change as stored by the app (UTC).

items.description: Team members on the board: `{id, name, role}`. `id` is the encrypted user id to use in `assignee_user_id` and `user_id`.

ideas_enabled.description: Whether the Ideas column is on.

post.summary: Create a post card in a stage.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace. The app checks your role may create posts (Write and edit their posts); the owner and the Workspace Manager always may.
Creates a post card in the stage you name with `stage_id` (required, with `title`). The idea fields plus accounts, a draft schedule and the per-network customisations, as in the post composer.
Each field is checked against the owner before the app is called: platforms against the known keys, accounts and labels against the owner's, media URLs must be public, schedule slots well formed. The app then applies the dashboard rules (your role's create permission, accounts belonging to the card's workspace, no schedule slot in the past).
Per-network customisations take the fields of `/api/post_content`: `first_comment`, a network's own text (`fb_message`, `in_message` and so on), its own media (`fb_image_url`, `in_video_url`), alt text and the platform options (`fb_post_type`, `in_post_type`, `yt_title`, `tk_privacy_status`, `gbp_cta`, the AI labels). The card's `description` stands for `message` and its `media` for the shared `image_url` and `video_url`. The fields are checked and any media they name is fetched into the owner's storage exactly as on `/api/post_content`, and the app stores the result the way its composer does, so the card publishes with the same per-network content and options.

Schedule slots are drafts: The slots you send stay on the card until it reaches the Scheduled column (`/api/workflow_card_advance` with `to_scheduled`, or client approval); only then do they become queue posts. The `at` time is read in the account's timezone, and the card reads it back in the owner's. Members without Publish or schedule cannot set slots: the app ignores `schedule` from them.

Customisations are a set: Sending any customisation field replaces the card's stored customisations with the fields you send, so send the whole set you want kept. Send none to leave the stored ones alone: when such an edit changes `description` or `media`, the stored customisations are rebuilt over the new caption and media, so every network gets the change and keeps its own options and its own text or media; on `/api/workflow_post_edit`, `clear_customizations` `true` drops them. Read the stored set back as `card.customizations` of `/api/workflow_card`, by network tab (the stored keys, not these exact param names).

Media hosting: Without customisation fields the `media` URLs are stored as sent (the app's own uploads are already on RecurPost storage). With customisation fields the shared media is fetched into the owner's storage the way `/api/post_content` does, the card reads back those URLs, and its tabs name the same files. A card with several videos carries only the first in the customised tabs.

title.description: Card title.

stage_id.description: Encrypted id of the stage the post starts in, from `columns[].stage_id` of `/api/workflow_board`. Not a Client Review stage: a post reaches the client only through the hand-over (`/api/workflow_card_advance`), where the app checks accounts, schedule and media.

description.example: Short teaser for the spring launch.

platforms.description: Platform keys (array, JSON-encoded array string or comma-separated): `instagram`, `facebook`, `linkedin`, `twitter`, `google`, `pinterest`, `youtube`, `tiktok`, `threads`, `bluesky`.

account_ids.description: Encrypted social account ids (array, JSON array string or comma-separated) the card will publish to. They must be the workspace owner's accounts (404 otherwise), and the app requires them to be attached to the card's workspace.

target_date.description: Target date in the owner's wall clock, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

assignee_user_id.description: Encrypted user id from `members[]` of `/api/workflow_board` or `/api/workflow_card`; `0` or an empty string clears the assignee. It must be the owner or an active member of a board workspace (404 otherwise). A person who may not work the stage is not assigned; with no assignee the app may pick one for the stage by its own rules. Read `assignee` on the card.

share_with_client.description: Whether the card is shared with the client for approval. Defaults to the workflow setting for posts. Only the owner and members with Send posts to clients can set it; for anyone else it is ignored and the workflow setting applies. Read `client_approval` on the card to see what was kept.

label_ids.description: Encrypted label ids of the owner's labels (`/api/label_list`): an array, a JSON array string or a comma-separated list, at most 50.

media.description: Up to 10 attachments as publicly reachable http or https URLs: an array, a JSON array string, a comma-separated string, or one `{url, type}` object. Each entry is a URL string or `{url, type}` with type `image` or `video`; without a type, `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.m4v` and `.webm` count as video, everything else as image.

schedule.description: Draft schedule slots, one object per slot (an array or a JSON array string): `{account_id, at}` with `at` as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` (wall clock of that account's timezone), or `{account_id, date, best_time: true}` with `date` as `YYYY-MM-DD` to let RecurPost pick the best time that day. `account_id` is an encrypted account id of the owner. Only the owner, the Workspace Manager and members with Publish or schedule may set the schedule; from anyone else the app ignores it without an error. A slot in the past is refused.

image_url.description: Shared images for the per-network build, as on `/api/post_content`: a JSON array, a JSON array string or one URL. Sending it counts as a customisation field. Without it the card's image media is used. The images are fetched into the owner's storage and replace the card's `media`.

video_url.description: Shared video for the per-network build, as on `/api/post_content` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Sending it counts as a customisation field. Without it the card's first video is used. The file is fetched into the owner's storage and becomes part of the card's `media`.

url.description: Link to share, as on `/api/post_content`. Counts as a customisation field.

host_images_on_recurpost.description: As on `/api/post_content`: `false` keeps your own image URLs instead of copying them to RecurPost storage. Counts as a customisation field.

alt_text.description: Alternative text per image, in `image_url` order; a single string applies to the first image. At most 1000 characters each. Saved on the Facebook, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and Bluesky tabs; Instagram does not take alt text here.

fb_image_url.description: Images for Facebook accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 15 images on Facebook. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `fb_video_url`.

fb_video_url.description: A video for Facebook accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `fb_image_url`.

fb_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `fb_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

tw_image_url.description: Images for Twitter/X accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 4 images on Twitter/X. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `tw_video_url`.

tw_video_url.description: A video for Twitter/X accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `tw_image_url`.

tw_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `tw_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

ln_image_url.description: Images for LinkedIn accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 20 images on LinkedIn. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `ln_video_url`.

ln_video_url.description: A video for LinkedIn accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `ln_image_url`.

ln_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `ln_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

in_image_url.description: Images for Instagram accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 10 media in all, images and video together on Instagram. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. May be combined with `in_video_url` into a carousel; `in_media_order` sets the order.

in_video_url.description: A video for Instagram accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. May be combined with `in_image_url` into a carousel.

in_media_order.description: The order of Instagram's own media as a list of the URLs given in `in_image_url` and `in_video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when both are sent. Any other URL answers 400.

gmb_image_url.description: Images for Google Business accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 1 image on Google Business. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `gmb_video_url`.

gmb_video_url.description: A video for Google Business accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `gmb_image_url`.

pi_image_url.description: Images for Pinterest accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 1 image on Pinterest. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `pi_video_url`.

pi_video_url.description: A video for Pinterest accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `pi_image_url`.

pi_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `pi_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

yt_video_url.description: A video for YouTube accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. YouTube takes a video only, so there is no `yt_image_url`.

tk_image_url.description: Images for TikTok accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 10 images on TikTok. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `tk_video_url`.

tk_video_url.description: A video for TikTok accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `tk_image_url`.

th_image_url.description: Images for Threads accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 20 media in all, images and video together on Threads. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. May be combined with `th_video_url` into a carousel; `th_media_order` sets the order.

th_video_url.description: A video for Threads accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. May be combined with `th_image_url` into a carousel.

th_media_order.description: The order of Threads's own media as a list of the URLs given in `th_image_url` and `th_video_url`. Media left out of the list follow, video first. Only read when both are sent. Any other URL answers 400.

th_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `th_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

bs_image_url.description: Images for Bluesky accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 4 images on Bluesky. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `bs_video_url`.

bs_video_url.description: A video for Bluesky accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `bs_image_url`.

bs_alt_text.description: Alternative text for the `bs_image_url` images, in that order; at most 1000 characters each. The shared `alt_text` is not applied to a network that has its own images.
example: Square crop of the sale banner

fb_message.description: Text for Facebook accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_message.description: Text for Twitter/X accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_made_with_ai.description: Label the post as made with AI on Twitter/X. X shows the label on the post.

ln_message.description: Text for LinkedIn accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

in_message.description: Text for Instagram accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

gmb_message.description: Text for Google Business accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

pi_message.description: Text for Pinterest accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

yt_message.description: Text for YouTube accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. On YouTube this is the video description.

tk_message.description: Text for TikTok accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

th_message.description: Text for Threads accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

bs_message.description: Text for Bluesky accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

first_comment.description: First comment posted right after the post, commonly hashtags. Applied on Facebook Pages, LinkedIn and Instagram feed posts unless a network-specific first comment is given.

fb_first_comment.description: Facebook first comment; overrides `first_comment` on Facebook.

ln_first_comment.description: LinkedIn first comment; overrides `first_comment` on LinkedIn.

in_first_comment.description: Instagram first comment (feed posts only); overrides `first_comment` on Instagram.

fb_post_type.description: Facebook post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`.

fb_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on Facebook. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

fb_mentions.description: Facebook pages to mention, up to 10: page ids from `/api/mention_search`, as a JSON array of ids or of objects with `page_id` and `name`. Write `@<page id>` in the text where each mention should appear; the publisher turns it into the page's mention on Facebook Pages. An id that is not all digits answers 400.

fb_background_id.description: Facebook text background for a post without `image_url` or `video_url`: an id from `/api/facebook_backgrounds` (letters, digits, underscore or dash, up to 64 characters). Applied on Facebook pages only.

fb_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Facebook post as made with AI. On a reel (`fb_post_type=reel`) Facebook shows its AI label on the reel; on an image post every image on the Facebook tab is labelled as an AI-generated photo, declared by you. Use `fb_ai_images` to label only some images or to give the provenance type.

fb_ai_images.description: Images to label as AI-generated photos on Facebook, named by the original URLs given in `image_url` (or `fb_image_url` when Facebook has its own images). A JSON array of URL strings, or of objects with `image_url` and `provenance_type`: `EXPLICIT` (declared by you, the default), `EXPLICIT_AI_EDIT` (edited with AI), `C2PA` (content credentials in the file), `IPTC` (IPTC AI metadata in the file) or `INVISIBLE_WATERMARK`. Labels the Facebook tab on its own, without `fb_is_ai_generated`. A URL that is not one of the post's Facebook images, or any other provenance type, answers 400.

ln_document.description: Public URL of a document to post as a LinkedIn document (carousel) post: PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX, detected from the file bytes, not the file name. The file is downloaded and stored on RecurPost storage and the LinkedIn tab becomes a document post. A file of another type is left as given and ignored by the publisher. Google Drive share links are resolved.

ln_document_title.description: Title shown on the LinkedIn document. Defaults to the file name without its extension.

ln_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on LinkedIn. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

in_post_type.description: Instagram post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`. A reel needs a `video_url`.

in_reel_share_in_feed.description: Whether a reel also appears in the profile feed. Only read when `in_post_type` is `reel`.

in_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for an Instagram reel. Only applied when `in_post_type` is `reel` and the post has a `video_url`; copied to RecurPost storage because Meta fetches it at publish time.

in_location_id.description: Instagram place id to tag the post with. Take `id` and `name` from `/api/instagram_locations`. `in_location_name` is required with it.

in_location_name.description: Name of the place in `in_location_id`, required with it.

in_location_city.description: City of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_location_country.description: Country of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_image_tags.description: People to tag on feed images. A JSON array of objects with `username`, `x` and `y` (fractions of the image width and height between 0 and 1) and `image` (1-based position in `image_url`, default 1). The leading `@` is optional. Any entry missing a username, with coordinates outside 0..1 or pointing past the last image answers 400.

in_reel_tags.description: Usernames to tag on a reel, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. Only saved when the post has a `video_url`; answers 400 without one.

in_collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. At most 3; more answer 400.

in_audio_id.description: Music for an Instagram reel: a track id from `/api/instagram_audio_search`. Needs `in_post_type` `reel`, a `video_url` and `in_audio_account_id`; ignored on feed and story posts.

in_audio_account_id.description: Encrypted id of the Instagram account the audio search ran for (the `account_id` in that answer). Required with `in_audio_id`.

in_audio_type.description: Kind of track, as the search returned it.

in_audio_title.description: Track title from the search, stored for display.

in_audio_artist.description: Artist from the search, stored for display.

in_audio_duration_ms.description: Track length in milliseconds from the search; 0 when omitted.

in_audio_volume.description: Volume of the added track, 0 to 100.

in_video_volume.description: Volume of the video's own sound under the track, 0 to 100; 0 mutes it.

in_trial_reel.description: Publish the reel as an Instagram trial reel (shown to non-followers first): `manual` leaves sharing to everyone up to you, `performance` lets Instagram share it when it does well. Reels only.

in_product_tags.description: Shopping tags on feed images. A JSON array of objects with `account_id` (encrypted Instagram account), `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`), `image` (1-based position in `image_url`, default 1), `x` and `y` (fractions 0 to 1, default 0.5) and optional `product_name` and `product_image` for display. Only kept on the Instagram tab.

in_reel_product_tags.description: Shopping tags on a reel. A JSON array of objects with `account_id` (encrypted Instagram account), `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`) and optional `product_name` and `image_url` for display. Needs `in_post_type` `reel`.

in_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Instagram post as AI-generated. Instagram shows its AI label on the post.

pi_title.description: Pin title. The destination link of the pin is `url` or the first link in the text.
pi_title.example: Summer Sale - Best Deals of the Season

pi_ai_modified.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: the Pin's content was generated or modified with AI.

pi_synthetic_performer.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: a person shown or heard in the Pin is AI-generated.

gbp_cta.description: Call-to-action button on the Google Business post. Case-insensitive. An unknown value or `None` saves no button. On a link post with no CTA given, `Learn more` pointing at the link is set automatically.

gbp_cta_url.description: Link the button opens. Not used for `Call now`. With `gbp_cta=Offer` and no `gbp_redeem_offer_link`, this value doubles as the redeem link.

gbp_offer_title.description: Offer title; offer fields are used when `gbp_cta` is `Offer`.

gbp_offer_start_date.description: Offer start, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in the workspace owner's timezone. Stored as sent without a check; the publisher reads the date and the time from it, so a date alone means midnight and a value that is not a date makes the offer fail on Google.

gbp_offer_end_date.description: Offer end, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in the workspace owner's timezone, after the start. Stored as sent without a check, like the start.

gbp_offer_coupon_code.description: Coupon code shown on the offer.

gbp_offer_terms.description: Terms and conditions of the offer.

yt_title.description: Video title. YouTube needs a `video_url`; `message` or `yt_message` is the description.

yt_category.description: Category name, matched exactly against the list. An unknown or missing name falls back to the default category of the workspace owner's YouTube settings (Entertainment when none is set).

yt_privacy_status.description: Video privacy. Lower-cased and stored as given, so use one of the listed values; an unknown value reaches YouTube and fails there. When omitted it is saved as `public`, and the other YouTube options and the AI label are kept.

yt_thumb.description: Custom thumbnail URL for the YouTube video. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off.

yt_video_made_for_kids.description: Whether the video is made for kids. Only `yes` switches it on.

yt_contains_synthetic_media.description: Tell viewers the video contains realistic content that was altered or generated with AI. YouTube shows a label on the video.

tk_privacy_status.description: Who can watch the TikTok video. Case-insensitive, spaces or underscores. Any other value, or none, is saved as `Public to Everyone`; the other TikTok options and the AI label are kept either way. `/api/tiktok_options` lists what the account allows.

tk_allow_comments.description: Allow comments on the TikTok video. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_duet.description: Allow duets. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_stitches.description: Allow stitches. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_promote_own_brand.description: Set to `1` to mark the video as promoting your own brand (TikTok's content disclosure).

tk_promote_other_brand.description: Set to `1` to mark the video as branded content for a third party.

tk_is_aigc.description: Add TikTok's AI-generated content label to the video.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`. The card is placed in this workspace; without it, or with the owner's signup default workspace, in the first board workspace by name.

message.description: The app's confirmation: `Post created.` or `Post created and assigned to <name>.`

card.description: The saved card in the card shape of `/api/workflow_board`; null when the app returned no card.

card.title: Launch teaser
card.description: Short teaser for the spring launch.

400.description:
invalid_id: workspace_id is not a valid id. Get ids from /api/workspace_list. (workspace_id is sent and does not decrypt to a workspace id.)

invalid_param: This workspace is not on the board. (workspace_id names a workspace of the owner that is not part of the board you see.)

missing_param: title is required. (title is missing or blank.)

missing_param: A post needs the stage_id it starts in; see workflow_board for the stages. (stage_id is missing or blank.)

invalid_id: stage_id is not a valid id. (stage_id does not decrypt.)

invalid_param: platforms must be among instagram, facebook, linkedin, twitter, google, pinterest, youtube, tiktok, threads, bluesky. (platforms holds an unknown key.)

invalid_param: target_date must be a date like 2027-10-20 or 2027-10-20 15:00. (target_date is sent and is not YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.)

invalid_param: share_with_client must be true or false. (share_with_client is sent with a value that is not a boolean.)

invalid_id: label_ids holds a value that is not a valid id. (A label id does not decrypt.)

invalid_param: label_ids takes at most 50 ids per call; <n> were sent. (More than 50 label ids.)

invalid_param: media takes at most 10 files. (More than 10 media entries.)

invalid_url: media must be publicly reachable http or https URLs. (A media URL is empty, has another scheme, or its host is a private, loopback or reserved address.)

invalid_id: assignee_user_id is not a valid id. (assignee_user_id is neither 0 nor a valid encrypted user id.)

invalid_id: account_ids holds a value that is not a valid id. (An account id does not decrypt.)

invalid_param: schedule must be a list of {account_id, at} or {account_id, date, best_time} objects. (schedule is not a list (or JSON list), or a slot is not an object.)

invalid_id: Each schedule slot needs a valid account_id. (A slot's account_id is missing or does not decrypt.)

invalid_param: A best_time slot needs date as YYYY-MM-DD. (best_time is true and date is not YYYY-MM-DD.)

invalid_param: A schedule slot needs at as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, or date with best_time true. (A slot has neither a valid at nor a best_time date.)

invalid_param: <the post builder's message> (A customisation field fails the option checks of /api/post_content (for example "in_trial_reel is manual or performance, on in_post_type reel only."); each check answers with its own text.)

invalid_url: <param> is not allowed: <url>. Send a publicly reachable http or https URL. (A URL the customisations name (image_url, video_url, a network's own media, a thumb, the LinkedIn document) has another scheme, no host, or points to a private or reserved address. A host that does not resolve answers "<param> is not allowed: <url>. The host could not be resolved.")

request_failed: Please choose a stage. (The app did not accept the stage.)

request_failed: Some selected social accounts are not part of "<workspace name>" - this post can only use accounts of its own workspace. (An account is the owner's but not attached to the card's workspace.)

request_failed: This post's scheduled times have already passed. Pick new times before continuing. (A schedule slot is in the past.)

request_failed: <the app's message> (Any other refusal of the app is relayed with its own text (markup stripped).)

invalid_param: A post cannot be created in Client Review. Create it in a work stage and use workflow_card_advance to hand it to the client. (stage_id is a Client Review stage.)

401.description: Authentication failed: token_required, token_invalid, token_expired, credentials_required or invalid_credentials.

403.description:
permission_denied: You are not a member of any workspace on this board. (The owner has no workspace you own or hold an active seat in.)

plan_restriction: You are not allowed to upload video file in your current plan. Please upgrade your RecurPost plan. (The customisations carry a video and the workspace owner's plan has no video.)

permission_denied: To create posts, please ask your workspace owner to give you the "Write and edit their posts" permission. (Your role may not create post cards.)

permission_denied: You are no longer a member of this workspace. Refresh the page to see your current boards. (The app no longer finds your seat in the card's own workspace.)

404.description:
workspace_not_found: Workspace not found or you do not have access to it. (workspace_id names a workspace you are not the owner or an active member of (a pending invite does not count).)

not_found: Stage not found in this workspace (stage_id). (stage_id is not a stage of the owner's workflow.)

not_found: Label not found in your account (label_ids). (A label id is not one of the owner's labels.)

not_found: Member not found in this workspace (assignee_user_id). (assignee_user_id is not the owner or an active member of a board workspace.)

not_found: Social account not found in this account (account_ids). (An account id is not one of the workspace owner's social accounts.)

not_found: Social account not found in this account (schedule account_id). (A slot's account is not one of the workspace owner's social accounts.)

415.description: unsupported_media: <param> did not return a recognizable image. (A media URL could not be fetched as the type it stands for while the customisations were built; other texts of the same code name the detected content type.)

422.description: media_failed: Failed to upload <param>. The URL was reachable but the file could not be processed. (A media file was fetched but could not be stored.)

429.description: Per-minute rate limit reached; see Retry-After.

500.description: internal_error: Something went wrong. Please try again later. (The app failed without a message.)

post.summary: Change a post card: its fields, media and per-network customisations.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace. The app checks your role may edit this card (your own or assigned card, or Edit others' post); setting the schedule needs Publish or schedule, client sharing needs Send posts to clients.
Changes the post card `id`. Fields left out keep their value, and only the fields you send are written. Everything the composer can change on a post is here: title, description, platforms, accounts, target date, assignee, client sharing, labels, media, draft schedule and the per-network customisations. An idea is refused here; change it with `/api/workflow_idea_edit`.
Each field is checked against the owner before the app is called: platforms against the known keys, accounts and labels against the owner's, media URLs must be public, schedule slots well formed. The app then applies the dashboard rules (your role's edit permissions, the card's stage, accounts belonging to the card's workspace, no schedule slot in the past, and at Client Review or Scheduled the hand-over gate on the edited content).
Per-network customisations take the fields of `/api/post_content`: `first_comment`, a network's own text (`fb_message`, `in_message` and so on), its own media (`fb_image_url`, `in_video_url`), alt text and the platform options (`fb_post_type`, `in_post_type`, `yt_title`, `tk_privacy_status`, `gbp_cta`, the AI labels). The card's `description` stands for `message` and its `media` for the shared `image_url` and `video_url`. The fields are checked and any media they name is fetched into the owner's storage exactly as on `/api/post_content`, and the app stores the result the way its composer does, so the card publishes with the same per-network content and options.

Updates are partial: Only fields present in the request are written. Clearing a field means sending it empty (`description`, `target_date`, `account_ids`, `label_ids`, `media`, `schedule` as `""` or `[]`). Move cards between stages with `/api/workflow_card_move`.

Schedule slots are drafts: The slots you send stay on the card until it reaches the Scheduled column (`/api/workflow_card_advance` with `to_scheduled`, or client approval); only then do they become queue posts. The `at` time is read in the account's timezone, and the card reads it back in the owner's. Members without Publish or schedule cannot set slots: the app ignores `schedule` from them.

Scheduled cards edit the queue: On a card already in the Scheduled column the edit goes to its queued posts before the card is saved: a change to `description`, `account_ids`, `media` or the customisations rewrites them, and `schedule` moves them to the times you send (without it they keep their times). Every account on the card needs a time, so add an account together with a `schedule` slot for it; otherwise the edit answers 400 and nothing changes. A refused post leaves the card and the queue as they were. `title` and `platforms` are card fields only and never touch the queue. The card keeps no draft schedule afterwards.

Customisations are a set: Sending any customisation field replaces the card's stored customisations with the fields you send, so send the whole set you want kept. Send none to leave the stored ones alone: when such an edit changes `description` or `media`, the stored customisations are rebuilt over the new caption and media, so every network gets the change and keeps its own options and its own text or media; on `/api/workflow_post_edit`, `clear_customizations` `true` drops them. Read the stored set back as `card.customizations` of `/api/workflow_card`, by network tab (the stored keys, not these exact param names).

Media hosting: Without customisation fields the `media` URLs are stored as sent (the app's own uploads are already on RecurPost storage). With customisation fields the shared media is fetched into the owner's storage the way `/api/post_content` does, the card reads back those URLs, and its tabs name the same files. A card with several videos carries only the first in the customised tabs.

title.description: New title; blank or missing keeps the stored one.

description.description: Description or caption draft. Send an empty string to clear it.
description.example: Short teaser for the spring launch.

platforms.description: Platform keys (array, JSON-encoded array string or comma-separated): `instagram`, `facebook`, `linkedin`, `twitter`, `google`, `pinterest`, `youtube`, `tiktok`, `threads`, `bluesky`.

account_ids.description: Encrypted social account ids (array, JSON array string or comma-separated) the card will publish to. They must be the workspace owner's accounts (404 otherwise), and the app requires them to be attached to the card's workspace. Send an empty string or empty array to clear.

target_date.description: Target date in the owner's wall clock, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. Send an empty string to clear.

assignee_user_id.description: Encrypted user id from `members[]` of `/api/workflow_board` or `/api/workflow_card`; `0` or an empty string clears the assignee. It must be the owner or an active member of a board workspace (404 otherwise). A person who may not work the card's stage is not assigned: the card is left unassigned, so read `assignee` on the card.

share_with_client.description: Whether the card is shared with the client for approval. Only the owner and members with Send posts to clients can change it; for anyone else it is ignored. Read `client_approval` on the card to see what was kept.

label_ids.description: Encrypted label ids of the owner's labels (`/api/label_list`): an array, a JSON array string or a comma-separated list, at most 50. Replaces the current labels; an empty value clears them.

media.description: Up to 10 attachments as publicly reachable http or https URLs: an array, a JSON array string, a comma-separated string, or one `{url, type}` object. Each entry is a URL string or `{url, type}` with type `image` or `video`; without a type, `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.m4v` and `.webm` count as video, everything else as image. Replaces the current media.

schedule.description: Draft schedule slots, one object per slot (an array or a JSON array string): `{account_id, at}` with `at` as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` (wall clock of that account's timezone), or `{account_id, date, best_time: true}` with `date` as `YYYY-MM-DD` to let RecurPost pick the best time that day. `account_id` is an encrypted account id of the owner. Only the owner, the Workspace Manager and members with Publish or schedule may set the schedule; from anyone else the app ignores it without an error. A slot in the past is refused. Replaces the current slots; an empty string or empty list clears them.

clear_customizations.description: `true` drops every stored per-network customisation of the card; the shared description and media stay. Ignored when customisation fields are sent along.

image_url.description: Shared images for the per-network build, as on `/api/post_content`: a JSON array, a JSON array string or one URL. Sending it counts as a customisation field. Without it the card's image media is used. The images are fetched into the owner's storage and replace the card's `media`.

video_url.description: Shared video for the per-network build, as on `/api/post_content` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Sending it counts as a customisation field. Without it the card's first video is used. The file is fetched into the owner's storage and becomes part of the card's `media`.

url.description: Link to share, as on `/api/post_content`. Counts as a customisation field.

host_images_on_recurpost.description: As on `/api/post_content`: `false` keeps your own image URLs instead of copying them to RecurPost storage. Counts as a customisation field.

alt_text.description: Alternative text per image, in `image_url` order; a single string applies to the first image. At most 1000 characters each. Saved on the Facebook, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and Bluesky tabs; Instagram does not take alt text here.

fb_image_url.description: Images for Facebook accounts instead of `image_url`, same rules and hosting as `image_url`. At most 15 images on Facebook. Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised; the other networks keep the shared media. Cannot be combined with `fb_video_url`.

fb_video_url.description: A video for Facebook accounts instead of `video_url`, same rules and hosting as `video_url` (mp4 or mov, paid plan). Replaces that network's whole media set and marks its tab as customised. Cannot be combined with `fb_image_url`.

fb_message.description: Text for Facebook accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_message.description: Text for Twitter/X accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

tw_made_with_ai.description: Label the post as made with AI on Twitter/X. X shows the label on the post.

ln_message.description: Text for LinkedIn accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

in_message.description: Text for Instagram accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

gmb_message.description: Text for Google Business accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

pi_message.description: Text for Pinterest accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

yt_message.description: Text for YouTube accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview. On YouTube this is the video description.

tk_message.description: Text for TikTok accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

th_message.description: Text for Threads accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

bs_message.description: Text for Bluesky accounts when it should differ from `message`. On a text-only post the first link in this text becomes that network's link preview.

first_comment.description: First comment posted right after the post, commonly hashtags. Applied on Facebook Pages, LinkedIn and Instagram feed posts unless a network-specific first comment is given.

fb_first_comment.description: Facebook first comment; overrides `first_comment` on Facebook.

ln_first_comment.description: LinkedIn first comment; overrides `first_comment` on LinkedIn.

in_first_comment.description: Instagram first comment (feed posts only); overrides `first_comment` on Instagram.

fb_post_type.description: Facebook post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`.

fb_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on Facebook. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

fb_mentions.description: Facebook pages to mention, up to 10: page ids from `/api/mention_search`, as a JSON array of ids or of objects with `page_id` and `name`. Write `@<page id>` in the text where each mention should appear; the publisher turns it into the page's mention on Facebook Pages. An id that is not all digits answers 400.

fb_background_id.description: Facebook text background for a post without `image_url` or `video_url`: an id from `/api/facebook_backgrounds` (letters, digits, underscore or dash, up to 64 characters). Applied on Facebook pages only.

fb_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Facebook post as made with AI. On a reel (`fb_post_type=reel`) Facebook shows its AI label on the reel; on an image post every image on the Facebook tab is labelled as an AI-generated photo, declared by you. Use `fb_ai_images` to label only some images or to give the provenance type.

fb_ai_images.description: Images to label as AI-generated photos on Facebook, named by the original URLs given in `image_url` (or `fb_image_url` when Facebook has its own images). A JSON array of URL strings, or of objects with `image_url` and `provenance_type`: `EXPLICIT` (declared by you, the default), `EXPLICIT_AI_EDIT` (edited with AI), `C2PA` (content credentials in the file), `IPTC` (IPTC AI metadata in the file) or `INVISIBLE_WATERMARK`. Labels the Facebook tab on its own, without `fb_is_ai_generated`. A URL that is not one of the post's Facebook images, or any other provenance type, answers 400.

ln_document.description: Public URL of a document to post as a LinkedIn document (carousel) post: PDF, PPT, PPTX, DOC or DOCX, detected from the file bytes, not the file name. The file is downloaded and stored on RecurPost storage and the LinkedIn tab becomes a document post. A file of another type is left as given and ignored by the publisher. Google Drive share links are resolved.

ln_document_title.description: Title shown on the LinkedIn document. Defaults to the file name without its extension.

ln_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for the video on LinkedIn. Ignored when the post has no `video_url`.

in_post_type.description: Instagram post type. Case-insensitive; an unknown value keeps `feed`. A reel needs a `video_url`.

in_reel_share_in_feed.description: Whether a reel also appears in the profile feed. Only read when `in_post_type` is `reel`.

in_thumb.description: Custom cover image URL for an Instagram reel. Only applied when `in_post_type` is `reel` and the post has a `video_url`; copied to RecurPost storage because Meta fetches it at publish time.

in_location_id.description: Instagram place id to tag the post with. Take `id` and `name` from `/api/instagram_locations`. `in_location_name` is required with it.

in_location_name.description: Name of the place in `in_location_id`, required with it.

in_location_city.description: City of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_location_country.description: Country of the tagged place, as returned by `/api/instagram_locations`.

in_image_tags.description: People to tag on feed images. A JSON array of objects with `username`, `x` and `y` (fractions of the image width and height between 0 and 1) and `image` (1-based position in `image_url`, default 1). The leading `@` is optional. Any entry missing a username, with coordinates outside 0..1 or pointing past the last image answers 400.

in_reel_tags.description: Usernames to tag on a reel, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. Only saved when the post has a `video_url`; answers 400 without one.

in_collaborators.description: Instagram usernames invited as collaborators, as a JSON array or a comma-separated string. At most 3; more answer 400.

in_audio_id.description: Music for an Instagram reel: a track id from `/api/instagram_audio_search`. Needs `in_post_type` `reel`, a `video_url` and `in_audio_account_id`; ignored on feed and story posts.

in_audio_account_id.description: Encrypted id of the Instagram account the audio search ran for (the `account_id` in that answer). Required with `in_audio_id`.

in_audio_type.description: Kind of track, as the search returned it.

in_audio_title.description: Track title from the search, stored for display.

in_audio_artist.description: Artist from the search, stored for display.

in_audio_duration_ms.description: Track length in milliseconds from the search; 0 when omitted.

in_audio_volume.description: Volume of the added track, 0 to 100.

in_video_volume.description: Volume of the video's own sound under the track, 0 to 100; 0 mutes it.

in_trial_reel.description: Publish the reel as an Instagram trial reel (shown to non-followers first): `manual` leaves sharing to everyone up to you, `performance` lets Instagram share it when it does well. Reels only.

in_product_tags.description: Shopping tags on feed images. A JSON array of objects with `account_id` (encrypted Instagram account), `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`), `image` (1-based position in `image_url`, default 1), `x` and `y` (fractions 0 to 1, default 0.5) and optional `product_name` and `product_image` for display. Only kept on the Instagram tab.

in_reel_product_tags.description: Shopping tags on a reel. A JSON array of objects with `account_id` (encrypted Instagram account), `product_id` (from `/api/instagram_products`) and optional `product_name` and `image_url` for display. Needs `in_post_type` `reel`.

in_is_ai_generated.description: Label the Instagram post as AI-generated. Instagram shows its AI label on the post.

pi_title.description: Pin title. The destination link of the pin is `url` or the first link in the text.
pi_title.example: Summer Sale - Best Deals of the Season

pi_ai_modified.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: the Pin's content was generated or modified with AI.

pi_synthetic_performer.description: Pinterest AI disclosure: a person shown or heard in the Pin is AI-generated.

gbp_cta.description: Call-to-action button on the Google Business post. Case-insensitive. An unknown value or `None` saves no button. On a link post with no CTA given, `Learn more` pointing at the link is set automatically.

gbp_cta_url.description: Link the button opens. Not used for `Call now`. With `gbp_cta=Offer` and no `gbp_redeem_offer_link`, this value doubles as the redeem link.

gbp_offer_title.description: Offer title; offer fields are used when `gbp_cta` is `Offer`.

gbp_offer_start_date.description: Offer start, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in the workspace owner's timezone. Stored as sent without a check; the publisher reads the date and the time from it, so a date alone means midnight and a value that is not a date makes the offer fail on Google.

gbp_offer_end_date.description: Offer end, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in the workspace owner's timezone, after the start. Stored as sent without a check, like the start.

gbp_offer_coupon_code.description: Coupon code shown on the offer.

gbp_offer_terms.description: Terms and conditions of the offer.

yt_title.description: Video title. YouTube needs a `video_url`; `message` or `yt_message` is the description.

yt_category.description: Category name, matched exactly against the list. An unknown or missing name falls back to the default category of the workspace owner's YouTube settings (Entertainment when none is set).

yt_privacy_status.description: Video privacy. Lower-cased and stored as given, so use one of the listed values; an unknown value reaches YouTube and fails there. When omitted it is saved as `public`, and the other YouTube options and the AI label are kept.

yt_thumb.description: Custom thumbnail URL for the YouTube video. Public image URL; copied to RecurPost storage unless `host_images_on_recurpost` is off.

yt_video_made_for_kids.description: Whether the video is made for kids. Only `yes` switches it on.

yt_contains_synthetic_media.description: Tell viewers the video contains realistic content that was altered or generated with AI. YouTube shows a label on the video.

tk_privacy_status.description: Who can watch the TikTok video. Case-insensitive, spaces or underscores. Any other value, or none, is saved as `Public to Everyone`; the other TikTok options and the AI label are kept either way. `/api/tiktok_options` lists what the account allows.

tk_allow_comments.description: Allow comments on the TikTok video. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_duet.description: Allow duets. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_allow_stitches.description: Allow stitches. Only `no` switches it off.

tk_promote_own_brand.description: Set to `1` to mark the video as promoting your own brand (TikTok's content disclosure).

tk_promote_other_brand.description: Set to `1` to mark the video as branded content for a third party.

tk_is_aigc.description: Add TikTok's AI-generated content label to the video.

post.summary: Move a card to a stage, or back to Ideas.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace. The app checks your role may move this card out of its column and into the target stage (stage roles, Approve for the client for a card in Client Review), as on the dashboard.
Puts the card in the stage named by `to`, or back in Ideas with `to` `ideas`. Client Review is not reached by a move: hand a card to the client by advancing it.
`assignee_user_id` names who picks the card up where it lands. The app enforces the dashboard rules: your role's permissions and the stage roles.

Notifications: Moves, reassignments and change requests trigger the same emails and push notifications the dashboard sends to the people involved, according to the owner's notification settings.

Client hand-over: A move never hands a card to the client: `/api/workflow_card_advance` from the stage before Client Review does that (and runs the hand-over gates). Urgent approval mails are `/api/workflow_urgent`.

to.description: An encrypted stage id from `columns[].stage_id` of the board, or the word `ideas`. A scheduled post cannot move back, and the client stage is refused.

assignee_user_id.description: Encrypted user id from `members[]` of `/api/workflow_board` or `/api/workflow_card`; `0` or an empty string clears the assignee. It must be the owner or an active member of a board workspace (404 otherwise). The app refuses a person who may not hold work in the target stage.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`. Picks the board owner; the card may sit on any workspace of that board you belong to.

message.description: The app's confirmation: `Card moved to <stage>.`, or `Pulled back from client review to <stage>.`

card.description: The card after the action, in the card shape of `/api/workflow_board`; null when the app returned no card.

post.summary: Move a card to the next column, or straight to Scheduled.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace. The app checks your role may advance this card (stage roles, Approve / reject in a review stage, Publish or schedule into Scheduled, Send posts to clients into Client Review), as on the dashboard; `card.actions.advance_blocked_by` of `/api/workflow_card` says why not.
Moves the card to the next column; with `to_scheduled` true it jumps straight to Scheduled and its draft slots become queue posts.
`assignee_user_id` names who picks the card up where it lands. The app enforces the dashboard rules: your role's permissions, stage gates (accounts and caption or media present, schedule times present, client approval before scheduling, no slot in the past) and the card still being where it was.

Scheduling is a side effect: `advance` with `to_scheduled` true (or an advance whose next column is Scheduled) turns the card's draft slots into real queue posts and sets `post_id`. The app refuses when a slot is already in the past.

Client hand-over: Advancing a card from the stage before Client Review hands it to the client (the hand-over gates apply) when the card is shared with the client. Urgent approval mails are `/api/workflow_urgent`; the client's answer is recorded with `/api/workflow_client_approve` or `/api/workflow_client_reject`.

post.summary: Add a stage to the workflow or change one.
post.description:
Permission: workspace owner only. The workflow is the account's and applies to every workspace of it.
Adds a stage when `stage_id` is absent and changes that stage when it is given; on a change the fields left out keep their value. A stage cannot be moved after it was added: `position` is used only when adding.
A `client` stage is the Client Review stage: only one is allowed, it must be the last stage before Scheduled, it takes no roles, and it is the only stage where the `reschedule` timeout policy and `reject_to_stage_id` apply. Every call answers with the full stage list afterwards.

Changing the type clears the roles: Turning a stage into a `client` stage drops its roles. Turning a client stage into a work or review stage keeps the `reschedule` policy only if you also send another `timeout_policy`; otherwise the call is refused.

Position: Positions are counted from the stage list after a save, so read them back from `stages[]` rather than assuming the one you sent. To reorder stages, use the Workflow Builder in RecurPost.

stage_id.description: Encrypted stage id from `stages[].id` of `/api/workflow_settings_get`: the stage to change. Omit it to add one.

name.description: Required when adding: stage name, 1 to 60 characters. On a change, a sent value replaces the name (blank is refused).

type.description: Required when adding: `work`, `review` or `client`, case-insensitive. On a change it defaults to the current type.

color.description: `blue`, `orange`, `teal`, `green`, `purple`, `red`, `yellow` or `pink`, case-insensitive. Defaults to `blue` when adding and to the current color on a change.

position.description: Only when adding: place in the board order, 1 first (default 1). A work or review stage asked for after the Client Review stage is put in its slot, so Client Review stays last. Ignored on a change: an existing stage keeps its place.

timeout_hours.description: Hours before the timeout policy runs: 0 for none, or one of 4, 8, 24, 48, 72, 168. Defaults to 0 when adding and to the current value on a change.

timeout_policy.description: What happens when the timeout passes: `hold`, `auto_approve`, `escalate`, or `reschedule` on the client stage only. Read only when `timeout_hours` is not 0; defaults to the current policy, else `hold`.

reschedule_by_days.description: With the `reschedule` policy: how many days the post is pushed by, 1 to 30. Defaults to the current value, else 1.

reject_to_stage_id.description: On the client stage: encrypted id (from `stages[].id`) of the stage a post the client rejects goes back to. It must be an earlier work or review stage of the workflow; any other stage is dropped silently and reads back as an empty string in `stages[]`. Ignored on a work or review stage.

roles.description: The roles that work the stage, as encrypted role ids or role names (case-insensitive), from `/api/roles`; a JSON array, a form array or a comma-separated string. Replaces the current roles; send an empty list to clear them. Left out on a change, the current roles stay. Ignored on a `client` stage, which has none.

post.summary: One page of an account's inbox items, filtered by status, type, bookmark, labels and assignee, or a delta since a moment.
post.description:
Permission: Inbox (`inbox`) in the workspace.
Returns the items of one account. An item is one inbox entry: a `comment` (a comment or mention on one of the account's posts, with the replies under it), a `message` (a direct message conversation with one person) or a `review` (one review). Items have a status: `to_review` (new, nobody has handled it), `assigned` (handed to a team member) or `reviewed` (done).
Without `updated_since` the list is one status at a time (`to_review` by default), sorted by `last_activity_at`, newest first unless `order` is `oldest`. With `updated_since` the filters and `order` are ignored and every item whose `last_activity_at` is after that moment is returned, whatever its status, newest first; poll it to read the delta instead of re-reading page 1.
The item shape documented here is the one returned by `/api/inbox_item` too; the other endpoints refer back to it.

Message items are lighter: A `message` item has no `post` and no `liked` field; it is a conversation, not a reaction to a post. Read its messages with `/api/inbox_conversation`.

Labels and assignees: `label_ids` may name labels of any inbox account of the workspace; labels of another account simply match nothing. `assigned_to` takes the workspace owner or one of their active team members.

First read of a Google Business location: A Google Business location that has never been synced is pulled from Google once before its first listing, so the first call can take a few seconds.

Polling with updated_since: Use `last_activity_at` of the newest item you already hold as the next `updated_since` (it is in the workspace owner's timezone, so send it without an offset); it is compared with a strict greater-than, so the item itself is not returned again. Items in any status come back, including ones you already reviewed, when they get new activity.

account_id.description: Encrypted account id from `/api/inbox_accounts`. Must be a Facebook page, LinkedIn company page, Google Business location or Instagram business account of the workspace.

status.description: Which status to list. Ignored when `updated_since` is given.

type.description: Only items of this kind. Omit for every kind. Ignored when `updated_since` is given.

bookmarked.description: `true` to return bookmarked items only. Accepts true/false, 1/0, yes/no, on/off. Ignored when `updated_since` is given.

label_ids.description: Encrypted label ids from `/api/inbox_label_list`, as an array, a JSON array string or a comma-separated string, at most 50. Returns items carrying any of them. Ignored when `updated_since` is given (the ids are still checked).

assigned_to.description: Encrypted user id from `/api/inbox_team_members`. Returns items assigned to that member. Ignored when `updated_since` is given (the id is still checked).

order.description: `oldest` puts the oldest activity first. Anything else is newest first. Ignored when `updated_since` is given.

updated_since.description: Return every item of the account that arrived or got a new comment or message after this moment, in any status, newest first. Send ISO 8601 with an offset or `Z`, e.g. `2026-10-15T09:30:00+05:30`, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (seconds optional), which is read in the workspace owner's timezone. The value is echoed back as `updated_since`.

post.summary: Replies to a comment or review item on the network.
post.description:
Permission: Reply to DMs & comments (`inbox-reply`) in the workspace.
Posts a reply from the account. By default it goes under the comment that raised the item; `parent_id` names another comment of the same item to reply under instead. For a Google Business review the reply answers the review itself: Google keeps one reply per review, so when the location already replied, the existing reply is replaced. The reply is published on the network through the account's connection and then recorded in the inbox as an `out` comment.
What each network accepts:
- Facebook page: `text`, `attachment_url` (an image, stored by RecurPost and attached to the comment), or both.
- LinkedIn company page: `text`, `attachment_url` (an image), or both.
- Instagram business: `text` is required; `attachment_url` is ignored.
- Google Business: `text` is required; `attachment_url` and `parent_id` are ignored.

This reaches the network: The reply is published on Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram or Google under the account's name immediately. There is no draft step.

Read the reply back: After a 200, `/api/inbox_comments` lists the new reply with `direction` `out`. The success body carries no comment id.

text.example: Yes, we open 9am to 4pm on Sundays.

attachment_url.description: Public http or https URL of an image to attach (Facebook and LinkedIn only). Hosts or redirects that resolve to private, loopback or reserved addresses are refused with 400 `invalid_url`; a URL that is not an image with 415.

parent_id.description: Encrypted comment id (from `/api/inbox_item` or `/api/inbox_comments`) to reply under. Must belong to the same item. Defaults to the comment that raised the item; not used for Google Business reviews.

post.summary: A suggested reply for an item, written by AI; nothing is sent.
post.description:
Permission: Reply to DMs & comments (`inbox-reply`) in the workspace.
Asks RecurPost's AI for a reply suggestion and returns the text. For a `message` item the last 20 stored messages of the conversation are used (empty ones skipped). For a `comment` item the post text, its link and the comment that raised the item are used; `comment_id` picks another comment of the item to answer instead. For a `review` item the review text is used. The suggestion is only returned; send it yourself with `/api/inbox_reply_comment` or `/api/inbox_reply_message`. No AI credit of the account is consumed.

Works on any account status: The suggestion is built from stored data, so it is available even when the account needs reconnection.

post.summary: Refreshes an account's inbox from its network, once per 10 minutes per account.
post.description:
Permission: Inbox (`inbox`) in the workspace.
For a Google Business location this pulls the latest reviews from Google into the inbox. For Facebook pages, LinkedIn company pages and Instagram business accounts the inbox is fed by webhooks; the sync renews the account's webhook subscription so new comments and messages keep arriving. Allowed once every 10 minutes per account; an earlier call answers 429 with a `Retry-After` header. Success is judged by the account's sync time moving.

You rarely need this: Facebook, LinkedIn and Instagram items arrive through webhooks within seconds without a sync. Call it when items stop arriving for an account, or to pull new Google reviews on demand.

post.summary: Read one automation.
post.description:
Permission: DM automations (`dm`) in the workspace.
Returns one automation of an Instagram account of the workspace.
This is the automation shape that `/api/dm_automation_list` also uses. The words the API uses for `status` are `active` (running), `paused` (switched off) and `pending` (the automation is attached to a scheduled post and waits for it to publish; RecurPost starts it then, and it cannot be set through the API). `mode` is `anyone` or `follow_to_unlock`.

post.summary: The automation counters of the last 30 days in one workspace, by day, automation or account.
post.description:
Permission: DM automations (`dm`) in the workspace.
Sums the automation counters of the workspace's accounts over the last 30 days: today and the 30 days before it, UTC dates. There is no date range to choose, as in the app; the window used comes back as `from_date` and `to_date`. Grouped by day unless `group_by` `automation` or `account` gives one row per automation or per account instead. `account_id` and `automation_id` narrow the rows. Only the workspace named by `workspace_id` (or your default workspace) is counted.
Fourteen counters are returned per row and in `totals`: `dm_sent`, `comment_reply_sent`, `non_follower_reply_sent`, `consent_dm_sent`, `consent_follower_dm_sent`, `consent_non_follower_dm_sent`, `consent_expired`, `follower_detected`, `non_follower_detected`, `consent_error`, `opening_dm_sent`, `cta_response_received`, `unfollower_dm_sent` and `cta_loop_completed`. The consent, follower, opening, cta and unfollower counters only move for `follow_to_unlock` automations.

Fixed window, like the app: The app shows DMs sent per automation over the last 30 days and offers no date picker, so this call offers none either. Dates sent along are ignored. The counters themselves are kept for 90 days.

Deleted automations keep their history: Counters of a deleted automation still appear in `day` and `account` totals and as an `automation` row with a blank name while they fall inside the 30-day window.

group_by.description: `day` gives one row per calendar day, newest first. `automation` gives one row per automation, `account` one per account, both in ascending internal id order. Case-insensitive.

account_id.description: Encrypted account id of the workspace; only rows of this account are summed.

automation_id.description: Encrypted automation id; only rows of this automation are summed. When `account_id` is also given the automation must be on that account.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

from_date.description: First day of the window: 30 days before today, UTC.

to_date.description: Last day of the window: today, UTC.

items.description: One row per group. Days without activity are left out.

id.description: Encrypted automation id, only when `group_by` is `automation`.

name.description: Automation name; blank when the automation was deleted since.

account_id.description: Encrypted id of the automation's account.

id.description: Encrypted account id, only when `group_by` is `account`.

dm_sent.description: Direct messages sent. The thirteen other counters listed in the description follow in the same way, one integer field each.

totals.description: The fourteen counters summed over every row.

post.summary: Create a comment-to-DM automation on an Instagram business account.
post.description:
Permission: Create an automation (`dm-create`) in the workspace.
Creates an automation on the account. Choose what it watches (`all_posts` or one `post_id`), what triggers it (`all_comments` or a list of `keywords`), the direct message with its optional button, and one to three public comment replies. In `follow_to_unlock` mode the four follow-loop texts are required as well. The new automation is active at once.
The account is checked first (it must be an account of the workspace), then the fields in the order listed under errors, then that the account is an Instagram business account.

Side effects: Creating an automation subscribes the account to Instagram comment webhooks and, when `post_media` is sent, downloads the file onto RecurPost storage. Keywords are trimmed, blank entries dropped, and stored comma-separated; matching is done by the app when comments arrive.

Lists in form bodies: `keywords` and `comment_replies` accept an array when the body is JSON. In a form-encoded body send a JSON array string such as `["price","link"]` or, for keywords, a comma-separated string; a plain string for `comment_replies` is one reply.

account_id.description: Encrypted Instagram business account id from `/api/dm_automation_accounts`. Accounts of other networks are refused.

dm_message.description: Text of the direct message sent to the commenter.
dm_message.example: Here is the link you asked for!

comment_replies.description: One to three public replies posted under the comment, each at most 1000 characters; RecurPost rotates through them. Send an array, a JSON array string, or a single string (one reply).

all_posts.description: true to watch every post of the account (`post_id`, `post_type` and `post_media` are then dropped). Required (as true) when `post_id` is not sent. Accepts true/false, 1/0, yes/no, on/off.

post_id.description: Instagram media id from `/api/dm_automation_posts`, at most 100 characters. Required when `all_posts` is not true; ignored when it is.

post_type.description: Media type of the watched post as returned by `/api/dm_automation_posts` (`type`), at most 50 characters. Stored for display only.

post_media.description: Thumbnail of the watched post, a publicly reachable http or https image URL. RecurPost downloads and stores it once.

all_comments.description: true to trigger on any comment; `keywords` is then dropped. Required (as true) when no keywords are given.

keywords.description: Words a comment must contain. An array, a JSON array string, or a comma-separated string; entries are trimmed and blank ones dropped. Required when `all_comments` is not true.

mode.description: `anyone` DMs every commenter. `follow_to_unlock` asks non-followers to follow first and needs `consent_dm_message`, `consent_button_title`, `opening_dm_message` and `cta_button_title`. Case-insensitive.

button_title.description: Label of the button under the DM. Send together with `button_url` or not at all.

button_url.description: Link the button opens, at most 1000 characters; a publicly reachable http or https URL (no private or local addresses). Send together with `button_title`.

name.description: Name shown in RecurPost, at most 255 characters. Blank becomes `Untitled`.

non_follower_comment_reply.description: Public reply used for non-followers in `follow_to_unlock` mode, at most 500 characters.
non_follower_comment_reply.example: Follow us and check your DMs!

consent_dm_message.description: First DM to a non-follower asking them to follow. Required in `follow_to_unlock` mode.
consent_dm_message.example: Follow us first and tap the button below.

consent_button_title.description: Button label under the consent DM, at most 255 characters. Required in `follow_to_unlock` mode.

opening_dm_message.description: DM sent when the follow check starts. Required in `follow_to_unlock` mode.
opening_dm_message.example: Welcome! Tap below once you follow.

cta_button_title.description: Button the user presses after following, at most 20 characters. Required in `follow_to_unlock` mode.

unfollower_dm_message.description: DM sent when the user still does not follow after pressing the button.
unfollower_dm_message.example: Looks like you are not following yet. Follow and tap again.

Send only the fields to change: every field of `/api/dm_automation_create` except `account_id` is accepted, and anything left out keeps its stored value (the account cannot be changed). The merged result is validated with the same rules as on create, so for example switching `mode` to `follow_to_unlock` needs the four follow-loop texts, and `all_posts` false needs a `post_id` unless the automation is attached to a scheduled post.
