post.summary: Analytics for one social account, or the overview of every account in the workspace.
post.description:
Permission: Reports & analytics (`reports`) in the workspace. The Reports feature must be on the workspace owner's plan.
Returns the report the Reports page computes for the period. With `account_id` it is that account's network report; without it, the workspace overview across every account of the workspace. The period is a named `period` (default `last_week`) or explicit `start_date` and `end_date`, as days in the workspace owner's timezone. Every report also covers the comparison window of equal length right before the period, so counters come as current and previous values.
The `report` object is the in-app report made fit for the API: tokens, the account list, the report logo and the fields already given in `account` are dropped; RecurPost's own ids inside it (`smpa_id`, `pcm_id`, `upcm_id`, `cd_id`, `user_id`, `label_id`, `ai_pcm_id` and the like) are encrypted strings; `sm_id` is replaced by `network`; `link_tracking.per_account` is keyed by encrypted account id; stored X posts carry `tweet_id` without their table row id. Every other numeric id left in the report is the network's own (post, video, campaign ids). Its keys depend on the network; see the note below.

Report keys per network: - Workspace overview (no account_id): `summary`, `top5_posts`, `all_top5_posts` plus `fb_`, `tw_`, `li_`, `gmb_`, `insta_`, `pinterest_`, `tiktok_`, `youtube_`, `threads_`, `bluesky_top5_posts`, `engagement_by_library_graph`, `per_account_table`, `link_tracking`, `link_clicks`, `yt_info_message`. `top5_posts`, `all_top5_posts` and every per-network `<network>_top5_posts` come back empty when the workspace shows members only their own posts and you are not the owner; `engagement_by_library_graph` comes back empty when your role lacks the Content library section (`library`).
- Facebook page: `summary`, `published_post_counts`, `top_countries`, `top_cities`, `audience_location_map`, `popular_post`, plus chart payloads.
- X (Twitter): `summary`, `summary_data`, `published_post_counts`, `audience_engagement`, `quote_tweets`, `bookmark_stats`, `best_time_insight`, `popular_post`, `chart_labels` with `daily_*` series, `heatmap_series`, `last_refresh_time`, `uncovered_ranges`.
- LinkedIn company: `summary`, `audience_growth`, `engagement_table`, `impressions_table`, `pageviews_table`, `publishing_table`, `conversion`, `content_type`, `funnel_data`, `reaction_breakdown`, `follower_demo`, `visitor_demo`, `best_time_insight`, `popular_post`, `current_followers`, `chart_labels` with `daily_*` series.
- LinkedIn profile: `summary`, `content_mix_rows`, `content_type_rows`, `publishing_rows`, `posts`, `recent_posts_total`, `best_time_insight`.
- Instagram: `summary`, `reach`, `views`, `interactions`, `accounts_engaged` (each with its `prev_` twin), `daily_reach`, `reach_by_*`, `content_performance_by_media_type`, `engagement_breakdown_cur`, `audience_data_by_age`, `_by_gender`, `_by_city`, `_by_country`, `follower_demographics`, `profile_taps_by_contact_button`, `recent_posts`, `reel_rows`, `story_views`, `story_reach`, `published_post_counts`.
- Pinterest: `analytics`, `account`, `split_device`, `split_format`, `top_posts`, `best_time_pins`, `boards`, `audience`, `published_pins_list`.
- TikTok: `summary`, `popular_post`, `engagement_breakdown`, `duration_breakdown`, `caption_length`, `hashtag_performance`, `aspect_ratio`, `mention_network`, `day_of_week`, `heatmap_series`, `chart_labels` with `daily_*` series.
- YouTube: `summary`, `channel_statistics`, `subscriber_count`, `total_videos`, `total_views`, `lifetime_watch_time_hours`, `top_posts`, `audience_countries`, `audience_cities`, `funnel_rows`, `traffic_sources_table`, `content_type_table`, `subscriber_sources_table`.
- Threads: `summary`, `page_impressions`, `audience_engagement`, `published_post_counts`, `popular_post`, `engagement_breakdown`, `content_mix`, `content_performance`, `funnel_data`, `demographics_*`, `top_countries`, `top_cities`, `reach_rate_stats`, `best_time_insight`, `chart_labels` with `daily_*` series.
- Bluesky: `summary`, `profile_overview`, `follower_growth`, `engagement_per_post`, `content_type_breakdown`, `publishing_behavior`, `funnel_stages`, `follow_ratio_stats`, `recent_posts`, `popular_post`, `mentions_list`, `new_followers_list`, `activity_feed`, `chart_labels` with `daily_*` series.

Chart payloads (`*_chart`, `*_option`) are ECharts option objects as drawn in the app. Google Business accounts answer the in-app Google Business report. Facebook profiles, Facebook groups and Instagram accounts connected the old way have no report and answer an empty `report` object.

Keys emptied by role: The top posts (`top5_posts`, `all_top5_posts` and every `<network>_top5_posts`) carry other members' post text and media, so they come back empty in the workspace overview when the workspace has show own posts on and you are not the owner. `engagement_by_library_graph` names the libraries, so it comes back empty without the Content library section (`library`). The key is missing, not empty.

Live network calls: The report is fetched from the network at call time and can take 10 to 60 seconds for a long period. Cache on your side; do not poll.

No implicit X Wallet spend: Report calls never buy X analytics. An X account is reported from what is already stored; when nothing is stored the call answers 409 `conflict`. The only call that debits an X Wallet is `/api/report_x_fetch` with `confirm=true`.

account_id.description: Encrypted social account id from `/api/social_account_list`. Leave out for the overview of every account in the workspace.

period.description: Named window in the workspace owner's timezone: `today`, `yesterday`, `last_week` (the 7 days before today, today left out) or `last_month` (the last 30 days including today). Ignored when `start_date` or `end_date` is sent.

start_date.description: First day of the period, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the workspace owner's timezone. Send it together with `end_date`; at most 366 days apart.

end_date.description: Last day of the period, `YYYY-MM-DD`, not before `start_date`.

account.description: `{id, name, network}` of the reported account (encrypted id), or `null` for the workspace overview.

compare_start.description: First day of the comparison window.

compare_end.description: Last day of the comparison window.

report.description: The network's report. Counters are objects `{cur_count, prev_count, percentage, flag}` where `flag` is `up` or `down` against the comparison window; daily series are arrays aligned with `chart_labels`; `popular_post` lists the period's posts with their metrics.

popular_post.description: Posts of the period, most engaged first, each with the network's per-post metrics (likes, comments, shares, views, reach, link, image, date). Present on most networks.

Metrics are the network's: The posts and numbers come from the network's own API for the window, so the list can differ from `/api/history_list` (posts made outside RecurPost appear, posts the network has not indexed yet do not).

post.summary: The account or post report as a PDF, produced now or emailed.
post.description:
Permission: Export & share reports (`reports-export`) in the workspace. The Reports feature must be on the workspace owner's plan.
Produces the Reports page as a PDF. `type` `account` renders one account's report, or the workspace overview when `id` is left out; `type` `posts` renders the per-post report of one account. Same `period` or dates as the other report calls.
Without `email` the PDF is generated inside the request and its RecurPost-hosted URL returned. With `email` (up to 25 addresses) the app generates it in the background and mails the link; the all-accounts overview cannot be emailed.

Slow without email: Without `email` the network is read and the PDF rendered inside the request, often 30 seconds or more. Prefer `email` for long periods, or raise your client timeout.

Emailed reports: With `email` the app queues the job and answers at once; the recipients get the link when the PDF is ready. Nothing is returned to poll.

X accounts: The PDF of an X account is drawn from the X analytics already stored; it never buys any. Fetch the period with `/api/report_x_quote` and `/api/report_x_fetch` (`confirm=true`) first, otherwise the PDF has no X figures.

id.description: Encrypted social account id from `/api/social_account_list`. Required for `type` `posts` and whenever `email` is sent; leave out for the all-accounts overview. The account report is not available for Facebook profiles, Facebook groups and Instagram accounts connected the old way; the posts report not for those nor Google Business.

period.description: Named window in the workspace owner's timezone: `today`, `yesterday`, `last_week` (the 7 days before today, today left out) or `last_month` (the last 30 days including today). Ignored when `start_date` or `end_date` is sent.

message.description: `Success`, or `The report will be emailed to a@example.com, b@example.com.` when `email` was sent.

post.summary: The pins of a Pinterest board with their metrics, and the board's daily impressions, saves and clicks over the period.
post.description:
Permission: Reports & analytics (`reports`) in the workspace. The Reports feature must be on the workspace owner's plan.
Returns, for one Pinterest account, the pins of a board with Pinterest's per-pin metrics and the board's day-by-day impressions, saves and pin clicks for the period, as the in-app Pinterest report shows them. By default the board is the one the account was connected with; `board_id` picks another board of the same Pinterest profile.
The pin list is the board's own (up to 100 pins, Pinterest's page) and its metrics are Pinterest's 90-day pin metrics, so they are not limited to the period; the `daily` rows are limited to the period and add up the ten pins with the most impressions.

Pin metrics are not period metrics: Pinterest hands out 90-day (or lifetime) metrics per pin, so the `pins` numbers do not change with `period`. Only `daily` follows the period.

Live network calls: The board and its pins are read from Pinterest at call time, one metrics call per top pin; expect several seconds. Cache on your side.

board_id.description: Plain Pinterest board id (digits only; other characters are dropped). Defaults to the board the account was connected with.

post.description:
Permission: Reports & analytics (`reports`) in the workspace; `format=pdf` needs Export & share reports (`reports-export`) as well. The Reports feature and the Paid Ads add-on must be on the workspace owner's plan.
Returns the in-app Paid Ads report for one account over the period: spend, reach, impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC and CPM against the comparison window, the top campaigns and ads, and the campaign, ad set (or campaign group) and ad tables. The account must be a Facebook page, an Instagram business account or a LinkedIn company page, and the ad account it reports on is one of the ad accounts that social account can see; `ads_account_id` picks one, the app's default otherwise.
The workspace owner's plan must carry the Paid Ads add-on; the owner's add-on covers every member's call. `format=pdf` renders the same report to a PDF and returns its URL instead of the data.

Paid Ads add-on required: The add-on is read on the workspace owner, not on the caller. A member of a workspace whose owner has no add-on gets the 403 even if the member's own plan has one.

Report keys per network: - Facebook page and Instagram business: `summary`, `page_impressions_reach_data`, `cpc_data`, `spent_data`, `age_gender_spend_data`, `age_gender_reach_data`, `age_gender_impressions_data`, `top3_campaigns`, `top6_ads`, `campaigns`, `adsets`, `ads`, `funnel_rows`, `placement_rows`, `device_rows`, `datewise`.
- LinkedIn company: `summary`, `page_impressions_reach_data`, `cpc_data`, `spent_data`, the three `age_gender_*` keys (empty on LinkedIn), `top3_campaigns`, `top6_ads`, `campaigns`, `campaign_groups`, `ads`.

Chart payloads are the option objects the app draws. Amounts are in `ads_account.currency`.

Live network calls: The report is fetched from the ad platform at call time and can take 10 to 60 seconds; the PDF longer. Cache on your side; do not poll.

post.summary: Engagement of the published posts by post label over the period, or the published posts of one label.
post.description:
Permission: Reports & analytics (`reports`) in the workspace. The Reports feature must be on the workspace owner's plan.
Sums, for every post label of the workspace owner, the posts published in the period and their likes, comments, shares and clicks, with the best post of each label and an eight-point trend across the period. Only posts that were actually published (not failed, not still queued) count.
Every part of the answer (counts, sums, trend, best post and the post list) covers only the published posts on the accounts of the call's workspace that you may see: in a workspace that shows members only their own posts (`show_own_posts`), a member's numbers leave out other people's one-off posts (library posts stay counted). The Reports by label page in the app sums across all of the owner's accounts; this call does not.
With `label_id` the call lists that label's published posts instead, newest first and paged.

Counts come from the app's own metrics: Likes, comments and shares are the counters RecurPost has collected for each published post, refreshed by its background jobs, not a live read from the networks; clicks are the clicks on the post's RecurPost-tracked link. The period runs from 00:00:00 of `start` to 23:59:59 of `end` in the workspace owner's timezone; the comparison window in `period` is not used by this call.

Scoped to the workspace and to what you may see: Labels belong to the workspace owner's account, so every workspace of the owner lists the same labels, but the numbers cover only posts on the accounts of the workspace you call with. In a workspace with `show_own_posts` on, a member sees only their own one-off posts and every library post; the owner and Workspace Manager see all.

post.summary: Ask the AI assistant about an account's report, or the workspace overview, for a period.
post.description:
Permission: Reports & analytics (`reports`) in the workspace. The Reports feature must be on the workspace owner's plan.
Feeds the report that `/api/report_account` would answer for the same `account_id` and period to the AI assistant as context and returns its answer to your `question`. Without `account_id` the context is the workspace overview across every account, with the same keys emptied as in `/api/report_account` (`top5_posts` under show own posts for a member, `engagement_by_library_graph` without the Content library section). The answer comes with a `chat_id` and the `history`; send both back with a new `question` to keep asking about the same report.
A new chat spends one AI post credit of the workspace owner and is refused when none is left; continuing a chat with `chat_id` is not refused for credits. Check the balance with `/api/ai_credits`.

The report is read live: Every call fetches the report from the network before asking the AI, so a question takes as long as `/api/report_account` plus the generation (often 15 to 60 seconds). Keep the period the same across the turns of one chat; the context is rebuilt from the period of each call.

Roles in history: Turns carry `user` and `assistant`. This differs from `/api/generate_content_with_ai`, whose `chat_history` names the assistant `system`; the two histories are not interchangeable, but a `chat_id` from either endpoint continues the same chat.

No implicit X Wallet spend: Report calls never buy X analytics. An X account is reported from what is already stored; when nothing is stored the call answers 409 `conflict`. The only call that debits an X Wallet is `/api/report_x_fetch` with `confirm=true`.

post.summary: The numbers behind the metric tiles of a custom report.
post.description:
Permission: Reports & analytics (`reports`) in the workspace. The Reports feature must be on the workspace owner's plan, and Custom Reports open to the owner (Agency or Admin plan, the Custom Reports add-on, or a running free trial).
The saved custom reports of a workspace are canvases of metric and note tiles over chosen accounts, with a default date mode, as built on the Custom Reports page. Reports belong to the workspace and its owner; every member with Reports & analytics reads and edits them. `report_id` is an encrypted string. This call reads the numbers behind the report's metric tiles, per account and combined, for the report's own `date_mode` (resolved in the workspace owner's timezone, as the canvas opens it) or for `period` / `start_date` and `end_date`, with the comparison window the canvas uses. Note and custom tiles carry no numbers. Only the report's accounts that are still in this workspace are read.
It never spends X Wallet money. Before reading, each X account of the report is checked against the X analytics already stored for the window and its comparison window. An X account whose data is not fully stored is left out of the read: it still appears in `accounts`, and each of its X tiles answers `{available: false, reason: "x_data_not_fetched", note}` (metrics not offered on X answer `reason` `not_supported`). Buy the data with `/api/report_x_quote` and `/api/report_x_fetch` (`confirm=true`), then read again. Fully covered X accounts are read from the stored data at no cost.

No implicit X Wallet spend: In the app, opening a custom report with an X account buys the missing X data from the viewer's X Wallet. The API never does: the only call that spends X Wallet money is `/api/report_x_fetch` with `confirm=true`. Tiles of an X account whose window is not stored answer `x_data_not_fetched`, and `force_refresh` leaves X accounts alone.

Live network calls: Figures not in the cache are read from the networks at call time; a large report can take 10 to 60 seconds. Cache on your side and use `force_refresh` sparingly.

period.description: Named window in the workspace owner's timezone: `today`, `yesterday`, `last_week` (the 7 days before today, today left out) or `last_month` (the last 30 days including today). Leave every period field out to use the report's own `date_mode`; `start_date` and `end_date` win over `period`.

start_date.description: First day of the period, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the workspace owner's timezone. Send it together with `end_date`; at most 366 days apart.

end_date.description: Last day of the period, `YYYY-MM-DD`, not before `start_date`.

force_refresh.description: Drop the cached figures of the report's non-X accounts so they are read from the networks again. X accounts are never refetched by this call.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

start.description: First day of the window read.

compare_start.description: First day of the comparison window.

compare_end.description: Last day of the comparison window.

items.description: The report's accounts in this workspace: those read, then the X accounts left out for want of stored data.

account_id.description: Encrypted account id.

network.description: Network key: `facebook`, `twitter`, `linkedin`, `instagram`, `pinterest`, `google_business`, `tiktok`, `youtube`, `threads` or `bluesky` (the account network keys of the API, not the catalog names of `/api/custom_report_metrics`).

metrics.description: One entry per metric key of the report's tiles (legacy keys resolved to the current one).

<account_id>.description: The metric's figures for one account, keyed by encrypted account id, as the canvas reads them: `available` true with `current_total`, `previous_total` and series or breakdown fields that depend on the metric (`currency` on money metrics); or `available` false with `reason` (`not_supported`, `no_data`, `fetch_failed`, a network error, or `x_data_not_fetched` with a `note`).

combined.description: The figures combined across the accounts that were read (sums, or averages for rates), with `percentage` and `flag` against the comparison window; `{available: false}` when no account had data.

tW6hJ3mN8s==.note: x_data_not_fetched: X analytics for this period are not stored yet. Price them with /api/report_x_quote and buy them with /api/report_x_fetch and confirm=true, then read this report again.

post.summary: Every metric a custom report tile can carry, with its networks, graph types and comparisons.
post.description:
Permission: any valid access token; no workspace is involved and no plan is checked.
The metric catalog of the Custom Reports canvas, the same one the page offers: 202 metrics, each with the key tiles carry as `metricId`, its name and category, what it means, how it is calculated and its limits, the networks it has data on, the graph types it can draw with the default one, and the comparisons it takes per graph type. The answer also carries the fixed lists a tile may use: the graph types, the sizes, the comparison values and the network names.
Two entries are special. `note` is a free-text tile (`body` instead of a graph) and `custom` is a metric whose numbers you type in; neither belongs to a network.
Networks are named by account type: `facebook_page`, `twitter`, `linkedin_profile`, `linkedin_page`, `pinterest`, `google_business`, `instagram`, `tiktok`, `youtube`, `threads`, `bluesky`. Send `network` to keep only the metrics that network reports. The catalog is the same for every account.

One catalog for the page and the API: The page and this call read the same catalog (the data of the page's own catalog script), and the networks per metric come from the metric registry that fetches the numbers, so what is listed here is exactly what a tile can show.

Legacy keys: Older reports may carry per-network metric keys from before the cross-network merge (`fb-follows`, `ig-saves`). `/api/custom_reports_save` still accepts them and stores the current key; this list shows current keys only.

network.description: Keep only the metrics this network reports: one of the network names above. Case does not matter.

limitations.description: Where it is not available or not comparable; blank when there is nothing to note.

items.description: The networks that report it, by the names above; empty for `note` and `custom`.

post.summary: Create a custom report or change one.
post.description:
Permission: Reports & analytics (`reports`) in the workspace. The Reports feature must be on the workspace owner's plan, and Custom Reports open to the owner (Agency or Admin plan, the Custom Reports add-on, or a running free trial).
The saved custom reports of a workspace are canvases of metric and note tiles over chosen accounts, with a default date mode, as built on the Custom Reports page. Reports belong to the workspace and its owner; every member with Reports & analytics reads and edits them. `report_id` is an encrypted string. This call creates a report (no `report_id`) or changes one (`report_id`). On a change, every field left out keeps its value; on a create, `name` is required and `date_mode` defaults to `Last 7 Days`. Tiles are checked against `/api/custom_report_metrics` the way the canvas checks them. Answers with the report as saved.

A save replaces the tile list: `tiles` and `accounts` are whole lists: send the complete list you want, not only the additions. Leave the field out to keep the current list.

Tiles follow the catalog: Every tile is checked against `/api/custom_report_metrics`: the key, the graph type and the comparison must be ones the canvas offers for that metric, so a saved report always renders; an unknown key is refused. `/api/custom_report_templates` gives ready-made tile sets. `compare` blank is stored as the canvas's `none` and read back as blank.

Date modes: The named modes are the canvas's own and are resolved on the day a report is read, in the workspace owner's timezone. `Last Month` here is the previous calendar month (compared with the month before it), unlike `period=last_month` of the data and PDF calls, which is the last 30 days.

report_id.description: Encrypted id of the report to change, from `/api/custom_reports_list`. Leave it out to create one.

name.description: Report name, 1 to 255 characters. Required on a create; optional on a change.

accounts.description: The social accounts the report covers, as encrypted ids from `/api/social_account_list` (a JSON array, a form array or a comma-separated string; up to 50, duplicates dropped). Every one must be an account of the workspace owner attached to this workspace. Send `[]` or an empty string to clear the list.

tiles.description: The tiles of the canvas, in display order, as a JSON array or a JSON string; at most 60 tiles and 200000 bytes of JSON. Each tile is an object. A metric tile: `metricId` (a metric key from `/api/custom_report_metrics`; a legacy key is stored under its current one), `title` (up to 120 characters; the metric name when blank), `viz` (one of the metric's `graph_types`; its `default_graph` when left out), `size` (`quarter`, `third`, `half`, `threeq` or `full`; default `quarter`; a `list` tile is always `full`) and `compare` (blank or `none` for none, `previous` for the previous period or `network` for the split by account; each only where the metric's `comparisons` list that graph type). A note tile: `metricId` `note`, `title`, `size` and `body` (up to 5000 characters). A custom metric tile: `metricId` `custom`, `title`, `viz`, `size` and the canvas's `cu` object with your figures, kept as sent. Other keys are dropped.

example.body: Numbers compare with the previous period.

date_mode.description: The period the report opens with: `Today`, `Yesterday`, `Last 7 Days`, `Last 30 Days`, `This Month`, `Last Month` (the previous calendar month) or a fixed range `YYYY-MM-DD|YYYY-MM-DD` (first day, a pipe, last day; at most 366 days apart). Case matters. `Last Week` is accepted and stored as `Last 7 Days`.

template_key.description: The template the canvas was started from (a `key` of `/api/custom_report_templates`), up to 50 letters, digits, `-` and `_`; blank for none. Kept for the app's own use.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

post.summary: A custom report as a PDF for its own period or a given one, produced now or emailed.
post.description:
Permission: Export & share reports (`reports-export`) in the workspace. The Reports feature must be on the workspace owner's plan, and Custom Reports open to the owner (Agency or Admin plan, the Custom Reports add-on, or a running free trial).
Renders one custom report to a PDF. Without a period field the report's own `date_mode` is used, resolved on the day of the call in the workspace owner's timezone; `period` or `start_date` and `end_date` override it for this PDF only. Without `emails` the PDF is generated inside the request and its RecurPost-hosted URL returned; with `emails` (up to 25 addresses) the app generates it in the background and mails the link.
It never spends X Wallet money: when an X account of the report has no stored X analytics for the period (and its comparison window), the call answers 409 `conflict` with `account_ids` instead of rendering. Buy the data with `/api/report_x_quote` and `/api/report_x_fetch` (`confirm=true`) or remove the X account from the report.

No implicit X Wallet spend: In the app, rendering a custom report with an X account buys the missing X data from the viewer's X Wallet. The API refuses with 409 instead; the only call that spends X Wallet money is `/api/report_x_fetch` with `confirm=true`. Once the window is stored the PDF renders without any charge.

Slow without emails: Without `emails` every tile is computed and the PDF rendered inside the request, often 30 seconds or more. Prefer `emails` for large canvases, or raise your client timeout.

Message with emails: With `emails` the answer is `The report will be emailed to a@example.com, b@example.com.` and nothing is returned to poll; the recipients get the link when the PDF is ready.

emails.description: Addresses to mail the PDF link to: one address, a comma-separated list, a JSON array or a form array; up to 25, lower-cased and de-duplicated. When sent, no `pdf_url` is returned.

period.description: Named window in the workspace owner's timezone: `today`, `yesterday`, `last_week` (the 7 days before today, today left out) or `last_month` (the last 30 days including today). Leave every period field out to use the report's own `date_mode`; `start_date` and `end_date` win over `period`.

start_date.description: First day of the period, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the workspace owner's timezone. Send it together with `end_date`; at most 366 days apart.

end_date.description: Last day of the period, `YYYY-MM-DD`, not before `start_date`.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

message.description: `Success`, or `The report will be emailed to a@example.com, b@example.com.` when `emails` was sent.

report_id.description: Encrypted id of the report rendered.

compare_start.description: First day of the comparison window.

compare_end.description: Last day of the comparison window.

pdf_url.description: Download URL of the PDF. Only present without `emails`.

post.summary: Generate post text from a prompt, with multi-turn follow-ups to refine it.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Sends your prompt to the AI assistant and returns the generated post text. The first call starts a chat and hands back an `ai_id`, a `chat_progress` marker and the `chat_history`. To refine the result, call again with a new `prompt_text` and pass all three back exactly as you received them; the assistant then answers in the context of the whole conversation.
Starting a new chat spends one AI post credit of the workspace owner; follow-ups in the same chat spend none. Check the balance with `/api/ai_credits`.

Send the history back byte for byte: `chat_progress` encodes the length of `chat_history` as JSON. Store the array as returned and send it back unchanged, as a JSON body or a JSON string; re-ordering keys, trimming whitespace in messages or appending your new prompt to it makes the check fail with the `correct chat history` error.

Assistant turns carry role system: The assistant's answers are stored with `role: system`, not `assistant`. Keep that value when you send the history back.

Zapier-era endpoint: This endpoint also accepts `emailid` + `api_key` in the body or an `Authorization: Basic` header (see Authentication). Called with the key in the body, every error comes back with HTTP 200 and the real status in the body's `status`, as it always did; with a Bearer token or Basic header the HTTP status is the real one.

Legacy endpoint: with body credentials errors arrive as HTTP 200 with the real status in the body field `status`. With a Bearer token or a Basic header it returns real HTTP status codes.

prompt_text.description: What to write, up to 5000 characters. On a follow-up call this is the refinement instruction, for example `Make it shorter and add emojis`.
prompt_text.example: Write a social media post about our summer sale on cold brew

ai_id.description: Encrypted chat id returned by the previous call. Send it to continue that chat; leave it out to start a new one. Must be a chat of the workspace owner's account. Requires `chat_progress` and `chat_history`.

chat_progress.description: Encrypted progress marker returned by the previous call. It is a check value on `chat_history`: the history you send must be the one the marker was issued for. Required with `ai_id`.

chat_history.description: The `chat_history` array of the previous response, unchanged: objects with `role` (`user` or `system`) and `content`. A JSON body array or a JSON string. Required with `ai_id`. Do not append your new prompt yourself; send it in `prompt_text`.

example.content: Write a social media post about our summer sale on cold brew
Beat the heat with 20% off every cold brew this week. Grab yours before the sun does.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to act in. Defaults to your default workspace. Get ids from `/api/workspace_list`.

chat_progress.description: Encrypted progress marker for this state of the chat. Pass it back together with `chat_history`.

items.description: Full conversation so far: the history you sent plus your prompt and the new answer.

role.description: `user` for your prompts, `system` for the assistant's answers.

example.ai_content: Beat the heat with 20% off every cold brew this week. Grab yours before the sun does.

post.summary: Suggest text variations for a library post, from the AI or from a web page; nothing is saved.
post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace.
Returns variation suggestions for one library post. With `source=ai` (the default) the assistant writes `count` short variations, each within the X character limit, in the tone set on the owner's account, from the `text` you give and the optional `url`. With `source=page` the app reads the page at `url` and extracts candidate sentences from it.
Nothing is stored and no AI credit is spent. Pick the suggestions you want to keep and save them with `/api/content_variation_add`.

Partial results with count above 1: Each AI variation is a separate generation. When a later one fails, the ones already produced are returned with status 200 and the loop stops, so check the length of `variations` rather than assuming `count` entries. Identical suggestions are collapsed into one.

Sized for X: AI variations are written to fit the X character limit (280, or 257 when a `url` is given) so they can serve as alternate copies on any network. The library post's own text is not changed.

text.example: Fresh beans just landed. Come and taste the new Ethiopian single origin this weekend.

url.description: Public http or https address. Required with `source=page`; with `source=ai` it is given to the assistant as context and subtracted from the character budget as a link. Addresses that resolve to private or reserved IP ranges are refused.

count.description: Number of variations to generate with `source=ai`, 1 to 3. Values outside the range are clamped. Ignored with `source=page`.

post.summary: Write a post from an AI template with your answers, and refine it.
post.description:
Permission: any active member of the workspace.
Writes the post from `answers` to the template's questions in the chosen `format`, with an optional `instruction`. The answer comes with a `chat_id` and `history`; send both back with a `question` (and the same template fields) to refine it.
A new generation spends one AI post credit of the workspace owner; a refinement of an existing chat spends none.

The answer fields are read by label: The app matches your answers to the template's questions by their text, so send the `label` values from `questions` as the keys of `answers`.

Refining keeps the template: On a refinement the template fields are checked again, so send `template_id`, `format` and `answers` again with the `question`, `chat_id` and `history`. A call without `chat_id` is a new generation and a new credit.

answers.description: Your answers to the template's questions, as an object `{question label: answer}` or an array of `{question, answer}`; 1 to 30 entries, each question 1 to 500 characters (not a plain number) and each answer up to 5000 characters. A JSON body value or a JSON string.

instruction.example: Keep it under 60 words and end with a question

question.description: On a refinement, what to change in the answer (1 to 5000 characters), sent with `chat_id` and `history`. Leave it out on the first generation.

post.summary: Draft up to a week of posts from one brief, written for the chosen accounts; nothing is scheduled.
post.description:
Permission: Publish or schedule (`publish`) in the workspace.
Asks the AI assistant for a set of post drafts across up to seven days, one to five posts per day, from an optional `idea`, in the given `tone` and `persona`, written for the networks of the `account_ids` you name. Every draft comes back as a base message, a per-network copy for each network in the plan and an image prompt you can pass to `/api/generate_image_with_ai`.
Nothing is scheduled or saved: post the drafts you keep with `/api/post_content` or add them to a library. One AI post credit of the workspace owner is spent per call.

Long generation: The assistant writes every draft and its per-network copies in one go; seven days of five posts can take a minute or more. Keep your client timeout generous and do not retry while a call is running: each call spends a credit.

Days are those the assistant returns: Drafts are grouped by the date the assistant put on them, normally the dates you asked for. A day the assistant left empty is absent from `days`.

tone.description: `neutral`, `cooperative`, `friendly`, `funny` or `sad` (the app's codes 1 to 5 are accepted too). Blank uses the writer's default rather than the owner's saved tone.

post.description:
Permission: Manage content (`lib-upload`) in the workspace.
Takes an AI result of the workspace owner's account and adds it to libraries as a post: `chat_id` adds the latest text of that chat as a text post, `image_id` adds that generated image set as an image post. Exactly one of the two is sent, with `library_ids`. The post is added at the end of each library, as the in-app "Add to library" button does. The owner's library post limit applies.
Ids are encrypted: `chat_id` is the value every AI endpoint returns (named `ai_id` by `/api/generate_content_with_ai`), `library_ids` come from `/api/library_list`.

Message: The success message is `Added to N library(ies).` where N is the number of libraries sent, whether or not every library got a new post; rely on `new_ids` for what was created.

image_id: `/api/generate_image_with_ai` returns the image URL only, not an `image_id`; the id belongs to the image sets kept in the app's AI history. To post an image you generated by API, pass its URL to `/api/add_content_in_library` or `/api/post_content` instead.
